- **Casos canónicos del issue**: preset comercial ✓ · cambio de dimensión (**customDims de F144 en paridad TS↔Go**) ✓ · cambio de material (BOM+precio) ✓ · agregado qty 3 (piezas y hardware ×3) ✓ · stale (fingerprint cambia con dims; release/stale completo espera **O1/#300** — dependencia documentada en el fixture) ✓ · material ambiental nunca en BOM/costo ✓ (guard existente `ambientLeakGuard` como evidencia adicional).
- **Deuda F144 cerrada como bug real de persistencia**: el backend Go reemplaza `project_items` con DELETE+INSERT y no conocía `customDims` → guardar desde web **borraba** la medida a medida. Ahora `ItemCustomDims` en el dominio Go, migración **000078** (`project_items.custom_dims` JSONB; la 77 colisionaba con f142-materials-dock), load/replace en storage, `ResolveBomWithDims` (override gana al preset; no-paramétrico rechaza; preset stale sigue fallando) y `CalcProjectBreakdown` pasa las dims. Round-trip create→update→clear probado contra Postgres real.
- **Gate "React no duplica lógica de negocio"**: `domainBoundaryGuard.test.ts` — sin aritmética de costo/merma ni evaluación de fórmulas paramétricas en packages/ui (importar de domain permitido). Detectó deuda preexistente en purchasing (valor de inventario en UI, Fase 3c) → allowlist documentada y registrada (contexto Procurement/Inventory).

### Evidencia

`go test ./...` 8 paquetes OK (storage contra Postgres real, migración aplicada) · `pnpm test` 2.924 OK · `pnpm typecheck` OK · paridad TS↔Go al primer intento contra expected calculados a mano.

### Deuda registrada

- **Fórmulas paramétricas dentro de agregados divergen TS/Go** (TS resuelve contra el sub-espacio del agregado, Go contra dims del padre) — documentada en el fixture (geometría fija a propósito); alinear es follow-up de #312/#313.
- stale→approval→change order→nuevo ProductionRelease completo → O1/#300.
- purchasing UI math → allowlist del gate (contexto dueño: Procurement/Inventory).

El issue queda **listo para cerrarse al mergear** #331+#332+#333 (los contract quedan como gate para futuras mejoras de Proyectar, DoD cumplido).

## Corrección del registro: el PR #333 nunca llegó a main

El comentario de cierre anterior decía "listo para cerrarse al mergear #331+#332+#333". Investigación de hoy (sesión F146): **#333 se mergeó con `baseRefName: feat/f144-precision-dims`** — su rama base — 13 segundos después de que #332 ya hubiera llevado esa rama a main. GitHub lo marcó MERGED, pero main nunca recibió el trabajo. Mismo patrón, mayor escala, en el **PR #330 (F142)**: mergeado a `feat/f141-proyectar-library` 2h después de que #329 ya la hubiera mergeado a main — todo el código F142 (migración 000077, backend de categorías, BoardMaterialPalette, scopes del dock) faltaba en main; sólo existía su entrada del ledger (restaurada a mano). Por eso `progress/current.md` de la sesión de #311 decía "#313 pospuesto": su árbol nunca vio este trabajo.

## Recuperación (hecha y verificada)

- **PR #335** — `recover/f142-materials-dock` → main: cherry-pick de los 4 commits F142, conflictos resueltos contra la evolución F143–F145-env de main.
- **PR #336** — `feat/f146-contracts-p3d7` → main: cherry-pick de `b1e5c68` **renumerado F145→F146** (colisión con #311 environment_multispace). Mergear #335 primero.

Verificación completa verde: `go test -count=1 ./...` 8 paquetes (storage contra Postgres real, migraciones 000077/000078), `pnpm test` 2.982, `pnpm typecheck` OK; contract TS 6/6 + Go 4 escenarios + 3 unitarios; diff vacío contra las ramas huérfanas salvo la renumeración. Review APPROVED con sección de recuperación (`progress/review_F146.md`).

**DoD del issue:** cumplido con los PRs de recuperación arriba (fixtures de los 5 casos canónicos, deterministas, anti-leak ambiental, sin fórmulas paralelas UI/domain — gate `domainBoundaryGuard`, contract como gate de futuras mejoras).

**Lección de proceso para PRs apiladas:** al cerrar un PR cuya base ya se mergeó a main, re-apuntar `base` a main ANTES de mergear. #330 y #333 se cerraron "verdes" sin tocar main.

## SDD F148 — Kit de benchmark de usabilidad 5★ (#314 P3D-8 · meta #308)

Base: `main` (post-F147, PR #337). Rama: `feat/f148-usability-benchmark`.

### Encuadre

#314 es **validación con usuarios reales**: esa evidencia no la produce un agente. Este slice entrega el **kit de medición** que vuelve esas sesiones estructuradas, comparables y recalibrables, y valida **por proxy** que el script canónico es completable en el build actual. #314 NO se cierra con esta feature: queda abierto hasta que existan sesiones reales registradas según el protocolo.

### Diagnóstico (exploración del estado actual)

- Los 11 pasos del script tienen soporte implementado (F141 biblioteca+búsqueda "bajo 600", F142 materiales por scope, F143 duplicate/align, F144 dimensiones, F145 multi-ambiente, #260 presentación, BOM/precio en chrome+inspector), pero **ningún flujo automatizado los recorre completos**: si una feature futura rompe un paso del script, nada falla hoy.
- No existe captura de métricas de usabilidad (tiempos por tarea, clicks, retrocesos, ayudas, errores). Único precedente instrumentado: `perfTelemetry` (F147) — patrón de módulo singleton + `window.__proyectarPerf*` + flag localStorage a reutilizar.
- El seed no tiene "Roble" (tableros: ARAUCO BLANCO / MADERADO FRENTE / MDF 3MM; ambientales: Porcelanato Claro (piso) / Muro Blanco Marfil (pared)). El protocolo operacionaliza "aplicar Roble a frentes" como "aplicar a los frentes un material distinto del actual" — la intención de la tarea es el scope, no el material literal.

### Alcance

1. **Tareas canónicas versionadas** (`USABILITY_TASKS` v1): los 11 pasos del issue con targets iniciales (primer mueble <60 s; material común <15 s; agregado común <30 s; duplicar/alinear 3 unidades <30 s; 0 internals del BOM) como constantes compartidas por panel, eventos y análisis.
2. **Telemetría de sesión** (`packages/ui/src/preview3d/usabilityBenchmark.ts`): sesión con timeline de eventos append-only (auto + facilitador), contexto de tarea vigente, persistencia en localStorage que **sobrevive recargas** (sesión real ≈20–30 min), export JSON versionado, y API `window.__proyectarUsability` para smoke/facilitador (patrón perfTelemetry).
3. **Costuras instrumentadas en el studio**: búsqueda de biblioteca, insert (click/drag), move-commit, duplicate/align/distribute (vía `runCommand` intent), edición de dimensión, cambio de opción (agregados), material tableros por scope, material ambiental (piso/muro/…), cambio de ambiente, undo/redo, presentar (abrir/cerrar), ver piezas (BOM), y contador de clicks del workspace. Todas no-op sin sesión activa (regla North Star: 0 costo en uso normal).
4. **Panel de facilitador** gateado por flag `muebles_usability_benchmark=1` (patrón seed perf): iniciar/cerrar sesión, marcar tarea (inicio/completada/abandonada), contadores +ayuda/+error, export/copy JSON. Tokens design.md, BEM, a11y, colapsable.
5. **Smoke del script canónico** (`tests/smoke/proyectar-usability.spec.ts`, `pnpm smoke:usability`): recorre las 11 tareas contra el seed demo como facilitador automático, afirma efectos reales + eventos esperados por tarea, exporta `test-results/proyectar-usability-proxy.json` con `source:"proxy"` + screenshot. Queda como **regresión permanente**: el script debe seguir siendo completable.
6. **Summarizer puro testeado**: tiempos por tarea (lista/mediana), ayudas/errores/retrocesos (undo)/clicks por tarea, cumplimiento de targets — función pura usada por tests y disponible para el análisis futuro de sesiones reales.
7. **Protocolo canónico** (`docs/proyectar-3d-usability-benchmark.md`): métricas operacionalizadas (cómo se captura cada una: auto/facilitador/post-sesión), targets + regla de recalibración con evidencia, guía del facilitador (consentimiento, **sin coaching**, frases neutras), hoja de observación + encuesta post-sesión (confianza/facilidad percibida, dónde buscó controles), manejo de datos (participantes anónimos), baseline **proxy** documentado como referencia no-usuario, y cómo los hallazgos reordenan #309–#313/#277–#297.

### Fuera de alcance (explícito)

- Ejecutar sesiones con usuarios reales (el entregable del issue, no de la feature; #314 queda abierto).
- Encuesta digital dentro de la app (papel/plantilla del protocolo).
- CLI de agregación multi-sesión (follow-up cuando existan ≥3 sesiones reales; el summarizer ya existe como función pura).
- Cambios de UX del editor: si el proxy run expone fricciones, se registran como hallazgos/issues, no se corrigen acá.

### Decisiones

- **D1 — Módulo en `packages/ui` junto a perfTelemetry**: mismo patrón singleton + `declare global` + idempotencia; sin dependencias nuevas.
- **D2 — Costo cero sin sesión**: todos los `track()` son early-return si no hay sesión; el panel no se monta sin flag; el listener de clicks se adhiere sólo con sesión activa. `smoke:perf` debe seguir verde sin cambios.
- **D3 — Data truth**: todo dato generado por automatización se etiqueta `source:"proxy"`; los tiempos del smoke NO son evidencia de usuario y el protocolo lo dice explícitamente.
- **D4 — Persistencia localStorage por mutación**: cada marca/evento persiste; `beginSession` pisa; export no borra (el facilitador cierra sesión al final).
- **D5 — El smoke usa las mismas vías que un usuario** (UI real, no API shortcuts, salvo las marcas del facilitador que son del facilitador).

### Plan de verificación

`pnpm test` + `pnpm typecheck` (tests unitarios del módulo: ciclo de sesión, reglas de tareas, persistencia round-trip, summarizer) · `pnpm smoke:usability` nuevo · `pnpm smoke` completo (perf gates intactos, 6/6) · `go test` no aplica (sin backend) · reviewer antes de cerrar.

## F148 — Kit de benchmark entregado (PR #339)

El kit de medición de este issue está implementado y verificado. **El issue permanece abierto**: la validación real son las sesiones con usuarios según el protocolo.

### Qué hay listo para las sesiones

- **Protocolo canónico**: `docs/proyectar-3d-usability-benchmark.md` (script, métricas operacionalizadas, targets + regla de recalibración, facilitador sin coaching, encuesta post-sesión, datos anónimos).
- **Panel del facilitador**: activar con `localStorage.setItem('muebles_usability_benchmark','1')` y recargar → panel abajo a la izquierda. Marca tareas, ayuda/error, exporta JSON (`source:"real"`).
- **Captura automática**: tiempos por tarea, clicks, retrocesos (undo/redo), búsquedas, inserciones, comandos, materiales, ambientes, presentación, BOM — todo atribuido a la tarea vigente.
- **Análisis**: `summarizeUsabilitySessions` (mediana por tarea, ayudas/errores/retrocesos/clicks, cumplimiento de targets). Guardar sesiones en `progress/benchmark/sessions/`.
- **Regresión permanente**: `pnpm smoke:usability` corre el script completo con UI real — si un paso del script deja de ser completable, CI/smoke local falla.

### Baseline proxy (referencia técnica, NO evidencia de usuario)

11/11 tareas completables por automatización en ~50 s (74 eventos, 34 clicks); tabla por tarea en el protocolo §8. Los tiempos reales de participantes son los que calibrarán los targets.

### Hallazgos registrados durante la construcción

- #338 — render loop preexistente (guest + selección + reload) en Cotizaciones; bloquea recargar a mitad de sesión, persistencia cubierta en unit.
- Piso sólo acepta material por drag (sin select): fricción candidata a aparecer en sesiones reales.

### Siguiente paso del issue

3–5 sesiones reales → JSONs + encuestas → análisis con el summarizer → recalibrar targets y reordenar #309–#313 / #277–#297 con evidencia.

## Reconciliación 2026-08-27 — VALIDACIÓN abierta (correcto)

- **Kit de medición: DONE** (F148, PRs #339/#340/#358): protocolo canónico `docs/proyectar-3d-usability-benchmark.md`, panel de facilitador (`muebles_usability_benchmark=1`), telemetría de sesión con persistencia, `summarizeUsabilitySessions`, regresión permanente `pnpm smoke:usability`.
- **Baseline proxy**: 11/11 tareas completables por automatización en ~50 s — referencia técnica etiquetada `source:"proxy"`, no evidencia de usuario.
- **Sesiones reales: 0** — `progress/benchmark/sessions/` sólo contiene el README.

Con los cierres de #309/#310 de hoy, este issue es el único blocker restante de la META #308. Queda abierta hasta existir 3–5 sesiones reales (JSONs + encuestas) y recalibración de targets con esa evidencia.

## Hallazgo (F148 / #314)

Al recargar la app en modo guest con un proyecto seleccionado, la lista de cotizaciones entra en un **render loop**: las cards de proyecto se desmontan/remontan a ~55 veces por segundo (medido con MutationObserver: 394 montajes en 8s). El click en una card nunca aterriza (Playwright: "element was detached from the DOM, retrying" ×290).

## Repro (medido con diagnóstico Playwright, dev server)

1. guest (`sessionStorage muebles_session=guest`) → `/quotes`;
2. click en card "Demo plantilla";
3. `page.reload()`;
4. la lista de `/quotes` re-renderiza en loop indefinidamente.

## Aislamiento

- Sin proyecto seleccionado + reload: **0 churn** (sin loop).
- Con proyecto seleccionado + reload: loop, **también con el flag del benchmark apagado** (225 unmounts/4s vs 215 con flag) → no es causa de F148; es preexistente y F148 simplemente es el primer smoke que recarga con selección activa.

## Impacto

- `tests/smoke/proyectar-usability.spec.ts` no puede incluir un paso de recarga a mitad de sesión (el click post-reload no aterriza).
- Usuario real guest que recarga con un proyecto abierto: UI inutilizable hasta deseleccionar (si el loop también ocurre con interacción real; verificar).

## Sospechas (a verificar)

- Loop effect→setState en la rehidratación del workspace guest cuando hay selección persistida (useProjectsScreenState / persistencia localStorage del shell).
- No hay errores de consola durante el loop.

## Meta

Bloquea la validación de recarga in-browser del kit de benchmark (#314); la persistencia de sesión queda cubierta a nivel unitario mientras esto exista.

comments.body:
Verificado y cerrado por F153 (PR #358).

**El loop ya estaba arreglado en main por el PR #342** (contrato de selección de `useProjectsScreenState`: URL→estado sin re-notificar, sólo intención local publica), mergeado ~9h después de abrir este issue — quedó abierto sin verificación.

**Repro exacto sobre main actual** (dev server, guest por UI, seed demo):
- reload en `/quotes/proj-demo-plantilla` → el detalle queda estable, URL sin rebote (8 muestras cada 400ms), sin parpadeo;
- lista `/quotes` tras reload → dos capturas separadas 600ms píxel-idénticas (cero churn) y el click en una card aterriza en el detalle (`/quotes/proj-cocina-lopez-demo`) — el canary original del issue.

**Meta desbloqueada:** la recarga in-browser a mitad de sesión del kit de benchmark (#314) que este issue bloqueaba ahora vive en el smoke `proyectar-usability.spec.ts` como regresión permanente: reload → sesión proxy persistida en localStorage → deep-link al detalle → reapertura del studio con la corrida colocada → clicks que aterrizan.

`pnpm smoke:usability` verde (37s); `pnpm test` 3.041 verdes; typecheck 0. Evidencia completa en `progress/current.md` y `progress/review_F153.md` (APPROVED).

## Objetivo

Definir y aprobar el límite arquitectónico y el contrato conceptual que permite usar SketchUp como superficie de autoría sin trasladarle la lógica industrial de Muebles.

**Invariante:** **SketchUp owns authoring/interaction; Muebles owns manufacturing truth.**

> **Estado:** COMPLETED el 2026-08-24 por [PR #357](https://github.com/tiagofur/muebleria/pull/357). La revisión documental posterior conserva el alcance y aclara identity, round-trip, provenance y gates sin reabrir esta issue.

## Dependencias

- META #290
- Autoridades: #300, #301 y #313
- `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/project-lifecycle.md`, `docs/production-flow-v2.md`

## Alcance

- estrategia canónica del programa;
- ADR de ownership;
- contrato conceptual versionado;
- identity, units, coordinate frames, revision, fingerprint e idempotency;
- authoring intent para relaciones paramétricas entre piezas/joints y provenance de operaciones derivadas;
- error model, capability negotiation y manufacturing preflight;
- matriz de ownership SketchUp/Muebles/machine adapter.

## Criterios de aceptación

- [x] `docs/sketchup-muebles-strategy.md` enlaza roadmap, arquitectura, lifecycle, producción y verificación.
- [x] ADR Accepted declara el invariante y alternativas rechazadas.
- [x] `docs/sketchup-manufacturing-contract.md` define envelope y schemas conceptuales con nombres técnicos en inglés.
- [x] El contrato separa authoring metadata de resolved manufacturing data.
- [x] El contrato deja explícito que joints/relationships expresan intención constructiva y que drilling/machining derivado se resuelve en Muebles, no en SketchUp.
- [x] Toda operación derivada conserva provenance no vacía hacia su `PartRelationship`, joint o `HardwarePlacement` manual de origen.
- [x] Todo output fabricable exige `designRevisionId`, `bomFingerprint` e idempotency.
- [x] Compatibilidad de máquina exige import/readback y operator sign-off.
- [x] Links relativos y referencias GitHub quedan verificados.

## Definition of Done

- documentación revisable en un PR `docs/*`;
- decisiones y consecuencias explícitas;
- dependencias enlazadas desde #290;
- el contrato es suficiente para implementar #356 sin inventar un segundo modelo industrial en Ruby;
- no hay afirmaciones de compatibilidad sin evidencia;
- ningún cálculo industrial se asigna a Ruby/SketchUp.

- PR: [#357](https://github.com/tiagofur/muebleria/pull/357)
- Documentos publicados: `docs/sketchup-muebles-strategy.md`, `docs/adr/0001-sketchup-authoring-muebles-manufacturing-truth.md` y `docs/sketchup-manufacturing-contract.md`
- La issue permanece cerrada; las implementaciones ejecutables continúan en #345–#356.

## Fuera de alcance

- implementar la extensión;
- endpoints o schemas ejecutables;
- generar PTX, DXF, G-code o machine code;
- modificar lógica de producción existente.

## Referencias

- #111, #227, #282, #286, #293, #300, #301, #313, #356
- `docs/roadmap-comercial-v2.md`
- `docs/proyectar-3d-north-star.md`
- `docs/verification.md`

- ✅ **El resultado identifica `projectId`, `designRevisionId` y `bomFingerprint`** (FNV-1a determinístico sobre inputs canonizados).
- ✅ **Errores incluyen `code`, `message`, `entityId`, `path`, `severity` y `remediation`** — completado en validación, machining y preflight; meta-test recorre una batería de escenarios bloqueados exigiendo los 6 campos.
- ✅ **Un cambio post-release marca outputs como stale** — `policy.release` (contexto server-side) con fingerprint distinto → `REVISION_STALE` error bloqueante con ambos fingerprints en `details`.
- ✅ **Máquina/perfil incompatible bloquea antes de exportar** — negotiation §10: `requiredCapabilities` derivadas de verdad resuelta (`granete.drilling` desde agujeros, `granete.panel-geometry` desde geometría de catálogo); bloquea ante capability ausente, versión distinta, constraint omitido o límite numérico insuficiente. **Capabilities nunca se infieren.**
- ✅ **Override explícito, auditable y server-authoritative** — `PreflightOverride` degrada sólo `MACHINE_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`/`REVISION_STALE` a warning dejando who/when/why en `issue.details.override`; un override forjado en runtime con otro code se ignora (test) — la ambigüedad crítica siempre bloquea. Los policy inputs nunca viajan en el `AuthoringEnvelopeV1`: sin bypass desde SketchUp.
- ✅ **Tests cubren happy path y fallos críticos** — 19/19 en preflight (6 del milestone + 13 del DoD).

### Definition of Done

- ✅ preflight determinístico y trazable (test de determinismo);
- ✅ mismos fixtures producen mismo fingerprint;
- ✅ UI sólo presenta resultados del dominio (feedback read-only ligado a `ManufacturingIdentity`, contract §7);
- ✅ no hay bypass desde SketchUp (policy context server-side + test);
- ✅ docs y contract fixtures actualizados: §11 del contract doc documenta los policy inputs server-side; ledger registra F163 (retroactivo — la evidencia existía pero faltaba la entrada) y F168.

### Verificación

Preflight 19/19 · domain 87 files/1106 tests · web 24/306 · typecheck 7/7 workspaces · `go test ./...` ok.

Con este cierre quedan desbloqueadas **#348** (PTX field validation, requiere field evidence de #306) y **#351** (machine profiles/postprocessors).
Cerrada con DoD completo — ver comentario de cierre con evidencia y progress/implementation_F168.md. Review APPROVED en progress/review_F168.md.

## Objetivo

Corregir las ambigüedades detectadas entre la estrategia, el manufacturing contract y el backlog de SketchUp + Muebles antes de congelar semantic metadata o avanzar el vertical slice.

**Invariante:** **SketchUp owns authoring/interaction; Muebles owns manufacturing truth.**

## Problema

- El orden publicado ubicaba el `minimum authoritative preflight` después de un gabinete denominado manufacturable y de hardware sync, aunque #349/#350 requieren ese gate.
- El contrato definía `componentId` e `instanceId` sin aclarar cuál identifica una definición reutilizable y cuál una instancia concreta.
- Round-trip, mutations/migrations, provenance y la identidad exacta de profile/adapter/evidence quedaban abiertos a interpretaciones incompatibles.
- #344 ya estaba completada por PR #357, pero algunos textos y checklists seguían presentándola como pendiente.

## Alcance

- alinear `docs/sketchup-muebles-strategy.md`, `docs/sketchup-manufacturing-contract.md` y `docs/roadmap-comercial-v2.md`;
- distinguir hard prerequisites, milestone gates, authority/reference y field evidence;
- definir `componentDefinitionId` y `componentInstanceId`, con anchors/hosts siempre instance-scoped;
- completar el contrato conceptual de round-trip, snapshot/tombstones, migrations, provenance y artifact identity;
- preparar y aplicar las correcciones coherentes en #290, #344, #346, #347, #349, #350, #351, #354 y #356;
- conservar la historia, los acceptance criteria, la Definition of Done y el posicionamiento de Proyectar 3D.

## Criterios de aceptación

- [ ] El orden ejecutable es #356 → milestone mínimo #347 → #349/#350 → gabinete manufacturable/demo.
- [ ] El cierre completo de #347 permanece prerequisite para #348/#351.
- [ ] Definitions reutilizables e instances concretas tienen identidad inequívoca; dos shelves de la misma definition no cruzan relationships ni machining.
- [ ] Round-trip y create/update/delete son versionados, correlacionados, idempotentes y fallan de forma segura.
- [ ] Provenance no admite un objeto vacío y obliga un origen válido.

- [ ] La documentación registra tres modos de entrada y dos rutas de autoría 3D.

- documentos canónicos revisados y mergeados;
- bodies de las issues relacionadas actualizados sin perder historia;

# Project Digital Thread — Quote ↔ Project Furniture ↔ Design Revision ↔ Manufacturing

## Objetivo

Implementar el contrato canónico que conecta cotización, identidad física del mueble, autoría 3D, revisiones de diseño, reconciliación y liberación productiva sin identidades paralelas ni sincronización destructiva.

## Fuente canónica obligatoria

Antes de implementar cualquier issue hija leer completa:

- `docs/architecture/project-design-digital-thread.md`
- `docs/adr/0003-project-owned-furniture-identity-and-versioned-design.md`
- `docs/architecture/domain-model.md`
- `docs/architecture.md`

Para cambios SketchUp leer además:

- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`
- `docs/sketchup-manufacturing-contract.md`
- ADR-0001

## Invariantes no negociables

1. Project owns `FurnitureInstance` identity.
2. `QuoteLine.quantity` es grouping comercial, no identidad física.
3. `Design` es client-agnostic; no crear `SketchUpProject` aggregate.
4. `DesignRevision` publicada y `QuoteRevision` aceptada son inmutables.
5. SketchUp `persistent_id` es locator técnico, no business ID.
6. Copiar una unidad gestionada crea un nuevo `FurnitureInstance`.
7. Reconciliation detecta/clasifica; nunca muta silenciosamente.
8. Granete sigue siendo manufacturing authority.
9. `ProductionRelease` fija exact `designRevisionId` + manufacturing revision/fingerprint; nunca `latest`.
10. Geometría/decoración no gestionada no entra a BOM.

Cualquier excepción requiere cambio explícito de ADR, no workaround local.

## Dependency graph

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["#385 Stable Project FurnitureInstance"] --> B["#386 QuoteLine ↔ FurnitureInstance"]
    A --> C["#387 Design + immutable DesignRevision"]
    C --> D["#388 SketchUp Project/Design binding"]
    B --> E["#389 Project Furniture panel + place existing"]
    D --> E
    E --> F["#390 Catalog insertion creates Project FI"]
    F --> G["#391 Duplicate identity handling"]
    C --> H["#392 Publish revision + manifest/artifacts"]
    D --> H
    G --> H
    B --> I["#393 Reconciliation"]
    H --> I
    I --> J["#394 Change classification + explicit requote"]
    J --> K["#395 Approval + exact ProductionRelease"]
    B --> L["#396 Web Project Furniture/Design workspace"]
    C --> L
    I --> L
    K --> L
    D --> M["#397 Adopt existing SKP"]
    F --> M
    H --> M
    I --> M
    K --> N["#398 E2E regression suite"]
```

## Issues en orden de implementación

| Slice | Issue | Entrega | Hard prerequisite principal |
|---|---:|---|---|
| DT-1 | #385 | Persist stable Project `FurnitureInstance` identity | docs/ADR merged |
| DT-2 | #386 | QuoteLine quantity ↔ physical FurnitureInstances | #385 |
| DT-3 | #387 | `Design` + immutable `DesignRevision` snapshots | #385 |
| DT-4 | #388 | Bind SketchUp model to Project/Design | #385, #387 |
| DT-5 | #389 | Project Furniture panel + place existing units | #386, #388 |
| DT-6 | #390 | Connected Catalog insertion creates Project FI | #385, #388, #389 |
| DT-7 | #391 | Detect/resolve duplicate managed identity | #390 |
| DT-8 | #392 | Publish immutable revision + manifest + artifacts + concurrency | #387, #388, #391 |
| DT-9 | #393 | QuoteRevision ↔ DesignRevision reconciliation | #386, #392 |
| DT-10 | #394 | Commercial/manufacturing/spatial classification + explicit new quote revision | #393 |

| DT-12 | #396 | Web Project Furniture + Design 3D workspace | #386, #387, #393; #395 for final release state |
| DT-13 | #397 | Adopt existing SketchUp model safely | #388, #390, #392, #393 |
| DT-14 | #398 | End-to-end Digital Thread regression suite | core #385–#395 |

## Parallelism permitido

Después de #385 pueden avanzar en paralelo:

- #386 (Sales/commercial link)
- #387 (Design aggregate)

Después de #387, #388 puede avanzar mientras #386 termina. No iniciar #389 hasta tener ambos #386 y #388. No iniciar publish/reconciliation saltando identidad/duplicate validation.

## Global Definition of Done

El programa se considera completo sólo cuando se demuestra el escenario E2E definido en `project-design-digital-thread.md` §29, incluyendo:

- quote con dos unidades físicas distintas;
- create Design from QuoteRevision;
- Project Furniture pending → place in SketchUp;
- cambio de una unidad + publish R1;
- reconciliation explícita + nueva QuoteRevision;
- approval + authoritative preflight + release pinned a R1;
- publish R2 sin alterar el release anterior;
- copy/paste genera nueva identidad;
- unmanaged decoration no aparece en BOM;
- stale base publish falla sin overwrite.

## Reglas para agentes

- Variables/tipos/funciones/APIs técnicas en inglés; copy UI en español.
- No implementar una issue dependiente antes de su hard prerequisite salvo discovery/planificación.
- Cada PR debe indicar qué invariantes del documento canónico toca y cómo se prueban.
- Cada issue debe añadir positive tests + negative proof del anti-pattern que evita.
- No cerrar un child issue por implementación parcial si su DoD no está demostrada.
- Si el documento canónico permite libertad de implementación (p.ej. signed upload vs multipart), escoger el mecanismo más simple compatible. No tratar ownership, identidad, inmutabilidad o release exacto como implementation detail.

## Objective

Make `FurnitureInstance` a persisted, project-scoped business identity that exists independently from QuoteLine, SketchUp entities and production rows.

Tracks #384.

## Mandatory authority

Read before implementation:
- `docs/architecture/project-design-digital-thread.md` §§2–5, 26, 28, 30–31
- `docs/adr/0003-project-owned-furniture-identity-and-versioned-design.md`
- `docs/architecture/domain-model.md`
- `docs/architecture.md`
- `docs/architecture/organization-foundation-v2.md`
- `docs/adr/0006-membership-lifecycle-and-organization-relationships.md`

## Hard prerequisites

- Documentation PR containing ADR-0003 and the canonical digital-thread document merged. ✅
- #447 Organization Foundation v2 documentation/ADR merged.
- **Gate A — Organization Foundation Readiness in #462 completed.**

Gate A is required because this issue creates the first new persisted business family after the multi-org audit. `furniture_instances` must start with the generated API contract, tenant transaction/RLS, lifecycle/audit conventions and upgrade gates rather than receive them through a second corrective migration.

Discovery/domain design that does not add persistence may continue before Gate A; schema/API implementation may not.

## Coordination with Organization Foundation v2

- #446 does not change Project/FurnitureInstance ownership or create an alternate identity.
- #449 defines RLS/table classification that this migration must register.
- #448 defines generated DTO/error/version conventions.
- #461 defines durable audit/outbox conventions for identity creation/removal.
- #456 consumes #385/#386 identities for cross-org ManufacturingOrder handoff; it does not recreate them.

## Required scope

- Audit current `FurnitureInstance` types/usages before adding schema. Reuse the existing domain concept; **do not create `ProjectFurniture` or an equivalent identity**.
- Define/persist stable `furnitureInstanceId`, `projectId`, `furnitureDefinitionId?`, origin/provenance and minimal lifecycle (`active|removed|cancelled` or domain-equivalent).
- Project-scoped create/read repository/API operations needed by later issues.
- Enforce that an instance belongs to exactly one Project.
- Make ID independent from authoring client, position, dimensions and SketchUp `persistent_id`.
- Preserve room/configuration/history in their owning contexts rather than turning FurnitureInstance into a mutable mega-snapshot.
- Define audit event(s) for creation/removal through the durable mechanism of #461.
- Register the table in RLS/policy inventory and Pilot/Foundation upgrade fixtures.
- Use version/ETag/idempotency conventions from #448 where create/retry/concurrency applies.

## Explicit non-goals

- QuoteLine relation (#386).
- Design/DesignRevision (#387).
- SketchUp UI/binding.
- Reconciliation.
- Production release changes.
- Reimplementing User/Membership/Organization or relationship ownership from #446.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Project can own a FurnitureInstance before any 3D design exists.
- [ ] Two FurnitureInstances can reference the same FurnitureDefinition and same parameters while retaining distinct IDs.
- [ ] Changing a configuration snapshot does not require changing the FurnitureInstance ID.
- [ ] Cross-project linking is rejected server-side.
- [ ] No new entity duplicates the semantic responsibility of FurnitureInstance.
- [ ] Public/API DTOs expose only required identity/provenance fields.
- [ ] Storage migration is backwards-safe for existing projects.
- [ ] Table ownership/RLS policy and direct SQL cross-org tests exist from the first migration.
- [ ] API uses generated contracts and typed errors; no manual parallel DTO.
- [ ] Creation/removal audit is durable and transactionally coupled where required.
- [ ] Fresh DB + upgrade fixture + Gate A/DT tests remain green.
- [ ] Tests prove identity is not derived from position/name/definition/SketchUp IDs.

## Negative proof required

Add tests demonstrating that:

- two identical physical units do **not** collapse into one identity;
- a repository query with a missing tenant filter still cannot cross org under the app DB role;
- a random org/project ID in the payload cannot attach the instance outside the actor's authorized Project;
- retry with the same idempotency key does not create a second identity.

## Definition of Done

Gate A is green; domain + persistence + generated API/storage + RLS + durable audit tests are green; applicable `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`, Go tests and upgrade fixtures pass. PR explains how invariants I1, I2, I7 and I9 from the digital-thread contract and organization-foundation invariants are preserved.

## Objective

Connect commercial quote grouping to stable project furniture identity without treating `QuoteLine` or `quantity` as physical identity.

Tracks #384.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/project-design-digital-thread.md` §§6, 15–16, 25.1, 25.3, 26, 28, 30–31
- ADR-0003
- `docs/architecture/domain-model.md`

## Hard prerequisite

- #385

## Required scope

- Audit the current Quote/QuoteRevision/QuoteLine model before adding storage.
- Introduce an explicit relation (or equivalent normalized representation) between a QuoteRevision/QuoteLine and one or more `FurnitureInstance`s.
- Preserve the distinction: `QuoteLine.quantity` = commercial grouping; FurnitureInstances = physical units.
- Add an idempotent materialization service for units that need individual traceability.
- Define safe behavior for draft quantity increase/decrease.
- Never recycle a FurnitureInstance ID after it has design/accepted/commercial/production history.
- Preserve accepted QuoteRevision immutability; later changes create a new revision.
- Ensure quote-first creation can produce units that later appear in Project Furniture without creating new IDs.

## Required cases

```text
QuoteLine qty 1 → FI-001
QuoteLine qty 3 → FI-010, FI-011, FI-012
```

If only FI-010/FI-011 are later modeled, FI-012 must remain a distinct quoted unit eligible for `quoted_not_modeled` reconciliation.

## Explicit non-goals

- Design aggregate/revisions (#387).
- SketchUp placement.
- Reconciliation UI/engine (#392).
- ChangeOrder entity (future; use QuoteRevision for MVP).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `quantity=N` materializes N unique physical identities when individual traceability is required.
- [ ] Re-running materialization does not create duplicate units.
- [ ] Draft quantity increase adds only the required additional units.
- [ ] Draft quantity decrease does not silently reuse/remove units that already have durable history.
- [ ] Accepted QuoteRevision is not mutated in-place.
- [ ] The relation can answer which physical units a quote line represents.
- [ ] Tests cover qty 1, qty >1, increase, decrease, accepted revision and idempotency.

## Negative proof required

A test must fail if an implementation tries to use one `QuoteLine.id` as the identity for all `quantity > 1` units.

## Definition of Done

Domain/storage/API tests green. PR explains how I2, I3 and I10 are preserved.

issues.body:
## Objective

Bind one SketchUp model to one exact Granete Project/Design working context without making the `.skp` file, its path or SketchUp technical IDs the business identity.

Tracks #384 and coordinates with #465.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/project-design-digital-thread.md` §§11–13, 18, 26, 28, 30–31
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-backend-web-integration-excellence.md` once merged
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`
- `docs/sketchup-manufacturing-contract.md`
- ADR-0001 and ADR-0003
- #496 generated API contract

## Hard prerequisites

- Foundation Gate A #462
- #385 stable Project FurnitureInstance identity
- #387 Design + immutable DesignRevision

## Required scope

### Model-level binding

Store versioned Granete-owned metadata equivalent to:

```text
Dictionary: com.granete.project

projectId
designId
baseRevisionId
schemaVersion
```

Add/read/recover the binding on model open and save/reopen.

### Authoritative validation

Before considering a model connected:

- validate active organization/session/capability;
- validate Project exists and is authorized;
- validate Design belongs to that Project;
- validate base revision exists and is an allowed working base;
- validate plugin/API/schema compatibility;
- surface unbound, invalid, archived/deleted Design, stale base, unauthenticated, unauthorized and incompatible states distinctly.

No model metadata is mutated before validation succeeds.

### Identity convergence

Align current top-level `instanceRef` semantics with Project-owned `furnitureInstanceId`:

- do not preserve two permanent business IDs for the same physical furniture;
- compatibility aliases remain explicitly documented and never promoted to server identity silently;
- `Sketchup::Entity#persistent_id`, entity ID, definition GUID, name, dimensions and path are locators/evidence only;
- a changed host locator does not change Project/Furniture identity.

### Dialog/host context

Expose to the plugin state/inspector:

- organization summary allowed for display;
- Project/Design identity and human label;
- exact base revision;
- connected/unbound/stale/invalid/incompatible state;
- capabilities;
- next actions/remediation.

The dialog consumes the shared host runtime #498 when available and generated contract #496.

## Secure Web handoff coordination

#499 owns the Web-to-SketchUp pairing/deep-link protocol. #388 consumes its accepted pairing result to write the exact binding.

Rules:

- no web JWT or reusable SketchUp credential in custom URI/query;
- no raw UUID paste as the primary production workflow;
- invoking a deep link alone is not confirmation;
- failed pairing/rebind preserves the previous valid binding.

## Rebind/switch behavior

Switching an already-bound model is explicit and reviewed:

- show current vs target Project/Design/base revision;
- inventory current managed FurnitureInstance IDs;
- reject foreign/cross-project identity silently becoming valid;
- route adoption/mapping requirements to #397;
- route differences after publication to #393;
- keep old binding until target validation succeeds.

## Correct downstream ownership

- #389 owns Project Furniture panel/place existing units.
- #390 owns connected catalog insertion/create Project FI.
- #391 owns copied/duplicated business identity.
- **#392 owns revision publication/artifacts.**
- #393 owns reconciliation.
- **#397 owns adoption of an existing SKP.**
- #499 owns secure Web↔SketchUp pairing.

## Explicit non-goals

- Project Furniture panel/placement (#389).
- Revision publication/upload (#392).
- Copy identity repair (#391).
- Existing model business adoption (#397).
- Creating local Project/Design business identity.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Binding survives save/close/reopen.
- [ ] Binding never relies on filename/path.
- [ ] Design is validated as belonging to the exact Project.
- [ ] Cross-organization/foreign Design fails indistinguishably and safely.
- [ ] `persistent_id`/GUID can change without changing `furnitureInstanceId` or model binding.
- [ ] Compatibility `instanceRef` is explicitly aliased/migrated and cannot become a second permanent identity.
- [ ] Unbound, stale, archived, unauthenticated, unauthorized and incompatible states are distinct.
- [ ] Invalid/stale binding blocks publish/release paths.
- [ ] Failed validation/rebind preserves the previous valid binding and model hierarchy.
- [ ] #499 pairing result writes the same exact Project/Design/base revision shown in React.
- [ ] Ruby/backend contract tests and real-host save/reopen prove the binding.

## Negative proof required

Tests/review fail if:

- moving/renaming the `.skp` changes business context;
- filename/folder implies Project/Design;
- foreign Design is accepted because the ID format is valid;
- metadata is written before server validation;
- a local `instanceRef` is silently promoted to Project-owned identity;
- rebind overwrites current binding before target acceptance;
- publication/adoption is implemented here instead of #392/#397;
- a web bearer token appears in pairing/deep-link data.

## Definition of Done

A real SketchUp model can be securely connected, reopened and validated against one exact Project/Design/base revision, with technical host locators independent from business identity, safe rebind behavior, generated contracts and correct coordination with #389–#393, #397 and #499.

## Objective

Support design-first insertion from the reusable SketchUp Catalog while preserving Project-owned identity: a catalog selection must create a new Project FurnitureInstance before becoming a managed productive object.

Tracks #384.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/project-design-digital-thread.md` §§13, 21, 25.2, 26, 28, 30–31
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`
- ADR-0001 and ADR-0003

- #385
- #388
- #389

## Required scope

When a model is connected to a Project/Design:

```text
FurnitureDefinition selected
→ create FurnitureInstance in Project
→ server returns furnitureInstanceId
→ resolve/render SketchUp furniture
→ persist semantic metadata with that ID
```

- Reuse project-scoped FurnitureInstance creation from #385.
- Carry origin/provenance (`design` or domain-equivalent).
- Ensure failed remote identity creation cannot leave an apparently valid managed/productive object.
- If geometry creation fails after server identity creation, define explicit cleanup/retry/orphan handling; do not silently create another ID on retry.
- Keep insertion idempotent where retries/network failures can repeat a request.
- Keep current extension token/security model in mind; if current read-only extension auth blocks this write, solve the auth capability explicitly and narrowly rather than tunneling identity creation through unrelated GETs.

## Explicit non-goals

- Offline-first local productive identity/sync protocol.
- Copy/paste duplicate semantics (#391).
- Quote creation/repricing (#394).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Catalog insertion in a connected Project creates exactly one new FurnitureInstance.
- [ ] The returned ID is stored in the top-level semantic entity.
- [ ] Retry/network replay cannot create duplicate FurnitureInstances.
- [ ] Failed create does not produce a publishable managed object with fake/local identity.
- [ ] Design-first FurnitureInstance is visible to later reconciliation as modeled_not_quoted.
- [ ] Authorization is least-privilege and server-enforced.
- [ ] Ruby/backend contract tests cover success, retry and failure.

## Negative proof required

Test that a random local/SketchUp-generated ID cannot be accepted as authoritative Project identity in the connected MVP.

## Definition of Done

Connected design-first insertion works end-to-end and applicable TS/Go/Ruby gates are green. PR explains I1, I5 and I7 compliance.

## Objective

Prevent copy/paste / Move+Copy in SketchUp from leaving two managed physical units with the same `furnitureInstanceId`.

Tracks #384.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/project-design-digital-thread.md` §§14, 25.4, 26, 28, 30–31
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`
- ADR-0001 and ADR-0003

## Hard prerequisites

- #390

## Required scope

- Observe/detect duplicate top-level managed `furnitureInstanceId` values after relevant SketchUp copy/add operations and on model validation/publish precheck.
- Preserve the original instance ID on the original entity.
- Create exactly one new Project FurnitureInstance for the copied physical unit with provenance (`origin=duplicate`, `originFurnitureInstanceId=<source>` or domain-equivalent).
- Rewrite only the copied entity's business metadata to the new ID.
- Define deterministic handling when it is not initially obvious which duplicate is the original; use observer/context/persistent locator only as technical evidence, never as new business identity.
- On remote failure, surface an explicit invalid/unsynced state and block publish/release until identity ambiguity is resolved.
- Re-scan on model open/publish to catch duplicates created while observer/runtime was unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Copy FI-001 results in FI-001 + a new distinct FI-XXX.
- [ ] New instance preserves provenance to FI-001.
- [ ] Repeated observer callbacks/retries do not create multiple new Project records for one copy.
- [ ] Definition, dimensions, name and position are not used as identity.
- [ ] A model containing unresolved duplicate business IDs cannot publish a valid DesignRevision.
- [ ] Save/reopen preserves resolved identities.
- [ ] Ruby + backend tests cover copy, retry, reopened duplicate and failure.

## Negative proof required

Fixture with two top-level entities carrying FI-001 must be rejected or repaired; it must never pass publish validation as two legitimate units.

## Definition of Done

Host-safe duplicate behavior implemented and verified with applicable Ruby/RBZ/backend tests. PR explains I8 and I7 compliance.

comments.body:
## Architecture dependency update — native ComponentInstance copy semantics

Copy/duplicate handling must be implemented against the native managed hierarchy from **#415** (authority: **#413 / `docs/architecture/sketchup-native-entity-model.md`**).

In addition to allocating a new Project `furnitureInstanceId` for the copied physical unit, normalize SketchUp definition ownership so the copy cannot remain coupled to a mutable top-level definition shared with the original. V1 policy is one generated top-level SketchUp ComponentDefinition per FurnitureInstance; `make_unique`/rebind may be used as a host mechanism, but the Granete business ID is never derived from the SketchUp definition.

Unresolved copy state remains unpublishable exactly as this issue already requires.

## Objective

Implement revision publication from an authoring working copy to an immutable DesignRevision with semantic manifest, `.skp` artifact, preview/integrity metadata and optimistic concurrency.

Tracks #384.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/project-design-digital-thread.md` §§8–11, 17–18, 21, 25.6, 26, 28, 30–31
- ADR-0003
- `docs/sketchup-manufacturing-contract.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`

## Hard prerequisites

- #387
- #388
- #391

## Required scope

- Define `manifest` schema v1 and validation for project/design/baseRevision/source/items.
- Export managed FurnitureInstances only; unmanaged architecture/decoration must not enter the productive semantic manifest.
- Persist `model.skp`, `manifest.json`, and at least one preview artifact or explicit placeholder strategy if preview generation is technically deferred.
- Persist storage key, MIME/content type, size, SHA-256, authoring client/version/plugin version and uploader/timestamps where available.
- Use object/file storage for heavy artifacts; relational DB stores metadata/indexed revision items.
- Publication flow must be atomic from the business perspective: a revision is not `published` until required artifacts + manifest validation succeed.
- Validate all FurnitureInstances belong to the Project; reject duplicate business IDs.
- Implement optimistic concurrency using `baseRevisionId`.
- On successful publish, update the working model binding to the newly published revision.
- Choose multipart vs signed upload as an implementation choice; document the chosen mechanism and failure cleanup.

## Concurrency rule

```text
client base R7 + server current R7 → publish R8
client base R7 + server current R8 → explicit conflict, no overwrite
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Published revision is immutable.
- [ ] Manifest schema is versioned from v1.
- [ ] Server does not need to parse `.skp` to know managed items.
- [ ] Unmanaged geometry is absent from semantic DesignRevisionItem/BOM input.
- [ ] Artifact hashes/integrity metadata persist.
- [ ] Failed upload/finalize cannot leave a falsely published revision.
- [ ] Stale `baseRevisionId` returns structured conflict and leaves current revision unchanged.
- [ ] Reopen after publish sees the new baseRevisionId.
- [ ] Contract tests cover valid, invalid manifest, duplicate ID, cross-project ID, stale base, failed artifact and retry.

## Negative proof required

A `.skp` file containing unmanaged decoration plus managed furniture must publish only the managed semantic subgraph; arbitrary geometry must never become BOM input by scanning.

## Definition of Done

Backend/storage/Ruby integration tests green; applicable end-to-end publish smoke proven. PR explains I4, I11–I14 compliance.

# Project Digital Thread — React workspace tracker

## Objective

Coordinate the React product surfaces that expose Project-owned `FurnitureInstance`, Designs, immutable DesignRevisions, reconciliation, approval and exact ProductionRelease without delaying Web integration until the entire backend/SketchUp program is finished.

Tracks #384. This issue is a **tracker**, not a single implementation slice.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/sketchup-backend-web-integration-excellence.md` once merged
- `docs/architecture/project-design-digital-thread.md`
- `docs/adr/0003-project-owned-furniture-identity-and-versioned-design.md`
- `docs/design.md`
- `docs/architecture.md`
- #496 generated furniture/Design API contract

## Why the original scope was split

The previous issue combined three independently valuable and dependency-heavy products:

```text
Project Furniture matrix
+ Designs/revisions/artifacts
+ reconciliation/approval/release
```

Implementing them as one late Web issue would create a long backend-first program and discover Go↔React contract/UX problems only near the end. The approved plan now delivers vertical React slices alongside their backend authorities.

## Child issues

| Order | Issue | Delivery | Hard prerequisites |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| WEB-DT-1 | #500 | Project Furniture matrix and physical-unit traceability | Gate A #462, #385, #386, #496 |
| WEB-DT-2 | #501 | Designs, immutable revisions and 3D artifact history | Gate A, #387, #392, #496 |
| WEB-DT-3 | #502 | Reconciliation, explicit requote, approval and exact ProductionRelease | #386/#387/#392–#395, #496; integrates #501 |
| DT-SU handoff | #499 | Secure Web-to-SketchUp Project/Design pairing | #385/#387/#388, #460, #496 |

## Ownership boundary

React presents authoritative read models and invokes explicit commands. It does not own:

- physical furniture identity;
- revision immutability;
- reconciliation classification;
- manufacturing/preflight logic;
- approval/release decisions;
- artifact integrity;
- machine compatibility.

Those remain in Project/Design/manufacturing backend/domain owners.

## Shared UX rules

- Copy UI in Spanish; technical types/functions/contracts in English.
- Every historical or approval-sensitive view is pinned to exact revision IDs, even when the UI labels them R1/R2/etc.
- Never use ambiguous `latest` as an approval/release input.
- `quoted_not_modeled`, `modeled_not_quoted`, `modified`, etc. are contextual projections, not a persisted mega-status on `FurnitureInstance`.
- Quantity > 1 becomes distinct physical units where unit traceability is required.
- Published DesignRevision and accepted QuoteRevision are immutable.
- Preview/artifacts come from server metadata/storage, never browser `.skp` parsing.
- React consumes generated DTOs/clients from #496 and tenant-safe server state.
- Loading, stale, partial, empty, no-results, forbidden, conflict, offline and error are distinct accessible states.
- Success appears only after server-authoritative commit or a reviewed optimistic contract with rollback.
- Web-to-SketchUp handoff uses #499; no web JWT/custom-URI credential leakage.

## Progressive delivery order

```text
Gate A
→ #385/#386
→ #500 Web Project Furniture

#387/#388
→ #499 pairing contract/runtime

#392
→ #501 Designs/revision history/artifacts

#393/#394/#395
→ #502 reconciliation/approval/release
```

The children may share components/read models where appropriate, but may not collapse into an oversized PR that hides partial completion.

## Tracker acceptance criteria

- [ ] #500 is complete and proves quantity > 1/unit identity.
- [ ] #501 is complete and proves immutable exact revision history/artifacts.
- [ ] #502 is complete and proves explicit reconciliation/requote/approval/release.
- [ ] #499 provides a secure exact Design handoff to SketchUp.
- [ ] All Web surfaces consume #496 generated contracts and tenant-scoped server state.
- [ ] A newer DesignRevision never retargets an existing ProductionRelease.
- [ ] React does not duplicate domain/manufacturing/reconciliation logic.
- [ ] Cross-organization capability/redaction behavior is proven.
- [ ] Browser E2E participates in #398's Digital Thread gate.

## Negative proof required

The tracker cannot close if:

- Web integration is represented by mocks/static local data;
- Project Furniture collapses quantity into QuoteLine identity;
- old revision views silently show latest data;
- React parses `.skp` or computes manufacturing/reconciliation truth;
- Web tokens appear in SketchUp deep links;
- release history retargets after a newer DesignRevision;
- one child is marked done by an isolated component without its generated API/backend integration.

## Definition of Done

#500, #501, #502 and #499 are closed according to their real Definitions of Done, their exact-revision and identity invariants are covered by browser/backend/SketchUp E2E, and the Project workspace communicates the complete digital thread without duplicated business or manufacturing truth.

# Material-aware furniture resolution — espesor efectivo y propagación de acabados

## Objetivo

Cerrar una inconsistencia crítica entre catálogo, motor paramétrico, layout Go y Granete for SketchUp: **el material seleccionado debe participar en la resolución geométrica antes de evaluar fórmulas y todos los componentes ligados al mismo rol de material deben actualizarse juntos**.

Tracks #290. Se cruza con el Digital Thread de #384 para persistencia/revisiones de diseño, pero la corrección de verdad geométrica no debe esperar a ese programa.

## Síntoma real observado

Un mueble puede tener un material elegido de 16 mm y, aun así, SketchUp dibuja partes del cuerpo a 15 mm y frentes a 18 mm. Además, cambiar el acabado de cuerpo/frente no garantiza todavía, como contrato verificable, que todas las piezas dependientes cambien material + espesor + geometría de forma coherente.

## Causa técnica confirmada

- `packages/domain/src/engine/bom.ts` ya resuelve `T` desde `MaterialBoard.thicknessMm` cuando existe una elección para el `optionRole`.
- `backend-go/internal/domain/engine/resolve.go` expande el BOM compuesto con `Component.ThicknessMm` antes de resolver materiales.
- `backend-go/internal/domain/engine/layout.go`, que alimenta el layout de SketchUp, repite el mismo orden para `T`, fórmulas, posiciones y AABB; el material se adjunta después principalmente para identidad/visual.
- El plugin Ruby consume correctamente `dimensionsMm` del layout resuelto; arreglar el espesor localmente en Ruby duplicaría manufacturing truth y violaría la arquitectura.

## Invariantes no negociables

1. **Granete owns manufacturing truth.** SketchUp no calcula espesor industrial.
2. Para una pieza de tablero con material elegido, el espesor efectivo es `MaterialBoard.thicknessMm`.
3. El espesor efectivo entra **antes** de fórmulas de tamaño, posición, poses y anchors.
4. `Component.ThicknessMm` es fallback/default de autoría cuando no existe material resuelto; no gana sobre un material elegido.
5. La relación de acabado es semántica por rol (`optionRole` / material binding), nunca por nombre, color o textura.
6. Cambiar un acabado implica **re-resolve + rebuild**, no sólo repintar geometría existente.
7. La dimensión exterior del mueble permanece estable salvo fórmula explícita; cambian las dimensiones internas/dependientes.
8. Herrajes y features anclados a piezas deben seguir la geometría recalculada.
9. Si una regla existe en TS y Go, debe existir prueba de paridad que detecte drift.
10. Un error de resolución no puede dejar el modelo SketchUp parcialmente reconstruido.

## Autoridad documental

Este programa añade/actualiza como autoridad:

- `docs/architecture/material-aware-furniture-resolution.md`
- `docs/architecture/smart-furniture-engine.md`
- `AGENTS.md`

Y debe leerse junto con:

- `docs/architecture/parametric-furniture-library.md`
- `docs/architecture/domain-model.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`
- `docs/architecture/catalog-option-selector.md`
- `docs/sketchup-manufacturing-contract.md`

## Issues en orden

| Slice | Issue | Entrega | Hard prerequisite |
|---|---:|---|---|
| MT-DOC | #409 | Contrato canónico material-aware y referencias arquitectónicas | — |
| MT-1 | #402 | Go BOM + layout usan el mismo espesor efectivo del material | #409 |
| MT-2 | #403 | Binding semántico por rol, compatibilidad de `optionRoles[]` y aliases | #409 |
| MT-3 | #404 | SketchUp re-resuelve y reconstruye todas las piezas afectadas | #402 + #403 |
| MT-4 | #405 | Regresión/paridad TS ↔ Go ↔ SketchUp con espesores mixtos/agregados | #402 + #403 + #404 |

## Dependency graph

```mermaid
graph TD
    D["#409 Contrato material-aware"] --> A["#402 MT-1 Effective thickness"]
    D --> B["#403 MT-2 Material binding roles"]
    A --> C["#404 MT-3 SketchUp propagation/rebuild"]
    B --> C
    A --> T["#405 MT-4 Parity/regression"]
    B --> T
    C --> T
```

## Escenario de aceptación del programa

Un gabinete de 600 mm tiene componentes históricamente definidos con espesores 15/18 mm. Se selecciona:

```text
BODY  -> Blanco 16 mm
FRONT -> Blanco 16 mm
```

Resultado esperado:

- laterales, piso, techo, entrepaños y demás piezas ligadas a `BODY` usan 16 mm;
- puertas/frentes ligados a `FRONT` usan 16 mm;
- fórmulas como `PW - 2*T` usan `T=16`;
- posiciones como `rightSide.x = PW - T` usan `T=16`;
- el mueble continúa midiendo externamente 600 mm;
- SketchUp refleja exactamente el layout resuelto por Granete.

Después se cambia sólo:

```text
FRONT -> Roble 18 mm
```

El cuerpo permanece en 16 mm; todas las puertas/frentes pasan a 18 mm y sus herrajes/anchors se recalculan.

## Fuera de alcance

- resolver espesor mediante `pushpull` local en Ruby;
- buscar piezas por color/nombre de material;
- convertir SketchUp en fuente de verdad de BOM;
- migrar automáticamente roles históricos ambiguos sin mapeo explícito;
- fingir persistencia de scope “toda la obra” antes de que el binding Project/Design de #384 esté disponible.

## Definition of Done

- #402–#405 cerradas con pruebas;
- no existe drift conocido entre TS y Go para effective thickness;
- el cambio de material de un rol actualiza todas y sólo las piezas dependientes;
- el smoke de SketchUp demuestra rebuild atómico y preservación de identidad;
- documentación y AGENTS apuntan a la autoridad correcta.
