- #405 TS↔Go↔SketchUp parity/regression for mixed thicknesses and propagation — **closed/completed**.

The original failure mode is covered by the delivered contract and tests:

```text
selected MaterialBoard thickness
→ effective T before formulas/poses/anchors
→ exact Go BOM/layout result
→ native SketchUp rebuild
→ role-isolated propagation
→ failure preserves previous valid hierarchy
```

Remaining professional interactions such as moving shelves and editing/substituting hardware are intentionally owned by #467/#468 and the shared host runtime #498. They do not represent unfinished material-aware resolution and must not keep this META open.

Result: the global Definition of Done of #401 is satisfied. Closing as completed; future regressions belong in focused defects against #402–#405 contracts rather than reopening the program.

issues.title: [META][P0] Material-aware furniture resolution — espesor efectivo y propagación de acabados

issues.body:
## Objective

Make both Go furniture resolvers—the manufacturing BOM resolver and the SketchUp layout resolver—use the **selected `MaterialBoard.thicknessMm` as the effective thickness** before evaluating geometry, formulas, positions, poses or anchors.

Tracks #401 and #290.

## Hard prerequisite

- #409 — canonical material-aware architecture contract merged to `main`.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/material-aware-furniture-resolution.md` (delivered by #409)
- `docs/architecture/smart-furniture-engine.md`
- `docs/architecture/parametric-furniture-library.md`
- `packages/domain/src/engine/bom.ts` as current TS semantic reference

## Problem

Today the TypeScript domain already resolves `T` from the chosen material when a component role has a material choice. Both Go paths diverge: `backend-go/internal/domain/engine/resolve.go` expands composed BOM components with `T = Component.ThicknessMm` before material resolution, and `layout.go` does the same for the SketchUp layout before attaching the selected material.

That creates observable drift such as:

```text
selected material = Blanco 16 mm
left/right body component definition = 15 mm
front component definition = 18 mm
SketchUp result = 15 / 18 mm   ❌
expected = 16 / 16 mm           ✅
```

This is not a SketchUp rendering bug. It is a server-side manufacturing/layout truth bug.

## Required scope

1. Add one canonical effective-thickness resolution path in Go and consume it from both `resolve.go` and `layout.go`:

```text
component optionRole
  -> selected material id
  -> active MaterialBoard
  -> effective T = material.thicknessMm
  -> evaluate formulas/poses/AABB
```

2. When no material is selected for a preview role, preserve current authoring fallback behavior using component/default thickness.
3. Use effective `T` consistently in both Go BOM expansion and Go layout expansion, including:
   - length/width formula context;
   - spatial formula context;
   - `defaultPoseForPlacement`;
   - board local dimensions;
   - AABB/translation derivation;
   - hardware anchor host geometry.
4. Audit `layout.go` for hardcoded `T: 18` or equivalent fallback values, especially agregado parent/unit contexts and legacy paths. Replace hardcoded manufacturing assumptions where the selected role/material is available.
5. Keep `LayoutComponent.ThicknessMm` consistent with the effective thickness actually used to build `DimensionsMm`.
6. Preserve explicit unknown/inactive-material failure semantics.
7. Do **not** patch thickness in Ruby/SketchUp.

## Canonical precedence

```text
selected active MaterialBoard.thicknessMm
  > component authoring/default thickness
  > explicit legacy fallback only where no material binding exists
```

A selected material must never lose to the component's nominal thickness.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A component nominally authored at 15 mm but bound to a selected 16 mm material resolves with `ThicknessMm == 16` in both Go BOM and Go layout outputs.
- [ ] A component nominally authored at 18 mm but bound to the same selected 16 mm material resolves with `ThicknessMm == 16`.
- [ ] Formula `PW - 2*T` is evaluated using selected material thickness.
- [ ] Default right-side placement uses `PW - T` with selected material thickness.
- [ ] Go BOM and Go layout agree for mixed roles: BODY=16 and FRONT=18 produce different effective thicknesses in the same furniture.
- [ ] Hardware anchored to FRONT follows the recalculated 18 mm front geometry.
- [ ] Agregado components use their own resolved material thickness rather than an unrelated hardcoded 18 mm context where `T` is semantically available.
- [ ] Existing no-choice preview behavior remains deterministic.
- [ ] Unknown/inactive selected material fails loudly before mutating any SketchUp model.

## Negative proof required

Add regression tests that fail if:

- `comp.ThicknessMm` wins over a selected material;
- a hardcoded 18 mm leaks into a formula for a component whose selected material is 16 mm;
- `LayoutComponent.ThicknessMm` and the thickness axis in `DimensionsMm` disagree.

## Suggested implementation area

Primary:

- `backend-go/internal/domain/engine/resolve.go`
- `backend-go/internal/domain/engine/resolve_test.go`
- `backend-go/internal/domain/engine/layout.go`
- `backend-go/internal/domain/engine/layout_test.go`

Reference/parity:

- `packages/domain/src/engine/bom.ts`

API contract should remain client-agnostic; SketchUp continues consuming resolved boxes.

## Explicit non-goals

- changing material-role authoring semantics (MT-2);
- changing the SketchUp selector/rebuild flow (MT-3);
- introducing client-side manufacturing calculations;
- migrating old component roles automatically.

## Definition of Done

Go BOM and layout tests prove one shared effective-thickness rule drives every dependent calculation and no known nominal/hardcoded-thickness path can reproduce the original 16→15/18 mismatch.
issues.title: [P0][MT-1] Resolve effective board thickness from selected MaterialBoard in Go BOM and layout

issues.body:
## Objective

Define and enforce how furniture components declare **which finish/material selection they follow**, so changing one material role updates all and only the intended pieces.

Tracks #401 and #290.

## Hard prerequisite

- #409 — canonical material-aware architecture contract merged to `main`.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/material-aware-furniture-resolution.md`
- `docs/architecture/domain-model.md`
- `docs/architecture/parametric-furniture-library.md`
- `docs/architecture/catalog-option-selector.md`

## Problem

Physical component identity and material-selection identity are different concerns.

Examples:

```text
LEFT_SIDE      = physical/semantic placement
BASE           = physical/semantic placement
SHELF          = physical/semantic placement
DOOR           = physical/semantic placement

BODY           = material binding role
FRONT          = material binding role
BACK           = material binding role
PLINTH         = material binding role
```

Today components persist `optionRoles: string[]`, but TS BOM and both Go resolvers consume only `optionRoles[0]`, while UI discovery/validation iterates every entry. A second board role can therefore appear configurable but never govern the piece. Catalogs can also be authored with fragmented roles such as `LATERAL`, `INTERIOR`, `FONDO`, `FRENTE`. If the user conceptually chooses “Cuerpo”, we must not require separate choices for every physical part unless the furniture definition intentionally wants different finishes.

## Canonical decision

For the current compatibility model, **`optionRoles[0]` is the single persisted material-binding key**. A rectangular board participating in material selection must not declare multiple competing board roles; additional entries are invalid/ambiguous until an explicit model evolution defines their meaning. Do not introduce a parallel `materialRole` field merely to rename the same concept unless implementation proves it necessary.

The semantic distinction must still be explicit:

- component `placement` / physical role answers **what piece is this / where does it belong?**
- component primary `optionRoles[0]` answers **which material choice does this piece follow?**

Never infer the binding from component name, material name, color, texture, manufacturer or current visual appearance.

## Required scope

1. Document and enforce the distinction between physical role and material binding role.
2. Establish workshop-friendly role conventions for common furniture while keeping the system open/extensible:
   - `BODY`
   - `FRONT`
   - `BACK`
   - `PLINTH`
   - other explicit workshop-defined roles where truly needed.
3. Update catalog authoring semantics so pieces intended to share one finish use the same `optionRole`.
4. Keep UI labels sourced from `OptionGroup.name`; do not expose raw internal codes when a friendly label exists.
5. Preserve backward compatibility for existing roles. **No blind automatic migration** from `LATERAL`/`INTERIOR` to `BODY`; ambiguous catalogs require explicit mapping/editor changes.
6. Ensure structures, module-level components and agregado components use the same binding semantics.
7. Validate that one role can bind many component instances and one furniture can contain multiple independent roles.
8. Add validation for empty/invalid board binding roles and for `optionRoles.length > 1` on rectangular boards that participate in material selection.
9. Centralize legacy alias behavior currently present only in TS: direct role wins; otherwise `ZOCLO`, `PUERTA`, `PUERTA_*` and `FRENTE_CAJON` may inherit `FRENTE`. Go must mirror the same explicit alias table or reject the unsupported alias—never silently use different lookup semantics.

## Reference scenario

A base cabinet contains:

```text
left side      -> BODY
right side     -> BODY
base           -> BODY
top            -> BODY
shelf          -> BODY
door           -> FRONT
back           -> BACK
```

Material choices:

```text
BODY  -> Blanco 16
FRONT -> Roble 18
BACK  -> Blanco 6
```

Changing `FRONT` must not alter BODY or BACK. Changing `BODY` must update every body component, regardless of their physical placement/name.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A definition can bind multiple physical component types to one material role.
- [ ] Door and drawer-front components can share `FRONT` across normal module components and agregados.
- [ ] BODY selection affects left/right sides, base, top, shelves and other explicitly bound pieces without name-based logic.
- [ ] Existing custom workshop option roles continue to work when used as the single primary binding.
- [ ] Rectangular boards with multiple material-binding roles are rejected or surfaced as ambiguous; no secondary role appears selectable without affecting resolution.
- [ ] TS and Go apply the same explicit direct-role/legacy-alias precedence.
- [ ] Option-group labels remain configurable and user-facing.
- [ ] No code path selects dependent components by material display name, color or texture.
- [ ] Validation/tests cover one-to-many role binding and mixed-role furniture.

## Negative proof required

Tests must reject or expose:

- a material-binding decision inferred from current color/name;
- a component that silently changes role because of physical placement;
- an agregado front that fails to follow the same `FRONT` choice as a normal door when both are explicitly bound to `FRONT`;
- a second `optionRoles[]` entry that appears configurable but never affects the resolved material;
- TS resolving a legacy alias while Go silently falls back to nominal thickness or a different material.

## Suggested implementation areas

Likely touches:

- component/catalog domain types and validation
- module/structure/agregado editors in React
- catalog projection to SketchUp (`materialRoles`)
- fixtures/tests

Prefer evolving existing `optionRole` semantics over adding a parallel `materialRole` field unless a concrete incompatibility is demonstrated.

## Explicit non-goals

- resolving effective thickness itself (MT-1 / #402);
- SketchUp rebuild behavior (MT-3);
- automatic migration of ambiguous legacy catalogs;
- hardcoding Granete to kitchen-only role names.

## Definition of Done

The catalog has an explicit, tested single-binding contract for “these components follow this finish selection”, including multi-role rejection and identical alias precedence across TS, Go, web editors and SketchUp.
issues.title: [P0][MT-2] Define canonical material binding roles for furniture components

issues.body:
## Objective

Harden Granete for SketchUp so changing a furniture material selection updates **every component bound to that role**, including effective thickness, dependent dimensions, positions and hardware anchors, by asking Granete to re-resolve the full layout and atomically rebuilding the **native managed ComponentInstance hierarchy**.

Tracks #401, #413 and #290.

## Hard prerequisites

- #402 — effective material thickness in Go BOM/layout
- #403 — canonical material binding semantics
- #415 — native SketchUp Furniture/Part ComponentInstance renderer

#414 is an indirect prerequisite through #415 and provides the authoritative local part transform/orientation contract.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/material-aware-furniture-resolution.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-native-entity-model.md`
- ADR-0004
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`
- `docs/architecture/smart-furniture-engine.md`
- `docs/sketchup-manufacturing-contract.md`
- ADR-0001

## Why the native-entity prerequisite was added

The previous plan correctly required re-resolve + rebuild, but the runtime still uses Group-based boxes. Implementing the final material rebuild against that renderer would harden an architecture that #415 immediately replaces.

Canonical target:

```text
material selector
  -> materialChoices[role] = materialId
  -> Granete resolves effective material/thickness
  -> local dimensions + authoritative part transforms
  -> native Furniture/Part ComponentInstance layout
  -> atomic SketchUp rebuild
```

## Required behavior

When the user changes:

```text
FRONT: Blanco 16 -> Roble 18
```

Granete for SketchUp must:

1. update authoring intent (`materialChoices.FRONT`);
2. request a fresh full layout from Granete;
3. receive all resolved local board dimensions/transforms/hardware with effective thickness;
4. rebuild/rebind affected managed native part ComponentInstances inside the owning furniture;
5. preserve the top-level Furniture ComponentInstance business identity and outer placement/transform;
6. update persisted metadata only for the successfully resolved/rebuilt state;
7. keep roles not changed by the user untouched in intent;
8. refresh every component sharing `FRONT`, including doors and drawer fronts inside agregados;
9. recalculate hardware placements from their host component geometry;
10. never mutate an immutable/shared part SketchUp ComponentDefinition in a way that changes unrelated furniture/parts.

## Definition lifecycle during rebuild

Follow #413/#415:

- top-level furniture SketchUp definition is unique per `FurnitureInstance` in V1;
- part definitions may be unique or immutable-shared;
- if material thickness/model changes geometry, rebind/recreate the part definition/instance as needed;
- do not use non-uniform SketchUp scale;
- do not edit a shared definition in-place.

## Atomicity requirement

A failed remote/layout resolution must **not** destroy the current valid furniture geometry.

Preferred sequence:

```text
resolve/validate new layout
→ prepare definitions/assets
→ start SketchUp operation
→ replace/rebind child hierarchy
→ write accepted metadata
→ commit
```

Any failure before commit aborts and leaves the previous valid hierarchy intact.

## Identity requirements

Preserve across a successful material change:

- Project `furnitureInstanceId` when available;
- compatibility `instanceRef` only as required by #388 migration;
- top-level furniture world transform/location;
- Project/Design binding;
- Granete `componentInstanceId` semantics for resolved children;
- authoring parameters/material choices.

SketchUp child `persistent_id`s and generated definition GUIDs are technical implementation details and may change during regeneration.

## Furniture-scope vs project-scope

This issue fully supports **this furniture** scope.

For “toda la obra” / project default:

- preserve `project defaults + item overrides` semantics;
- durable project-wide propagation remains tied to #384 Project/Design persistence;
- temporary authoring-session defaults must not be presented as persisted manufacturing truth.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Changing `BODY` updates all BODY-bound native part ComponentInstances and no FRONT/BACK part.
- [ ] Changing `FRONT` updates a normal door and all drawer fronts bound to FRONT.
- [ ] A 16→18 mm choice changes local SketchUp part geometry/definition according to server result, not only texture.
- [ ] Local axes remain correct after rebuild.
- [ ] Dependent positions/transforms follow the new resolved layout.
- [ ] Front-hosted hardware moves with recalculated host geometry.
- [ ] Top-level furniture business ID and world transform survive rebuild.
- [ ] FI-A material change cannot alter FI-B through shared SketchUp definitions.
- [ ] `materialChoices` metadata round-trips after save/reopen/update.
- [ ] Resolution/rebuild failure leaves previous valid native hierarchy intact.
- [ ] Undo produces one coherent user action.
- [ ] No Ruby method derives manufacturing thickness or part orientation locally.
- [ ] No managed productive dimension change uses non-uniform scale.

## Negative proof required

Tests detect:

- paint-only update;
- only first component of a role updates;
- drawer fronts in agregados miss FRONT propagation;
- failed resolution clears the furniture;
- business identity/world transform loss;
- shared definition mutation changes another furniture;
- Group-only rebuild accepted as final target;
- Ruby infers orientation from role/AABB.

## Likely implementation areas

- `apps/sketchup-extension/src/granete_for_sketchup/ui/dialog_controller.rb`
- `apps/sketchup-extension/src/granete_for_sketchup/model/furniture_builder.rb`
- `apps/sketchup-extension/src/granete_for_sketchup/resources/dialog.html`
- metadata/round-trip/native hierarchy tests

## Explicit non-goals

- manufacturing thickness rules in Ruby;
- durable Project/Design sync outside #384;
- optimizing to differential geometry patching;
- automatic legacy Group migration (#416).

## Definition of Done

A material change demonstrably re-resolves and atomically rebuilds the canonical native ComponentInstance hierarchy with correct material-driven geometry, while preserving furniture identity/placement and preventing shared-definition side effects.
issues.title: [P0][MT-3] Re-resolve and atomically rebuild SketchUp furniture when a material role changes

issues.body:
## Objective

Add a regression/parity suite that permanently detects drift between the TypeScript manufacturing domain, the Go BOM/layout resolvers and the SketchUp adapter for **material-driven thickness, dependent geometry and role propagation**.

Tracks #401 and #290.

## Hard prerequisites

- #402
- #403
- #404 for the full SketchUp propagation scenario

Tests for #402/#403 may land incrementally before #404, but this issue closes only after the complete cross-layer scenario is covered.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/material-aware-furniture-resolution.md`
- `docs/verification.md`
- `docs/architecture/smart-furniture-engine.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`

## Why a dedicated parity slice

This bug exists because two engines evolved differently:

```text
TypeScript domain: selected MaterialBoard -> T
Go BOM/layout:     Component.ThicknessMm -> T
```

Both paths had tests, but the fixtures mostly used matching 18 mm values, so semantic drift remained invisible. This must become an explicit contract fixture, not an incidental unit test.

## Canonical fixture

Create one reusable cabinet fixture (or equivalent mirrored fixtures) with deliberately conflicting nominal component thicknesses:

```text
left/right side nominal = 15
base/top/shelf nominal   = 18
door nominal             = 18
back nominal             = 15
```

Materials:

```text
white16 = 16 mm
front18 = 18 mm
back6   = 6 mm
```

Bindings:

```text
BODY  -> left/right/base/top/shelf
FRONT -> door + drawer fronts
BACK  -> back
```

Include an agregado with 3 drawer fronts bound to `FRONT` and at least one visible hardware placement anchored to a front.

## Required scenarios

### Scenario A — all visible boards 16 mm where bound

```text
BODY  -> white16
FRONT -> white16
```

Prove:

- every BODY board resolves to 16 mm despite 15/18 nominal values;
- every FRONT board resolves to 16 mm;
- formulas using `T` use 16;
- placements using `PW - T` use 16;
- SketchUp receives and builds the same resolved dimensions.

### Scenario B — mixed roles

```text
BODY  -> white16
FRONT -> front18
BACK  -> back6
```

Prove role isolation and correct mixed thicknesses in one furniture instance.

### Scenario C — change FRONT 18 -> 16

Prove after update:

- all doors and all 3 drawer fronts change;
- BODY/BACK remain unchanged;
- front-hosted hardware recomputes from new host geometry;
- furniture instance identity and outer transform remain stable;
- metadata stores the new material choice.

### Scenario D — failure safety

Use an unknown/inactive material or simulated layout failure and prove SketchUp keeps the previous valid managed furniture intact.

## Cross-engine assertions

Where the representation differs (e.g. Go AABB vs TS board-local dimensions), compare semantic invariants rather than byte-identical payloads:

- component/part role and identity mapping;
- effective thickness;
- evaluated length/width;
- relevant position/pose consequences;
- selected material id;
- unchanged external furniture dimensions;
- affected-vs-unaffected role set.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] TS fixture proves selected material thickness wins over component nominal thickness.
- [ ] Go BOM and Go layout fixtures prove the same result.
- [ ] A parity test/contract comparison fails if either engine reverts to component thickness.
- [ ] Agregado drawer fronts participate in the same FRONT binding.
- [ ] SketchUp builder test verifies `dimensionsMm` are consumed without local thickness rewriting.
- [ ] Inspector/update round-trip verifies a role change rebuilds every dependent board.
- [ ] Failure/rollback path is covered.
- [ ] Fixtures intentionally include non-18 thicknesses; no parity test is allowed to pass only because all defaults equal 18.

## Negative proof required

At least one test must specifically fail against the pre-fix Go behavior (`comp.ThicknessMm` winning) so the regression is demonstrated, not merely inferred.

## Likely implementation areas

- `packages/domain/src/engine/*.test.ts`
- `backend-go/internal/domain/engine/resolve_test.go`
- `backend-go/internal/domain/engine/layout_test.go`
- `backend-go/internal/api/furniture_layout_test.go` if query/material contract needs coverage
- `apps/sketchup-extension/test/unit/furniture_builder_test.rb`
- `apps/sketchup-extension/test/unit/dialog_controller_test.rb`
- existing material selector/round-trip tests

## Definition of Done

The exact original mismatch (selected 16 mm but 15/18 mm SketchUp geometry) is reproducible by a pre-fix regression and impossible to reintroduce without failing TS/Go/SketchUp verification.
issues.title: [P0][MT-4] Add TS ↔ Go ↔ SketchUp parity regressions for material thickness and finish propagation

issues.body:
## Objetivo

Documentar el contrato arquitectónico canónico que ordena la resolución de materiales y geometría del mueble antes de implementar los cambios de motor.

Tracks #401 y el programa SketchUp #290. Esta entrega documental desbloquea la implementación de #402 y #403.

## Problema

TypeScript, los resolvers Go y Granete for SketchUp no expresan hoy una única regla verificable para:

1. resolver el `MaterialBoard` elegido antes de evaluar `T`, fórmulas, posiciones, poses y anchors;
2. propagar un cambio de acabado a todas y sólo las piezas vinculadas al mismo material-binding role;
3. tratar de forma compatible `optionRoles[]`, aliases históricos y fallbacks nominales.

La ausencia de este contrato permitió que TS use el espesor del material mientras Go BOM/layout usan el espesor nominal del componente.

## Alcance requerido

- Crear `docs/architecture/material-aware-furniture-resolution.md` como autoridad canónica.
- Documentar el pipeline normativo:

```text
selected MaterialBoard
→ effective thickness T
→ geometric formulas
→ spatial formulas / pose
→ anchors / AABB
→ resolved DTO
→ renderer
```

- Diferenciar physical/placement role de material-binding role.
- Establecer que, en el modelo actual, `optionRoles[0]` es el único binding de material; roles adicionales de tablero son inválidos/ambiguos hasta una evolución explícita.
- Documentar aliases históricos y el drift actual entre TS y Go.
- Definir fallback nominal sólo cuando no existe un binding/material aplicable.
- Definir propagación por role, reconstrucción atómica y comportamiento ante material desconocido/inactivo.
- Incluir una matriz de estado actual y una matriz de verificación TS ↔ Go BOM ↔ Go layout ↔ SketchUp.
- Añadir referencias concisas desde las autoridades existentes y `AGENTS.md`.

## Archivos previstos

- `docs/architecture/material-aware-furniture-resolution.md`
- `docs/architecture.md`
- `docs/architecture/smart-furniture-engine.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`
- `docs/architecture/catalog-option-selector.md`
- `AGENTS.md`

## Criterios de aceptación

- [ ] La documentación declara que `MaterialBoard.thicknessMm` gana sobre el espesor nominal cuando existe una selección aplicable.
- [ ] El orden de resolución impide evaluar fórmulas/posiciones antes de conocer el material efectivo.
- [ ] La documentación reconoce que el defecto actual afecta tanto `resolve.go` como `layout.go`.
- [ ] La semántica vigente de `optionRoles[]` y de los aliases queda explícita, sin prometer una migración automática ambigua.
- [ ] Un cambio de role se define como re-resolve + rebuild atómico, no como repintado.
- [ ] Las matrices muestran estado actual, target y prueba requerida por runtime.
- [ ] Las fuentes canónicas enlazan el nuevo contrato sin duplicar reglas extensas.
- [ ] El PR es exclusivamente documental y enlaza #401–#405.

## Verificación

- Readback estructural de todos los Markdown modificados.
- Enlaces/rutas citados existen.
- Ningún archivo de motor, UI, API, test productivo o fixture es modificado.

## Fuera de alcance

- Implementar #402–#405.
- Corregir el espesor en Ruby.
- Migrar automáticamente catálogos con múltiples roles ambiguos.
- Afirmar persistencia project-wide antes del Digital Thread #384.

## Definition of Done

El contrato queda versionado en `main`, los documentos canónicos apuntan a él y #402/#403 pueden implementarse sin decisiones de dominio implícitas.

issues.body:
# SketchUp native entity model — Furniture/Parts as ComponentInstances

## Objective

Evolve Granete for SketchUp from the current `Group` + AABB-box renderer toward a native SketchUp model where managed furniture and physical parts are `Sketchup::ComponentInstance`s with explicit local axes, contract identities and safe definition lifecycle.

Tracks #290. Align with #384 (Project Digital Thread), #401 (material-aware resolution) and the authoring identity contract from #346.

## Confirmed current gap

```text
CURRENT
Furniture Group
  ├── Board Group + faces/pushpull
  └── Hardware Group/asset

TARGET
Furniture SU ComponentInstance
  ├── Board/Part SU ComponentInstance
  ├── Hardware SU ComponentInstance
  └── optional semantic Aggregate/Subassembly SU ComponentInstance
      └── nested managed instances
```

Current `LayoutComponent` exposes `lengthMm/widthMm/thicknessMm` plus world/AABB `translationMm`/`dimensionsMm`, while board rotation remains internal to the resolver. Simply replacing `add_group` with `add_instance` would therefore create components with an incomplete local frame or force Ruby to reconstruct placement rules.

## Canonical identity decision

Do **not** collapse the authoring schema identities into SketchUp or catalog IDs.

| Identity | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `furnitureInstanceId` | Project-owned physical furniture identity |
| `furnitureDefinitionId` | Granete furniture catalog/template identity |
| `componentInstanceId` | concrete authoring/component occurrence |
| `componentDefinitionId` | stable reusable **authoring-definition ID** from the Granete contract (#346) |
| `catalogComponentId` | optional catalog component reference/provenance |
| SU ComponentDefinition GUID | host technical locator only |
| SU `persistent_id` | host technical locator only |

Hard rules:

```text
componentDefinitionId != native SU definition GUID
componentDefinitionId != catalogComponentId unless an explicit future schema maps them
furnitureInstanceId   != persistent_id
```

A native SU ComponentDefinition may carry/associate the Granete `componentDefinitionId` in namespaced metadata; its host GUID is never the contract ID.

## Canonical host decisions

1. Top-level managed furniture = native `Sketchup::ComponentInstance`.
2. Physical managed board/part = nested native `Sketchup::ComponentInstance`.
3. Optional subassembly/agregado level only for real semantic identity/interaction; no fixed three-level wrappers.
4. V1 top-level SU ComponentDefinition is isolated per `FurnitureInstance` to prevent shared-definition edits FI-A→FI-B.
5. Part SU definitions may be unique initially; sharing only when generated definitions are immutable/content-addressed by `resolvedGeometrySignature`.
6. Board geometry lives in local coordinates; Granete sends authoritative local→parent transform/orientation.
7. Ruby never infers rotation from role/name/AABB and never calculates manufacturing thickness.
8. Managed productive dimensions are regenerated/rebound, never represented by non-uniform scale.
9. Material change #404 rebuilds this native hierarchy atomically.
10. Copy/paste #391 allocates a new business ID and isolates the copied top-level host definition.
11. Legacy Granete Groups migrate explicitly (#416); arbitrary user geometry stays unmanaged.
12. OpenCutList compatibility is validation/convenience only, never manufacturing authority.

## Local axes

Retain current engine convention unless explicitly versioned:

```text
local X = widthMm
local Y = thicknessMm
local Z = lengthMm
```

World AABB may remain for preview/backward compatibility but does not replace the local frame.

## Material-aware sequence

```text
MaterialBoard choice
→ effective thickness (#402)
→ local dimensions/poses
→ authoritative transform (#414)
→ native renderer (#415)
→ material rebuild (#404)
→ parity regression (#405)
```

Therefore #404 must not close on the Group renderer as its final implementation.

## Digital Thread impact

- #388 binding remains based on Granete business IDs, not native definition IDs.
- #389 Place existing FI uses #415 hierarchy.
- #390 creates/gets Project FI before connected rendering.
- #391 copy/duplicate uses top-level managed ComponentInstances but allocates identity server-side.
- #392 publishes semantic managed state, not arbitrary SketchUp components.
- #397 separates legacy representation migration (#416) from business adoption.
- #398 asserts required native-host invariants and leaves low-level host/OCL checks to #417.

## Issues / order

| Slice | Issue | Delivery | Hard prerequisite |
|---|---:|---|---|
| SU-ENT-DOC | #418 | canonical doc + ADR + cross-doc reconciliation | — |
| SU-ENT-1 | #414 | authoritative local transform/orientation | #418 |
| SU-ENT-2 | #415 | native Furniture/Part ComponentInstance renderer | #414 |
| SU-ENT-3 | #416 | legacy Group representation migration | #415 |
| SU-ENT-4 | #417 | native host + OpenCutList validation | #414 + #415 |

```mermaid
graph TD
  D["#418 docs + ADR"] --> T["#414 local transform"]
  T --> R["#415 native renderer"]
  R --> M["#416 legacy migration"]
  T --> V["#417 host/OCL validation"]
  R --> V
  R --> MAT["#404 material rebuild"]
  MAT --> PAR["#405 material parity"]
  R --> PF["#389 Place existing FI"]
  R --> DUP["#391 copy/duplicate"]
  M --> ADOPT["#397 adopt existing SKP"]
```

## Definition of Done

- #418 approved/merged;
- #414 removes orientation inference from Ruby;
- #415 renders furniture/physical parts as native ComponentInstances with identity/definition isolation;
- `componentDefinitionId` remains independent from native GUID and catalog reference;
- #404 rebuilds the native hierarchy;
- #416 preserves legacy models without inventing identity;
- #417 provides real SketchUp/OpenCutList evidence;
- Digital Thread placement/copy/adoption consume the model without creating parallel identity concepts.

issues.title: [META][P0] SketchUp native entity model — Furniture/Parts as ComponentInstances

issues.body:
## Objective

Extend the resolved furniture layout consumed by Granete for SketchUp so every managed board carries enough **authoritative local geometry + transform information** to be instantiated as a native SketchUp `ComponentInstance` with correct local axes, without re-deriving placement rules in Ruby.

Tracks #413 and #290. Intersects #401/#402 because effective thickness changes local board geometry.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/sketchup-native-entity-model.md`
- ADR-0004 (native SketchUp entity model)
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`
- `docs/architecture/material-aware-furniture-resolution.md`

## Problem

Current `LayoutComponent` exposes both semantic local dimensions (`lengthMm`, `widthMm`, `thicknessMm`) and a world/workshop AABB (`translationMm`, `dimensionsMm`), but the public transform contains **translation only**. Rotation exists only inside the resolver's intermediate `layoutBoard` (`rotX/rotY/rotZ`).

That is sufficient to draw a pre-baked axis-aligned Group box, but insufficient to create a native part ComponentDefinition with stable local axes and then place a ComponentInstance correctly.

Ruby must not infer orientation from `slotId`, placement name or AABB dimension order.

## Required target contract

Each resolved board needs an authoritative local-to-furniture transform, for example:

```json
{
  "componentInstanceId": "...",
  "localDimensionsMm": {
    "widthMm": 564,
    "thicknessMm": 16,
    "lengthMm": 570
  },
  "transform": {
    "translationMm": [16, 0, 100],
    "rotationQuaternion": [0, 0, 0, 1]
  }
}
```

Exact representation may be quaternion, orthonormal basis, matrix, or equivalent deterministic transform. Do not expose Euler ambiguity merely because current internals store Euler values.

The contract must distinguish:

- local part geometry/dimensions;
- local→furniture placement/orientation;
- optional AABB for convenience/preview/backward compatibility.

## Local axes invariant

Retain one explicit board-local convention consistent with current engine semantics:

```text
local X = widthMm
local Y = thicknessMm
local Z = lengthMm
```

If the implementation chooses another convention, update all canonical docs/tests in the same PR. Grain/orientation behavior must be deterministic relative to local axes.

## Material-aware requirement

The transform and local dimensions are produced **after** material resolution/effective thickness resolution from #402. A selected 16 mm board must produce local `thicknessMm=16` and any dependent transform must already include the consequences of `T=16`.

## Backward compatibility

- Existing AABB `translationMm`/`dimensionsMm` may remain temporarily for old plugin versions.
- Add an explicit layout schema/revision or capability marker if required so old clients do not silently reinterpret new fields.
- Unknown/new transform contract must fail safely in incompatible plugin versions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A left side, horizontal shelf, back and door all expose correct local dimensions and orientation independently of world AABB shape.
- [ ] Ruby can instantiate every board using only generic transform application; no role-specific rotation table exists in the plugin.
- [ ] 90° placements preserve correct local axes after transformation.
- [ ] Effective material thickness participates before transform derivation.
- [ ] AABB derived from the new local geometry + transform matches current resolved AABB within numeric tolerance.
- [ ] Aggregado child boards use the same contract.
- [ ] Hardware host references remain tied to `componentInstanceId` after the transform contract change.
- [ ] API/Go tests cover serialization and parity with engine board pose.

## Negative proof required

Tests must fail if a client would need to infer board rotation from `slotId`, role name, dimensions or `min-corner AABB` alone.

## Likely implementation areas

- `backend-go/internal/domain/engine/layout.go`
- layout DTO/API tests
- `apps/sketchup-extension/src/granete_for_sketchup/library/catalog_provider.rb` contract parsing tests

## Explicit non-goals

- changing the SketchUp renderer itself (#415);
- calculating manufacturing geometry in Ruby;
- changing material binding semantics (#403).

## Definition of Done

The resolved layout is a sufficient generic scene/authoring contract for a native part ComponentInstance renderer, with stable local axes and no Ruby placement heuristics.
issues.title: [P0][SU-ENT-1] Expose authoritative local part transform/orientation in resolved SketchUp layout

issues.body:
## Objective

Replace the current managed `Group` renderer in Granete for SketchUp with the native entity hierarchy defined by #413: top-level managed furniture as `Sketchup::ComponentInstance`, physical board/components as nested `Sketchup::ComponentInstance`s, and optional semantic subassemblies only where they represent real domain/authoring structure.

Tracks #413 and #290.

## Hard prerequisites

- #414 — authoritative local part transform/orientation contract
- #418 — canonical docs/ADR merged

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/sketchup-native-entity-model.md`
- ADR-0004
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`
- `docs/sketchup-manufacturing-contract.md`
- #346 semantic metadata/round-trip contract

## Identity contract

Do not confuse three different namespaces:

```text
componentDefinitionId = stable Granete authoring-definition ID (#346)
catalogComponentId    = optional catalog component reference
SU definition GUID    = native host locator only
```

Likewise `componentInstanceId` is the Granete authoring/component occurrence identity and does not derive from native `persistent_id`.

A generated/imported SU ComponentDefinition may store/associate `componentDefinitionId` in namespaced metadata, but the host GUID never becomes that contract ID.

## Current behavior to replace

```text
model.active_entities.add_group       -> furniture
main_group.entities.add_group         -> board/hardware fallback
faces + pushpull inside Groups        -> visible box
```

This was acceptable as a visual MVP but is not the final host model.

## Required target hierarchy

```text
Top-level Furniture SU ComponentInstance
  SU definition isolated per FurnitureInstance in V1
  metadata -> furniture business identity + authoring intent

  ├── Board/Part SU ComponentInstance
  │    SU definition -> local solid geometry at origin
  │    instance transform -> server-resolved local→parent pose
  │    metadata -> componentInstanceId + componentDefinitionId
  │                + optional catalogComponentId + slot/role/binding
  │
  ├── Hardware SU ComponentInstance
  └── optional semantic Aggregate/Subassembly SU ComponentInstance
       └── nested managed instances
```

## Definition lifecycle V1

### Furniture

- Dedicated generated SU ComponentDefinition per managed `FurnitureInstance`.
- Do not share a mutable top-level SU definition merely because two units use the same Granete `FurnitureDefinition`.
- Material/parameter rebuild FI-A must not mutate FI-B.

### Parts/components

Safest first implementation:

- unique generated SU definition per rendered part instance is acceptable;
- sharing allowed only for immutable definitions keyed by deterministic `resolvedGeometrySignature`;
- never mutate a shared definition in-place when geometry changes;
- rebind/recreate an instance to another immutable definition when needed.

The geometry signature is an optimization key and never replaces `componentDefinitionId`/`componentInstanceId`.

## Geometry rules

- build board geometry in definition-local coordinates at origin;
- use local `lengthMm/widthMm/thicknessMm` + authoritative transform from #414;
- do not bake world AABB coordinates into definition faces;
- no non-uniform scale for productive dimensions;
- top-level furniture transform remains the user placement/orientation.

## Metadata rules

At minimum preserve/normalize:

Furniture:
- `furnitureInstanceId` once Project-owned identity is available;
- compatibility `instanceRef` during migration only;
- `furnitureDefinitionId`;
- parameters/materialChoices;
- Project/Design references according to #384 stage.

Managed child:
- `componentInstanceId`;
- `componentDefinitionId` authoring-definition ID;
- optional `catalogComponentId`/catalog reference;
- slot/semantic role/material-binding role;
- schema/generation metadata as needed.

## Materials

Visual material application remains host rendering. Manufacturing material/effective thickness remains server/domain truth.

The renderer consumes #402/#414 results; it never recalculates thickness or orientation.

## Selection / Outliner

- top-level click selects the furniture as primary managed unit;
- drill-down reaches semantic nested ComponentInstances;
- names are human-readable but non-authoritative;
- rename never changes Granete IDs;
- selection can recover owning furniture via InstancePath/metadata.

## Atomicity / Undo

Insertion/rebuild is one coherent SketchUp operation.

- failure leaves no half-managed hierarchy;
- rebuild preserves furniture business identity + world transform;
- child host `persistent_id`s may change during regeneration;
- accepted metadata is written only with the accepted hierarchy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Newly inserted managed furniture is top-level `Sketchup::ComponentInstance`, not Group.
- [ ] Every resolved physical board is nested `Sketchup::ComponentInstance` with local solid geometry.
- [ ] Local axes/dimensions match #414 after standard orientations and furniture world rotation.
- [ ] Two furniture units from same Granete definition diverge independently without host-definition side effects.
- [ ] `componentDefinitionId` remains stable contract identity and is not native GUID.
- [ ] Optional catalog reference remains separate from authoring-definition identity.
- [ ] Rename does not alter IDs.
- [ ] Move/rotate uses top-level transform without rewriting child geometry.
- [ ] Materials do not become manufacturing authority.
- [ ] Hardware asset/fallback paths preserve native entity semantics.
- [ ] Existing selection/controller resolves furniture + nested metadata.
- [ ] No managed physical board is final-rendered only as raw faces/Group wrapper.

## Negative proof required

Tests fail if:

- FI-A rebuild changes FI-B via shared mutable top-level definition;
- world coordinates are baked into part definition geometry;
- productive dimension change uses non-uniform scale;
- native SU GUID/name becomes `componentDefinitionId`, `catalogComponentId` or business identity;
- Ruby infers orientation from role/AABB.

## Likely implementation areas

- `apps/sketchup-extension/src/granete_for_sketchup/model/furniture_builder.rb`
- metadata store/writer
- asset loader integration
- builder/selection/round-trip tests

## Explicit non-goals

- Project-owned identity creation (#385/#390);
- copy/paste business lifecycle (#391);
- legacy Group migration (#416);
- OpenCutList validation (#417);
- changing material-binding semantics (#403).

## Definition of Done

Granete inserts and rebuilds furniture as an identity-safe native SketchUp ComponentInstance hierarchy, preserving #346 authoring identities while keeping native host IDs and catalog references explicitly separate.
issues.title: [P0][SU-ENT-2] Render managed furniture and board parts as native SketchUp ComponentInstances

issues.body:
## Objective

Provide an explicit compatibility path for `.skp` files created by current Granete versions where managed furniture/parts are represented as `Group`s, so the new native ComponentInstance model can be adopted without losing business identity, placement or authoring intent.

Tracks #413, #465 and #290. Coordinates with Digital Thread adoption #397.

## Hard prerequisites

- #415 — native ComponentInstance renderer available

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/sketchup-native-entity-model.md`
- ADR-0004
- `docs/architecture/project-design-digital-thread.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-plugin-excellence.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-authoring-interaction-contract.md`
- `docs/sketchup-excellence-execution-plan.md`

## Legacy reality

Current builder persists Granete metadata on:

- top-level furniture `Group`;
- nested component `Group`s;
- local faces/pushpull geometry.

Some models may carry only legacy `instanceRef`/project refs, not the future Project-owned `furnitureInstanceId` from #384.

## Required behavior

On open/validation/adoption, classify each Granete-marked entity:

```text
native_component_model
legacy_group_model
unsupported_or_corrupt
unmanaged_geometry
```

For a legacy Group with valid Granete metadata:

1. preserve the top-level world transform;
2. preserve known Granete semantic/business identity fields exactly;
3. re-resolve the current furniture definition/parameters/material choices through Granete when available;
4. create the native ComponentInstance hierarchy from authoritative resolved layout;
5. replace legacy managed geometry inside one undoable operation only after the replacement is valid;
6. retain migration provenance/schema marker;
7. never infer missing Project/Furniture business identity from geometry/name/location.

## User-facing migration workflow

Migration must be a product workflow, not only an internal adapter.

For a model containing legacy Granete entities, provide a review step conceptually equivalent to:

```text
7 muebles de una versión anterior detectados
6 listos para actualizar
1 requiere revisión

[Revisar] [Actualizar compatibles]
```

Requirements:

- user can see counts/classification before destructive conversion;
- unsupported/corrupt entries are not silently deleted;
- batch migration may process compatible items, but each replacement must validate before removing its source;
- report success/failure honestly per item;
- no model-wide “success” if one migration failed;
- migration remains undoable according to the chosen batch operation policy;
- reopening a successfully migrated model does not repeatedly prompt for the same entities.

## Relationship with #397

This issue handles **host representation migration** (`Group` -> native `ComponentInstance`).

#397 handles **business adoption** of an existing SketchUp model into a Project/Design (`Link/Create/Ignore`).

Rules:

- a legacy Granete Group with a valid Project-owned `furnitureInstanceId` can be representation-migrated without creating a new business identity;
- a legacy/local `instanceRef` that has not been reconciled with Project identity must remain compatibility metadata until #388/#397 resolves it;
- migration must not pretend a local ID is authoritative server identity.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Legacy top-level Group is detected deterministically by namespaced metadata, not by display name.
- [ ] Migration review classifies native/legacy/unsupported/unmanaged before conversion.
- [ ] Migration preserves world position/rotation and known authoring parameters/material choices.
- [ ] Valid existing business ID survives unchanged.
- [ ] Missing/foreign/duplicate business identity is surfaced for Digital Thread resolution, not guessed.
- [ ] Failure to resolve/rebuild leaves original legacy Group intact.
- [ ] Successful migration results in the exact native hierarchy expected by #415.
- [ ] Save/reopen does not re-run migration repeatedly after a successful schema upgrade.
- [ ] User can undo the migration as one coherent SketchUp operation according to the selected batch policy.
- [ ] Batch summary cannot report total success if any item remained legacy/failed.
- [ ] Real-host TestUp verifies at least one successful migration, one failure-preserves-source case and save/reopen.

## Negative proof required

Tests must fail if migration:

- creates a new FurnitureInstance merely because representation changed;
- matches identity by furniture name, dimensions or location;
- deletes the legacy Group before a replacement hierarchy is validated;
- silently treats arbitrary user Groups as managed Granete furniture;
- hides a per-item failure behind a green batch result.

## Likely implementation areas

- model scanner/metadata migration service
- `FurnitureBuilder`
- selection/model-open validation
- Ruby migration fixtures/stubs
- HtmlDialog migration review surface
- real-host TestUp fixtures

## Explicit non-goals

- general conversion of arbitrary woodworking models into Granete furniture;
- business adoption UI (owned by #397);
- copy/paste duplicate resolution (#391).

## Definition of Done

Existing Granete-generated Group models can be discovered, reviewed and migrated to the native ComponentInstance representation in a user-safe workflow without losing identity/intent, inventing Project identity or risking destructive silent conversion.
issues.title: [P1][SU-ENT-3] Migrate/adopt legacy Granete Group-based SketchUp entities safely

issues.body:
## Objective

Create a focused validation/regression slice proving that the native entity model from #413/#415 behaves correctly inside SketchUp and interoperates reasonably with common woodworking tooling such as OpenCutList without making third-party interpretation part of Granete manufacturing truth.

Tracks #413 and #290.

## Hard prerequisites

- #414 — local transform/orientation contract
- #415 — native ComponentInstance renderer

#416 is required for legacy migration scenarios but does not block validating newly created native furniture.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/sketchup-native-entity-model.md`
- ADR-0004
- `docs/verification.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`

## Why this is a separate validation issue

The architectural goal is not simply `Group -> ComponentInstance`. We need evidence that the resulting model has the expected woodworking/native-host behavior:

- parts are solid component instances;
- local axes correspond to semantic board dimensions;
- nesting is understandable in Outliner;
- selection/drill-down is predictable;
- component definition sharing does not leak edits across furniture;
- material/parameter rebuild remains valid;
- common cut-list tooling sees physical boards in a useful way.

## Canonical validation fixture

Use one cabinet containing at least:

```text
Furniture FI-A
  left side BODY
  right side BODY
  bottom BODY
  top BODY
  shelf BODY
  back BACK
  door FRONT
  drawer aggregate
    3 drawer fronts FRONT
  visible handle/hinge asset
```

Use deliberately mixed board thicknesses/materials after #402/#403 where available:

```text
BODY 16
FRONT 18
BACK 6
```

Create a second furniture FI-B from the same Granete FurnitureDefinition and change only FI-B FRONT material/dimensions to prove isolation.

## Native SketchUp checks

- top-level managed furniture is `Sketchup::ComponentInstance`;
- managed boards are nested `Sketchup::ComponentInstance`s;
- board definitions contain local solid geometry at origin;
- board instance transform places/orients them correctly;
- local axes/dimensions remain meaningful after cabinet rotate/move;
- `persistent_id`/definition GUID changes do not alter Granete business identity;
- Outliner names are useful but not authoritative;
- no non-uniform scale is used to represent manufacturing dimensions.

## Definition-sharing checks

If V1 uses unique part definitions, record that result explicitly.

If reuse exists:

- shared definitions must be immutable;
- a material/dimension rebuild must rebind/recreate rather than mutate unrelated instances;
- geometry signature behavior must be contract-tested.

## OpenCutList validation

Run/document a safe interoperability smoke against a representative supported OpenCutList version:

1. Open the generated `.skp`.
2. Generate/analyze parts without exploding Granete furniture.
3. Record whether physical board ComponentInstances are recognized as parts.
4. Record dimensions/orientation/material interpretation.
5. Record effects of nesting and any naming/tag conventions needed.
6. Document limitations explicitly.

This is **compatibility evidence only**. Granete BOM/edge/CNC/manufacturing outputs remain authoritative even if OpenCutList reports something different.

Do not add OpenCutList-specific manufacturing logic to Granete merely to make this smoke pass.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New native fixture passes all structural SketchUp checks.
- [ ] Rotated/moved furniture preserves correct local board axes.
- [ ] FI-A and FI-B remain independently rebuildable.
- [ ] Material-aware 16/18/6 fixture does not regress to group/AABB-only rendering.
- [ ] OpenCutList behavior is documented with version, expected result and known differences.
- [ ] No third-party output is used as authoritative BOM proof.
- [ ] Regression tests fail if managed physical boards revert to `Group` wrappers.
- [ ] Host smoke verifies selection + Outliner hierarchy on real SketchUp, not only Ruby stubs.

## Negative proof required

Validation must detect:

- board local axes lost because geometry is baked in world AABB coordinates;
- shared definition edit mutating another furniture;
- a managed board represented only as Group/raw faces;
- OpenCutList compatibility code contaminating domain/manufacturing rules.

## Relationship with existing test programs

- #405 owns material-thickness/role parity TS↔Go↔SketchUp.
- #398 owns Project Digital Thread end-to-end identity/revision behavior.
- #354 owns manufacturing output goldens.

This issue owns **SketchUp native host representation/interoperability** and should contribute fixtures/assertions to those suites rather than duplicate their domain responsibilities.

## Definition of Done

We have real SketchUp-host evidence that Granete's native hierarchy is structurally correct, identity-safe and useful to woodworking tooling, with limitations documented and manufacturing authority boundaries preserved.
issues.title: [P1][SU-ENT-4] Verify native SketchUp hierarchy, local axes and OpenCutList interoperability

issues.body:
## Objective

Document the canonical native SketchUp entity model for Granete before implementation, reconciling the current Group-based renderer, semantic metadata contract, material-aware rebuild plan and Project Digital Thread.

Tracks #413 and #290.

## Required scope

- Add `docs/architecture/sketchup-native-entity-model.md` as canonical authority.
- Add ADR-0004 recording why managed furniture and physical board parts use native `Sketchup::ComponentInstance`s.
- Correct `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`, which currently describes an aspirational 3-level Group hierarchy while runtime actually uses Groups and raw box geometry.
- Clarify `docs/sketchup-manufacturing-contract.md` so Granete `componentDefinitionId` is never confused with SketchUp `ComponentDefinition` GUID/identity.
- Link/align `docs/architecture/domain-model.md` and material-aware resolution docs.
- Define local axes, local geometry vs world transform, definition lifecycle, copy/duplicate safety, rebuild/atomicity, subassembly rules, hardware rules, legacy migration and third-party interoperability boundary.
- Record cross-issue dependencies with #384, #389–#398 and #401–#405.

## Canonical decisions to capture

1. Top-level managed furniture -> native `Sketchup::ComponentInstance`.
2. Physical board part -> nested native `Sketchup::ComponentInstance`.
3. Optional subassembly level only for real semantic aggregate/assembly identity.
4. V1 top-level SketchUp definition is unique per FurnitureInstance.
5. Part definitions may be unique initially; reuse only via immutable geometry-signature definitions.
6. Business IDs remain Granete-owned metadata; SketchUp GUID/entityID/persistent_id are technical locators.
7. Board definition geometry is local at origin; server provides authoritative placement/orientation.
8. Ruby never infers part orientation from role/AABB and never calculates manufacturing thickness.
9. #404 material rebuild targets the native hierarchy and must not be implemented as a final Group-only rebuild.
10. Legacy Groups require explicit representation migration; arbitrary user geometry remains unmanaged.
11. OpenCutList compatibility is verified, not authoritative.

## Verification

- Documentation-only PR.
- Structural readback of all modified Markdown.
- Links/issue references valid.
- No Ruby/Go/TS/React production code in this PR.

## Definition of Done

The architecture can be implemented by #414–#417 without unresolved decisions about host entity type, identity ownership, definition sharing, local axes, rebuild semantics or migration.

## Missing isolation tests

The following entity families have org-scoped storage methods but **no cross-org isolation test**:

| Family | Storage file | Key methods |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| Stock | `stock.go` | ListStock, UpsertStockMin, StockMovementCreate |
| Purchase Orders | `purchaseOrders.go` | ListPurchaseOrders, CreatePO, EmitPO |
| Quality | `quality.go` | MutateProjectQuality |
| Installation | `installation.go` | MutateProjectInstallation |
| Warranties | `warranties.go` | ListWarrantyTickets, CreateWarrantyTicket |
| Photos | `photos.go` | ListProjectPhotos, CreateProjectPhoto, ListShowcasePhotos |
| Internal Messages | `internal_messages.go` | ListProjectInternalMessages |
| Project Events | `projects.go` | ListProjectEvents, InsertProjectEvent |
| Part Executions | `partExecutions.go` | MutateProjectPartExecutions |
| Material Planning | `materialPlanning.go` | MutateProjectMaterialPlanning |
| Site Survey | `siteSurvey.go` | MutateProjectSiteSurvey |
| Project Picking | `projectPicking.go` | ListPicking |

| Ambient Materials | `ambient.go` | ListAmbientMaterials, CreateAmbientMaterial |
| Ambient Categories | `ambient.go` | ListAmbientCategories |

## Requirements

For each family, the test should verify:

1. **List** scoped to Org A returns only Org A rows
2. **List** scoped to Org B returns only Org B rows
3. **Get by ID** of Org A's row from Org B context returns not-found (same error as missing row, no existence leak)
4. **Write** from Org B targeting Org A's row fails without side effects

Use the existing `isolationSetup` / `scoped` helpers from `multi_org_isolation_test.go`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] All 15 families have at least one isolation test

## Context

Media uploads are partitioned by organization: `MEDIA_DIR/<org_id>/<filename>`. The `HandleMediaGet` handler resolves the file path from the JWT's org scope, so Org B cannot read Org A's files. However, there is no integration test that proves this at the storage/handler level.

## What to verify

### 1. Filesystem partitioning
- Upload a file as Org A → verify it lands in `MEDIA_DIR/<orgA>/`
- Upload a file as Org B → verify it lands in `MEDIA_DIR/<orgB>/`
- Org A's directory must not contain Org B's file and vice versa

### 2. Handler isolation
- GET `/api/media/<filename>` as Org A → should serve Org A's file
- GET `/api/media/<filename>` as Org B with Org A's filename → should return 404
- The filename must be resolved server-side from JWT scope, not from user input

### 3. Path escape prevention
- Upload with `../` in filename → should be rejected (400)
- GET with `../` in name → should be rejected (400)
- GET with `/` in name → should be rejected (400)

## Test location

`backend-go/internal/api/media_test.go` — add handler-level tests alongside existing media tests, or create `backend-go/internal/storage/media_isolation_test.go` for filesystem-level tests.

## Implementation notes

- The test needs a temp directory for `MediaDir` (use `t.TempDir()`)
- Mock the JWT claims with the correct org scope
- Use the `scoped` helper pattern from `multi_org_isolation_test.go`

## Acceptance

- [ ] Org A cannot read Org B's uploaded files
- [ ] Org B cannot read Org A's uploaded files
- [ ] Path traversal attempts are rejected
- [ ] `go test ./internal/api/ -run TestMedia` passes

**Tracking:** Pilot Readiness Gate audit (2026-08-26)

issues.body:
## Hallazgo (detectado durante #415)

Al expandir componentes resueltos, el instance id se genera por ENTRADA de `ComponentInstance`, no globalmente por componente:

```go
// backend-go/internal/domain/engine/layout.go (expandLayoutInstances)
id = fmt.Sprintf("%s%s-copy-%d", idPrefix, comp.ID, i)
```

Si una estructura/agregado contiene **dos entradas distintas** apuntando al mismo `ComponentID` (p.ej. `{comp-side, qty 1}` dos veces), ambas emiten `st-comp-side-copy-0` → `componentInstanceId` duplicado en el layout resuelto.

Paridad: el engine TS (`packages/domain/src/engine/bom.ts:498`, `${idPrefix}${component.id}-copy-${i}`) tiene el mismo comportamiento — limitación compartida, no divergencia Go↔TS.

## Impacto

- El renderer nativo de SketchUp (#415) ata metadata por `componentInstanceId`: ids duplicados colisionarían (la última escritura gana) y los hosts de herrajes (`hostComponentInstanceId`) serían ambiguos.
- No reproducible desde el autoring actual si la UI no permite duplicar entradas del mismo componente en una estructura (verificar).

## Propuesta

- Numerar copies globalmente por (prefix, componentID) dentro de la resolución, o
- rechazar/validar entradas duplicadas del mismo componente en `ValidateModule`.

Mantener paridad TS↔Go en el fix + contract fixture.

## Referencias

- Detectado en #415 (`TestLayoutComponentDefinitionIdentity` usó quantity=3 para esquivarlo); anotado en `progress/current.md` (F186).

Tests de paridad en ambos engines.

issues.body:
## Problem

The web app keeps a whole catalog snapshot per tab and catalog mutations can re-save that snapshot. The BroadcastChannel mitigation from #441 reduces the stale window, but it cannot prevent lost updates:

1. tab A edits entity X;
2. tab B still has an older snapshot;
3. tab B edits entity Y;
4. a whole-catalog save can overwrite A's newer X.

Visible side-by-side tabs and offline/retry windows remain vulnerable.

## Required outcome

Replace whole-catalog fan-out with server-authoritative per-entity persistence and optimistic concurrency.

Suggested contract:

- entity-specific POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE endpoints;
- `updated_at` or explicit version/ETag on mutable entities;
- `If-Match` on writes;
- HTTP 409 or 412 on stale writes with an actionable conflict payload;
- client reconciliation that reloads the affected entity and never silently overwrites;
- BroadcastChannel remains only a freshness hint, not a correctness mechanism.

## Coordination with Organization Foundation v2

Tracks the catalog-local persistence concern only.

- #448 is the mandatory shared authority for generated OpenAPI, typed error envelopes, ETag/`If-Match`, `Idempotency-Key` and request IDs. This issue must consume that contract rather than define a catalog-only variant.
- #454 owns cross-organization `CatalogPublication`, store subscriptions, immutable versions and overlays. This issue must not absorb publishing/network scope.
- Every query/mutation/cache key remains scoped by `organizationId`; ownership and RLS from #449 stay server-enforced.
- BroadcastChannel may trigger refetch/invalidation, but correctness comes from server versioning.

Hard prerequisite for implementation: #448 contract merged. #449 must be integrated before declaring multi-organization write paths complete.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Editing different entities in two tabs never reverts either change.
- [ ] Editing the same entity from a stale tab fails explicitly.
- [ ] Retry/offline paths are idempotent where applicable.
- [ ] Tests cover two clients, stale version, delete/update conflict and network retry.
- [ ] No whole-catalog mutation remains on normal web write paths.
- [ ] Multi-organization ownership and authorization stay server-enforced.
- [ ] Generated client/error/version contract from #448 is used; no manual response shape or string-matched conflict handling.
- [ ] CatalogPublication/subscription remains outside this issue and is consumed through #454.

## Context

Full solution deferred from #441; the current BroadcastChannel refresh is a bounded demo mitigation only.

This issue is coordinated by #446 but remains an independent catalog persistence slice.

issues.body:
# Organization Foundation v2 — Usuarios, Multi-Taller y Red de Ventas

## Objetivo

Cerrar de forma definitiva la base de identidad, autorización, aislamiento y colaboración entre organizaciones antes de continuar ampliando funciones de negocio.

Este programa convierte el MVP multi-organización de #325–#327 en una plataforma operable y segura para:

- usuarios que pertenecen a uno o varios talleres;
- membresías con roles múltiples y lifecycle explícito;
- fábricas, tiendas y distribuidores aislados;
- redes comerciales autorizadas por relaciones entre organizaciones;
- transferencia tienda → fábrica sin exigir que el vendedor pertenezca a la fábrica;
- soporte de plataforma auditado;
- UI React que nunca oculte errores mediante fallbacks ni muestre éxito antes de que el servidor confirme.

## Por qué es P0 ahora

La implementación actual tiene una base correcta (`User → Membership → Organization`, JWT scoped, aislamiento cross-org y support sessions), pero conserva caminos heredados single-workshop y estados parciales que hacen inseguro seguir agregando entidades y workflows:

- `/api/org/*` y `/api/admin/users/*` conviven en la misma pantalla;
- registro/aprobación global no tiene semántica correcta por organización;
- una membresía suspendida desaparece de la lista y no puede reactivarse desde UI;
- no existe garantía transaccional de último administrador;
- crear una tienda puede responder 201 aunque fallen catálogo o membresía bootstrap;
- `parent_organization_id` no expresa una relación comercial completa;
- un vendedor de tienda necesita hoy membresía en la fábrica para asignarla como fabricante;
- el frontend usa contratos manuales/casts que ya divergen de DTOs Go;
- el aislamiento depende de Go + tests, sin RLS de PostgreSQL como segunda barrera.

## Baseline existente — no reabrir ni duplicar

Se conservan como trabajo completado y fundamento histórico:

- #325 — modelo multi-organización;
- #326 — administración inicial de tiendas/equipos;
- #327 — ownership comercial/manufacturero y redacción de datos;
- #421/#422 y F179/F182 — aislamiento y Pilot Readiness;
- #303 — InstallationJob/visits/Field Issues/Punch/Closeout;
- PRs #419, #424, #427 y #429.

El programa no declara que ese trabajo “no sirvió”; lo endurece y reemplaza los bridges heredados con contratos definitivos.

## Resultado de reconciliación del backlog

- No se encontró una issue abierta que implemente RLS, last-admin, membership lifecycle, provisioning atómico u OrganizationRelationship; no hay duplicados abiertos que cerrar.
- #443 fue adaptada y queda **catalog-local**: per-entity writes/concurrency; consume #448/#449 y no absorbe CatalogPublication.
- #384 conserva la autoridad del Digital Thread. Se añadió coordinación y #385 ahora exige Foundation Gate A antes de crear schema.
- #303 permanece cerrada; #457 sólo añade ownership/asignación cross-org al workflow existente.
- #306 continúa como validación humana de piloto; #462 añade el gate técnico y no la sustituye.
- #290/#308 continúan como programas de SketchUp/Proyectar y no desplazan este P0.

## Invariantes no negociables

1. `User` es identidad global; no es fábrica, tienda ni puesto.
2. El acceso a una organización existe únicamente mediante una `Membership` activa.
3. Roles y sectores pertenecen a la membresía, nunca al usuario global.
4. `users.active` describe la cuenta global; el lifecycle del taller vive en `Membership.status`.
5. Onboarding B2B es invitation-first. Un admin de taller no aprueba/elimina identidades globales arbitrarias.
6. Toda organización activa conserva al menos un admin activo; el gate es transaccional y race-safe.
7. Cross-org devuelve 404 indistinguible de inexistente y PostgreSQL RLS refuerza el scope de Go.
8. El usuario DB de la app no usa `BYPASSRLS`.
9. Crear organización/partner es atómico desde el punto de vista de negocio: nunca 201 “activo” con pasos fallidos.
10. La autorización tienda↔fábrica proviene de `OrganizationRelationship`, no de que cada vendedor tenga membresía en ambas.
11. `parent_organization_id` queda como compatibilidad/migración, no como autoridad final de red.
12. Acciones sensibles usan commands explícitos, auditoría durable, idempotency y optimistic concurrency.
13. OpenAPI/DTOs generados son el contrato entre Go y React; prohibidos casts ciegos de `res.json()` en estas superficies.
14. Toda caché/server state se keyea por `organizationId`; cambiar taller no puede mostrar ni mutar datos del anterior.
15. No hay fallbacks silenciosos entre API nueva y legacy.
16. Variables, tipos, funciones y APIs técnicas en inglés; copy UI en español.

## Child issues

|---:|---:|---|---|
| 0 | #447 | Documento canónico + ADR-0006 + reconciliación | — |
| 1 | #448 | OpenAPI generado, typed errors, versioning/idempotency | #447 |

15. Completar #460/#461 y ejecutar **Gate B** de #462.

### Trabajo paralelo permitido

- #443 puede implementarse después de #448 y coordinarse con #449; no necesita esperar todo el Network Gate.
- Digital Thread discovery puede continuar; schema/API espera Gate A.
- UI component/design discovery puede avanzar sin conectar mocks como “done”.
- No se permite implementar #456 saltando relationship/catalog/price/identity pins.

## Gates del programa

### Gate A — Foundation

Debe cerrar antes de implementar nuevas familias persistentes de negocio, incluyendo DT-1 #385:

- contrato canónico + ADR;
- OpenAPI/typed error contract;
- RLS + tenant transaction context;
- lifecycle definitivo de Membership/Invitation;
- administración segura del equipo;
- lifecycle y provisioning atómico de Organization;
- eliminación de rutas/fallbacks legacy;
- sesiones críticas/audit durable;
- E2E del gate sobre PostgreSQL real + browser.

Discovery/documentación de otros programas puede continuar; implementación persistente debe esperar el gate.

### Gate B — Sales Network

Debe cerrar antes de declarar operable la Red de Ventas:

- `OrganizationRelationship`;
- catálogo/publicación autorizada para partners;
- wholesale/retail policy;
- transferencia comercial tienda→fábrica;
- visibilidad comercial vs manufacturera;
- instalación asignable a fábrica, tienda o partner;
- E2E store seller → factory → installation.

## Relación con issues abiertas

- #443 se conserva **catalog-only** y ya fue adaptada para consumir #448/#449; no absorbe Membership/Organization ni Publication.
- #384 se conserva como autoridad de FurnitureInstance/QuoteRevision/DesignRevision/ProductionRelease; #385 fue adaptada al Gate A. #456 consume sus identidades/revisiones exactas.
- #306 sigue siendo validación de campo. #462 es requisito técnico previo al piloto, no reemplaza evidencia humana.
- #290/#308 continúan como programas paralelos de authoring/UX, sin desplazar este foundation gate.

## Escenario E2E global obligatorio

```text
Platform admin crea Factory A
→ provisioning completo y admin bootstrap
→ Factory A crea relación con Store B
→ Store B queda activa con catálogo/política autorizada
→ Store admin invita Seller S
→ S acepta y entra directamente a Store B
→ S crea QuoteRevision sin membresía en Factory A
→ relación activa resuelve Factory A como fabricante
→ cotización se envía mediante command idempotente
→ Factory A recibe ManufacturingOrder exacta
→ Store B sólo ve estado comercial, nunca BOM/costos/CNC internos
→ factory clarifica/acepta/programa
→ instalación se asigna a una organización autorizada
→ visitas/issues/punch reutilizan #303
→ cierre queda auditado
→ suspender la relación bloquea nuevas órdenes sin borrar historia
```

Además:

- dos admins concurrentes no pueden dejar la organización sin admin;
- una falla durante provisioning no deja organización activa parcial;
- un actor de Org A no lee/escribe Org B ni por API ni por SQL bajo el rol de aplicación;
- cambio de taller en dos tabs no mezcla caché ni token;
- DTO Go y cliente TS se generan del mismo contrato;
- retirar un miembro revoca su acceso al taller sin afectar otras membresías;
- catálogo/precios nuevos no alteran quotes/orders pinneadas;
- support/platform nunca bypassan business scope.

## Global Definition of Done

- documento canónico y ADR merged;
- child issues cerradas según dependency graph;
- bridges `/api/admin/users/*` retirados del flujo de taller y sin callers;
- registration/approval legacy reemplazado por invitation-first;
- último admin, offboarding, seats y sesiones probados;
- RLS habilitado y forzado para tablas tenant;
- provisioning y relación comercial transaccionales/idempotentes;
- vendedor de tienda puede enviar a fábrica autorizada sin membresía en ella;
- React usa cliente generado, server state scoped y rollback/honest success;
- auditoría durable y legible;
- E2E real Go + PostgreSQL + navegador requerido en CI/pilot gate;
- documentación, código, migrations, issues y feature ledger quedan coherentes;
- no queda fallback temporal “después lo quitamos”.

## Reglas para agentes

- Leer el documento canónico y ADR antes de cualquier child issue.
- No iniciar una issue dependiente antes del hard prerequisite salvo discovery.
- Cada PR enumera invariantes tocados, migración, rollback y negative proof.
- Toda mutación sensible prueba happy path, denial, cross-org, stale version, retry e invariantes transaccionales.
- No cerrar por implementación parcial o UI aislada.
- No ampliar #443 o #384 para esconder trabajo de este programa.
- Una sola feature `in_progress` en el ledger salvo coordinación explícita del programa.
- Gate A y Gate B son criterios ejecutables; no se sustituyen por review visual o checklist manual.

issues.body:
## Objetivo

Convertir el aislamiento multi-organización de Granete en una garantía de aplicación **y de base de datos**, mediante contexto tenant por transacción, PostgreSQL Row-Level Security y eliminación del fallback runtime a la organización inicial.

Tracks #446.

## Hard prerequisites

- #447 — contrato canónico/ADR-0006.
- #448 — error/request contract disponible para exponer fallos de scope de forma consistente.

## Baseline que se conserva

- JWT con `org_id` y roles de membresía;
- revalidación live de usuario/membresía/organización;
- storage scoped y 404 cross-org;
- suites F179/F182 y #421/#422.

RLS no reemplaza esas defensas: evita que un nuevo query, upsert o code path Go pueda cruzar tenants por omisión.

## Alcance requerido

### Inventario y clasificación

Clasificar todas las tablas como:

1. **tenant-owned** — una organización propietaria;
2. **dual/multi-org shared** — por ejemplo recursos comerciales/manufacturer visibles para organizaciones explícitas;
3. **platform-global** — identities, organizations, support/audit metadata según contrato;
4. **append-only operational** — eventos/ledger con policy específica.

No aplicar una policy genérica incorrecta a proyectos compartidos. La matriz debe expresar lectura, escritura y ownership por tipo de tabla.

### Contexto por transacción

Introducir un runner/repositorio tenant-aware que en toda transacción de negocio establezca, como mínimo:

```sql
SET LOCAL app.organization_id = '...';
SET LOCAL app.user_id = '...';
SET LOCAL app.support_session_id = '...';
```

- El valor proviene de claims revalidados, nunca del body.
- El pool no puede filtrar contexto entre requests.
- Commands que toquen varias organizaciones usan un contexto explícito/autorizado del application service; no desactivan RLS globalmente.
- CLI, migrations, seed y tests deben declarar su modo de acceso de forma explícita.

### Policies

- `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` y `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` donde corresponda.
- Policies `USING` + `WITH CHECK` para reads/writes.
- Rol PostgreSQL de aplicación sin ownership de tablas y sin `BYPASSRLS`.
- Rol de migración separado.
- Acceso platform/support modelado; un `platform_admin` normal no obtiene business data.
- Soporte scoped hereda sólo la organización de la sesión auditada.

### Eliminar fallback runtime

- `OrgFromCtx` no debe devolver `InitialOrganizationID` para paths normales.
- Writes sin scope fallan loud.
- Tooling legacy debe pasar scope explícito o usar un puerto administrativo claramente separado.
- Añadir guard de arquitectura que impida nuevos usos de fallback en código productivo.

### Tests

- SQL directo bajo el rol de aplicación.
- A→B y B→A read/write/delete/upsert.
- shared-resource policy.
- support session.
- platform admin org-less.
- pool reuse/context leakage.
- transaction rollback.
- malicious body con `organization_id` ajeno.
- inventario que falle si se agrega tabla tenant sin policy.

### Operación

- Migración staged y reversible.
- Readiness check confirma policies/roles esperados.
- Runbook para diagnose policy denial sin exponer existencia.
- Métrica de RLS denials/violations sin datos sensibles.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Toda tabla de negocio está clasificada y cubierta por policy o excepción justificada.
- [ ] El usuario DB de runtime no tiene `BYPASSRLS` ni table ownership que anule FORCE RLS.
- [ ] Un query Go sin filtro tenant sigue sin poder leer/escribir otra organización.
- [ ] Pool reuse no hereda organization context previo.
- [ ] Shared sales/manufacturing rows respetan exactamente la matriz autorizada.
- [ ] Platform admin sin support session no accede a business data.
- [ ] No existe fallback runtime a InitialOrganizationID.
- [ ] Pilot readiness ejecuta assertions API + SQL/RLS.
- [ ] Nuevas migrations/tablas tenant fallan CI si no registran policy.
- [ ] Performance de queries críticas se mide antes/después; índices soportan las policies.

## Negative proof

Tests deben demostrar que:

- eliminar accidentalmente `WHERE organization_id = ...` en un repository no produce fuga;
- un `ON CONFLICT` con key conocida de otro tenant no muta la víctima;
- `SET` fuera de transacción no contamina la siguiente conexión/request;
- support token de Org A no alcanza Org B;
- un rol de aplicación no puede ejecutar `SET row_security = off` ni bypass equivalente.

## Fuera de alcance

- DB/schema separado por organización;
- cambiar la decisión de tenancy row-level de ADR-0005;
- modelar todavía todo el workflow tienda→fábrica (#453+);
- ocultar errores de policy mediante fallback a otra organización.

## Definition of Done

Aislamiento Go + PostgreSQL está activo en producción/pilot, toda tabla tenant tiene cobertura verificable, no existe fallback runtime y el gate de CI impide regresar a una protección basada sólo en disciplina de queries.
