issues.body:
## Objetivo

Endurecer la autenticación de Granete para multi-taller y soporte sin convertir la sesión finita de trabajo en una sesión renovable indefinidamente, eliminando JWTs web expuestos en storage/URLs y añadiendo revocación/MFA real para acciones sensibles.

Tracks #446.

## Hard prerequisites

- #448 — auth/session contracts y typed errors.
- #450 — identity/membership lifecycle.
- #451 — membership session revocation.
- #452 — organization lifecycle/session cut.
- #458 — session/org switch UX preparada para el contrato nuevo.

## Decisión de sesión vigente que debe preservarse

#441/#445 fijaron una jornada finita de **18 horas** y rechazaron un refresh sliding que convirtiera la sesión en indefinida.

Cualquier arquitectura nueva debe mantener:

```text
absoluteSessionExpiresAt = issuedAt + 18h
```

Un refresh/rotation técnico puede existir para reducir exposición del access token, pero **nunca extiende** el absolute lifetime. Al llegar al límite, re-login/step-up obligatorio.

## Problemas actuales

- Web persiste bearer JWT en `localStorage`; XSS puede extraerlo.
- Access token largo amplía impacto de robo aunque la revalidación DB ayude.
- `/auth/refresh` histórico dependía de token aún válido y no era un session protocol completo.
- AuthMiddleware acepta `?token=` de forma genérica para media; URLs pueden terminar en logs/history/referrer.
- JWT validation no expresa aún todo el contract de issuer/audience/key rotation/session id.
- Rate limit es in-memory por IP y confía en forwarded headers sin trusted-proxy policy explícita.
- No hay MFA/step-up para platform admin, admins de organización o soporte.
- No hay directorio/revocación de sesiones/dispositivos por membership.

## Session model requerido

### Server-side Session

```text
id
user_id
membership_id / active_org_id
client_type = web | mobile | sketchup | support
created_at
absolute_expires_at
last_seen_at
revoked_at/by/reason
device/session metadata sanitizada
refresh_family_id/rotation state cuando aplique
```

- La membership activa se revalida en cada request sensible como hoy.
- Suspender membership/org o revocar session corta acceso inmediatamente.
- Cambiar org emite/switches una session scope según contrato; no reutiliza roles del org anterior.

### Web credentials

Target preferido, sujeto al ADR/verification de esta issue:

- access token corto en memoria;
- refresh credential rotatoria en cookie `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite`;
- absolute 18h no sliding;
- CSRF defense para endpoints cookie-authenticated;
- refresh reuse detection revoca family;
- logout revoca server session y borra cookie;
- tabs coordinan session state sin copiar business data cross-org.

Si se elige otra implementación, debe ofrecer protección equivalente y documentar por qué.

### Mobile

- refresh/session secret en secure storage;
- access token corto en memoria;
- misma absolute lifetime/policy o una policy mobile explícita y auditada.

### SketchUp

- device/session credential least-privilege;
- capabilities explícitas, no “GET means safe” como único control;
- long-lived sólo con device registration/revocation y scope mínimo;
- no usar credential web.

### Support

- support session sigue separada, scoped, reason-required y time-boxed;
- MFA/step-up obligatorio para abrirla;
- read-only por default y elevación de write scope cuando el producto lo permita;
- actor real/banner/audit siempre presentes;
- org suspension/logout/expiry la cortan.

## MFA y step-up

Obligatorio para:

- platform admin;
- organization admin, al menos para transferencia de admin, cambios críticos y session revocation masiva;
- iniciar soporte;
- cambios de licencia/entitlements;
- exportaciones masivas/operaciones definidas por policy.

Soportar:

- WebAuthn/passkeys como target fuerte;
- TOTP como primer mecanismo/fallback;
- recovery codes almacenados con hash;
- MFA enrollment/recovery auditado;
- step-up timestamp/capability, no booleano cliente.

## JWT/token hardening

- Algoritmo exacto permitido, no cualquier HMAC compatible.
- `iss`, `aud`, `sub`, `exp`, `nbf`, `iat`, `jti/session_id`, token version.
- Key rotation con `kid` y runbook.
- Secrets fuera de repo, rotation/revocation probada.
- Token types no intercambiables entre web/mobile/SketchUp/support.
- Mensajes de error no revelan parser/identity state.

## Media authorization

Retirar bearer JWT genérico en query string.

Opciones permitidas:

- signed media URL corta y resource-scoped;
- fetch autenticado + Blob URL;
- object storage signed URL;
- media token específico, single-resource/short TTL.

Requisitos:

- org/resource authorization antes de firmar;
- no token de sesión en logs/referrer;
- revocación/expiry;
- cache headers correctos;
- cross-org 404.

## Rate limiting/trusted proxy

- Configurar lista explícita de trusted proxies; ignorar spoofed forwarding headers fuera de ella.
- Límites distribuidos/persistentes cuando haya varias instancias.
- Keys combinadas según endpoint: IP, normalized email, session/user/org, invitation token fingerprint.
- Backoff y `Retry-After` correcto.
- Límites para login, invitation accept/resend, support start, org provisioning, exports.
- Métricas/alertas de credential stuffing sin registrar secretos.

## Password/account recovery

- Reconciliar policy con invitation-first.
- Preferir passphrases ≥12 para nuevas credentials, con breach check cuando sea viable.
- Reset tokens hash/TTL/single-use.
- Email verification/recovery flow sin enumeración.
- Cambios críticos notifican al usuario/admin correspondiente.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Web ya no almacena bearer session token de larga vida en localStorage.
- [ ] La sesión nunca supera 18h por refresh/replay; test de reloj lo demuestra.
- [ ] Rotation/reuse/logout/revocation se prueban server-side.
- [ ] Suspender membership/org corta todas sus sessions sin afectar otras memberships.
- [ ] MFA/step-up protege platform/support/admin-sensitive commands.
- [ ] JWT valida algoritmo exacto, issuer, audience, version y session id.
- [ ] Key rotation tiene test/runbook sin downtime indebido.
- [ ] Media no acepta JWT genérico por query y sigue funcionando en React/SketchUp según cliente.
- [ ] Trusted proxy/rate limiting resiste spoof/restart/multi-instance según deployment target.
- [ ] CSRF/XSS/cookie implications están documentadas y testeadas.
- [ ] UI muestra expiry/revoked/step-up de forma clara sin loops.

## Negative proof

- Refresh al minuto 17:59 no extiende la session más allá de issuedAt+18h.
- Refresh token replay revoca la family.
- JWT web presentado como SketchUp/support es rechazado.
- `?token=<sessionJWT>` no autentica media/business routes.
- X-Forwarded-For enviado directamente por cliente no evade rate limit.
- Platform admin sin MFA reciente no abre support session.
- Membership suspendida en Store A no revoca session válida de Factory B del mismo User.

## Fuera de alcance

- SSO/SAML empresarial;
- billing;
- passwordless-only obligatorio para todos desde el primer release;
- cambiar el límite de 18h sin nueva decisión explícita.

## Definition of Done

Granete tiene sessions server-side revocables y bounded, credenciales separadas por cliente, MFA/step-up para superficies privilegiadas, media resource-scoped y un auth gate verificable que conserva la jornada finita decidida en #441.

comments.body:
## SketchUp client and pairing coordination — 2026-08-30

The final session/security design must explicitly support the new cross-product owners:

- #496 generated client/capability/version contract;
- #499 short-lived one-time Web→SketchUp Project/Design pairing;
- #504 local privacy-safe diagnostics;
- #503 resource-scoped manufacturing artifact access where authorized.

### Pairing rule

#499 may use an opaque launch/pairing grant, but it is **not** a reusable web or SketchUp session credential. Required properties:

```text
one-time
short TTL
exact organization/Project/Design/action scope
rate limited
revocable/audited
exchanged through the dedicated SketchUp client boundary
raw code never logged
```

No web JWT/access token/refresh token/device credential may appear in a custom URI or query string.

### Session/query integration

The server session model should expose a non-secret stable session identity or credential generation through the generated DTO so React query roots can distinguish logout→relogin of the same user/org without including a token in cache keys. This directly supports #458/#494 and later #499–#503.

### Diagnostics

#504 can export local environment/correlation evidence while offline/unauthenticated, but must never include session secrets, cookies, pairing grants, signed URLs or private model data.

These requirements extend #460's existing client separation; they do not create another session model.

issues.title: [P0][SEC-ORG] Bounded web sessions, MFA, media authorization and auth hardening

issues.body:
## Objetivo

Hacer que los cambios de identidad, membresía, organización y red comercial sean auditables de forma durable y operables mediante logs, métricas, trazas, readiness y una timeline humana; ningún evento crítico puede perderse porque el audit actual sea best-effort.

Tracks #446.

## Hard prerequisites

- #448 — request/error contracts (`requestId`).
- #449 — transaction/RLS context.

Puede implementarse incrementalmente en paralelo, pero cada child issue sensible de #446 debe consumir el mecanismo antes de cerrarse.

## Problemas actuales

- `audit()` intenta insertar y, si falla, sólo hace `slog.Warn`; la mutación de negocio puede completar sin evidencia de seguridad.
- Audit DTO/backend/UI divergen (`ip/details` vs `ip_address/metadata`).
- Plataforma muestra UUIDs/event types/JSON crudo como experiencia primaria.
- Listados carecen de paginación/filtros robustos.
- `/api/health` puede responder OK sin probar PostgreSQL/migrations/outbox/media.
- Falta correlación request→actor→org→relationship→resource.
- No existe tracing end-to-end ni métricas específicas de organization foundation.

## Transactional audit/outbox

Para mutaciones críticas:

```text
BEGIN
business mutation
audit record / outbox event
COMMIT
```

- La mutación y la evidencia se confirman juntas.
- Publicación/projection externa es at-least-once e idempotente.
- Outbox tiene retries/backoff/dead-letter/visibility.
- Failure de serializer no descarta el evento; usa schema validado antes de commit.
- No usar best-effort para roles, memberships, sessions, licenses, organizations, relationships, catalog publications, price policies u orders.

Telemetría no crítica puede seguir best-effort; security/business audit no.

## Audit schema

Campos mínimos estructurados:

```text
id
event_type/schema_version
occurred_at
actor_user_id
actor_membership_id
actor_organization_id
target_user_id / target_membership_id
target_organization_id
relationship_id
resource_type/resource_id
request_id/trace_id
support_session_id
ip/user_agent sanitizados
reason_code/reason
before/after o structured changes redacted
details
```

Reglas:

- append-only;
- no passwords, JWTs, raw invitation tokens, refresh secrets ni payloads completos de cliente;
- before/after allowlist por event type;
- actor real preservado en soporte;
- retention/export policy explícita;
- timestamp DB/server authoritative.

## Event vocabulary

Mínimo para #446:

- login/session/MFA/support lifecycle;
- invitation lifecycle;
- membership role/status/sector/offboarding/admin transfer;
- organization provision/lifecycle/license/entitlements;
- relationship lifecycle/policy/capability/terms;
- catalog publication/subscription/apply;
- price book/policy/discount approval;
- quote submission/manufacturing order decisions;
- installation assignment/reassignment/data grant;
- RLS/authorization denial agregado, sin confirmar resource existence.

No mezclar audit de seguridad con `project_events`, stock/floor ledgers; pueden correlacionarse por IDs.

## Human-readable audit API/UI

Backend devuelve read model tipado:

```text
Tiago Furtado cambió los roles de Ana López
Vendedor → Gerente de ventas
Organización: Tienda Monterrey
Motivo: Promoción
Fecha / IP / Request
```

- Label/copy se deriva de event schema conocido, no de parsear JSON arbitrario en React.
- Fallback seguro para versiones desconocidas.
- Filters: date, actor, target, event family, org, relationship, resource, support session.
- Pagination cursor-based.
- Detail drawer con changes y correlation IDs.
- Export CSV/JSON sanitizado y autorizado.
- Platform ve audit global metadata; business details sólo según support/scope.
- Organization admins ven su audit permitido, no platform-only secrets.

## Logs/traces

Toda request incluye:

```text
request_id
trace_id
user_id
membership_id
organization_id
support_session_id
relationship_id cuando aplique
route/method/status/duration_ms
error_code
```

- OpenTelemetry o equivalente para React/API/PostgreSQL/outbox.
- Sampling/PII policy.
- Slow query spans.
- Propagation desde cliente generado.
- No registrar Authorization/cookies/tokens/passwords.

## Metrics/SLOs

### Security

- login fail/rate limited;
- invalid/revoked sessions;
- cross-org/RLS denials;
- MFA/support starts;
- last-admin blocks;
- invitation failures/replays.

### Product foundation

- invitation created/accepted/time-to-accept;
- active/suspended memberships;
- provisioning duration/failures por step;
- active/suspended relationships;
- catalog sync status;
- quote submissions/review time/clarifications;
- action-required orders;
- installation assignments/issues.

### Infrastructure

- p50/p95/p99 route latency;
- DB pool/waits/slow queries;
- outbox lag/retries/dead letters;
- media/storage failures;
- readiness/migration drift;
- backup/pilot gate result.

No inventar KPIs; aplicar Data Truth Contract.

## Health/readiness

Separar:

```text
/api/health/live
/api/health/ready
```

`ready` verifica, según deployment:

- PostgreSQL connection;
- expected migration version;
- RLS policy inventory;
- app DB role properties;
- outbox consumer/lag threshold;
- media/object storage write/read check controlado;
- required secrets/config;
- provisioning subsystem.

No exponer detalles sensibles públicamente; logs internos conservan causa.

## Alerting/runbooks

Alertas mínimas:

- repeated cross-org/RLS denial anomaly;
- provisioning_failed;
- outbox dead letter/lag;
- audit insert failure/constraint;
- support session anomaly;
- DB/readiness failure;
- invitation/login abuse;
- backup/pilot readiness failure.

Runbooks enlazan event/error codes y rollback/repair steps.

## CI/security supply chain

Añadir gates apropiados:

- `govulncheck`;
- `gosec` o revisión equivalente;
- CodeQL;
- dependency/OSV review;
- container/image scan;
- secret scanning;
- SBOM/artifact provenance cuando el deployment lo soporte.

Definir qué hallazgos bloquean merge/release.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mutación crítica y audit/outbox son atómicas.
- [ ] Worker reintenta sin duplicar projections/actions.
- [ ] Audit schema no serializa secretos y tiene tests por allowlist.
- [ ] Platform/Organization audit renderiza texto humano y details tipados.
- [ ] Pagination/filter/export funcionan y respetan scope.
- [ ] Request/trace IDs correlacionan UI→API→DB→outbox.
- [ ] Health live/ready detecta DB/migration/RLS/outbox failures.
- [ ] Métricas/alertas cubren foundation/network sin inventar datos.
- [ ] RLS denials son observables sin confirmar resource existence al cliente.
- [ ] CI añade security/dependency/container gates documentados.

## Negative proof

- Audit insert/outbox falla: business mutation crítica hace rollback.
- Worker procesa dos veces: projection sigue idempotente.
- Event details incluyen token/password: schema/test lo rechaza.
- Audit de Org A no aparece a Org B.
- Platform admin org-less no abre business detail desde audit.
- PostgreSQL caído/migration drift: live puede seguir vivo, ready falla.
- UI recibe event version desconocida: muestra fallback seguro, no crash/JSON leak.

## Fuera de alcance

- data warehouse/BI empresarial completo;
- SIEM externo obligatorio;
- reemplazar project/stock/floor ledgers por security audit;
- prometer SLO sin baseline medido.

## Definition of Done

Todas las operaciones críticas de #446 dejan evidencia durable y correlacionable; operadores y admins entienden qué ocurrió; readiness/alerts detectan fallas antes del usuario; CI reduce regresiones de seguridad y supply chain.
issues.title: [P0][OPS-ORG] Durable audit outbox, human-readable security timeline and observability

issues.body:
## Objetivo

Crear gates automatizados obligatorios que demuestren en infraestructura real que Usuarios, Multi-Taller y Red de Ventas funcionan y permanecen aislados antes de reabrir el roadmap normal de nuevas funciones.

Tracks #446.

## Filosofía

- No mocks en los boundaries críticos de auth, PostgreSQL, RLS, migrations, router y browser.
- Un skip en modo gate es failure, siguiendo F179.
- Positive path + negative proof + concurrency + failure injection.
- El gate se ejecuta desde base fresca y desde upgrade de una base representativa.
- Los tests verifican hechos y datos, no sólo status codes o source grep.

## Gates

### Gate A — Organization Foundation Readiness

Hard prerequisites:

- #448 OpenAPI/typed client;
- #449 RLS;
- #450 identity/membership/invitation;
- #451 team safety;
- #452 organization lifecycle/provisioning;
- #458 Web Organization UX;
- mecanismo durable de #461 para events críticos;
- session-critical portion de #460 cuando el gate la consuma.

Gate A debe cerrar **antes de iniciar nuevas familias persistentes de negocio**, incluyendo implementación DT-1 #385, salvo discovery/documentación.

### Gate B — Sales Network Readiness

Hard prerequisites:

- Gate A;
- #453 relationships;
- #454 catalog publication;
- #455 pricing;
- #456 ManufacturingOrder handoff;
- #457 installation assignment;
- #459 Web Network UX;
- #460/#461 completos para seguridad/operación de red.

## Infraestructura de test

- PostgreSQL real efímero con rol de migration y rol de app sin BYPASSRLS.
- Migrations completas desde cero.
- Upgrade fixture desde schema multi-org actual con datos sanitizados/sintéticos.
- API/router Go reales.
- Browser E2E real, preferentemente Playwright.
- Outbox worker/read models reales o harness equivalente.
- Media storage fixture/signed URL flow.
- Clock control para expiry/absolute session.
- Failure injection points explícitos.
- Fixtures deterministas; cero datos personales reales.

## Gate A scenarios obligatorios

### Identity/onboarding

1. Platform/bootstrap crea Factory A correctamente.
2. Admin invita new user; invite accepted; entra directo a Factory A.
3. Existing user acepta invite de Factory B; memberships aisladas.
4. Expired/revoked/rotated/replayed token falla correctamente.
5. Public register no crea pending membership implícita.

### Membership/team

6. Roles múltiples y capabilities correctas por org type.
7. Membership suspended permanece visible y pierde acceso inmediatamente.
8. Reactivation restaura sólo esa org.
9. Gerente de ventas/producción no escala fuera de policy.
10. Seats limit bloquea activation/accept.
11. Offboarding reasigna customers/projects o devuelve blockers.
12. Session revocation afecta sólo membership objetivo.

### Last admin/concurrency

13. Dos admins concurrentes se degradan/suspenden: una operación falla `LAST_ADMIN`.
14. Transfer admin es atómica.
15. Stale If-Match no sobrescribe roles/status.

### Tenant/RLS

16. A→B/B→A list/get/write/delete/upsert por APIs.
17. SQL directo bajo app role tampoco cruza tenants aunque falte filtro Go.
18. Pool reuse no filtra tenant context.
19. Platform admin org-less no accede business data.
20. Support session accede sólo su org y deja actor real.
21. Shared-resource policies cumplen matriz exacta.

### Organization provisioning

22. Fresh provision success produce org active/readiness completa.
23. Failure inyectada en cada step nunca produce active parcial.
24. Retry con misma idempotency key reusa misma org.
25. Same key/different payload conflict.
26. Slug collision concurrente determinista.
27. Suspend/reactivate/offboard/terminate respetan sessions/blockers/history.

### React/session/cache

28. Login/switch A→B no muestra ni muta datos A.
29. Dos tabs siguen la policy elegida y no mezclan scope.
30. `/org/team` failure no dispara legacy fallback.
31. Membership suspended aparece en tab correcto.
32. Platform muestra provisioning real/typed DTO.
33. Success no aparece antes del server commit.
34. Absolute session no supera 18h; revocation/MFA paths según #460.

## Gate B scenario E2E obligatorio

```text
Platform admin provisiona Factory A
→ Factory A crea/provisiona Store B y relationship
→ publica CatalogPublication v1
→ asigna PriceBook/PartnerPolicy v1
→ Store admin invita Seller S
→ S acepta y entra a Store B
→ S crea QuoteRevision pinneada a catalog/price v1
→ S selecciona Factory A por relationship sin membership en A
→ submit retry/double click crea exactamente una ManufacturingOrder
→ Factory A ve la order exacta y Store B ve projection comercial
→ Factory solicita clarification
→ Store responde/nueva revision según contract
→ Factory acepta/programa
→ Factory publica v2 y activa PriceBook v2; order/quote v1 permanecen iguales
→ Store no puede leer BOM/cost/CNC/internal notes
→ InstallationOrder se asigna a Partner C
→ Installer de C accede sólo a jobs asignados
→ visita/issues/punch/closeout reutilizan #303
→ suspender relationship bloquea nuevas submissions sin borrar historia
```

Variantes obligatorias:

- Store con dos fábricas exige selección explícita.
- UUID de factory no relacionada falla.
- Catalog subscription stale/conflict/failure rollback.
- Price discount fuera de policy requiere approval.
- Relationship/organization suspended durante cada fase.
- Outbox duplicate/retry no duplica order/event/projection.
- Unrelated Org D obtiene 404 en todas las resources compartidas.
- Data grant de installer expira/revoca al reassign/cerrar.

## Contract/legacy guards

El gate falla si quedan callers/runtime paths de:

- `/api/admin/users/*` desde Team;
- `ApproveUser` con InitialOrganizationID;
- fallback `/org/team → /admin/users`;
- parent_organization_id como authority de autorización;
- generic Project PUT que cambia manufacturer/handoff;
- JWT de sesión genérico por query media;
- DTOs manuales incompatibles en superficies migradas;
- audit best-effort para commands críticos;
- tablas tenant sin RLS policy registrada.

## Verification matrix

Cada scenario debe mapear:

- issue/acceptance criterion;
- actor + active organization;
- endpoint/command;
- DB/RLS assertion;
- audit/outbox assertion;
- UI assertion cuando aplica;
- positive result;
- negative proof;
- cleanup/upgrade coverage.

Mantener documento canónico de matriz y coverage inventory.

## CI/release integration

- Gate A y B son jobs identificables.
- No skips en branch/release gate.
- Failure bloquea merge/deploy según phase.
- Artifacts sanitizados: traces, screenshots, DB diagnostics, policy inventory.
- Nightly puede ejecutar matrix/chaos más amplia; PR gate conserva el core completo.
- Pilot deploy exige Gate A; Red de Ventas real exige Gate B.
- `scripts/pilot-gate.sh` o sucesor integra ambos sin verde falso.

## Performance/security checks

Con baselines medidos, incluir:

- N+1 en organization/platform/member lists;
- p95 razonable de org switch/team list/order queue;
- RLS/index query plans críticos;
- invitation/login rate limit;
- no secrets/PII en logs/artifacts;
- dependency/security scan gates de #461.

No fijar números inventados: medir baseline y documentar budgets aprobados.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Gate A cubre todos los scenarios Foundation y bloquea regresiones.
- [ ] Gate B cubre el E2E network completo y variantes maliciosas.
- [ ] PostgreSQL/RLS/API/browser/outbox reales participan.
- [ ] Upgrade fixture detecta migration/data issues, no sólo fresh DB.
- [ ] No skips permitidos en gate mode.
- [ ] Legacy guard confirma eliminación real, no sólo falta de uso en happy path.
- [ ] Failure injection prueba rollback/repair/idempotency.
- [ ] Artifacts diagnósticos son útiles y no contienen secretos.
- [ ] Docs/CI/deployment enlazan el gate obligatorio.
- [ ] #446 no se cierra hasta ambos gates y global E2E verdes.

## Negative proof

- Deshabilitar RLS o eliminar una policy hace fallar Gate A.
- Reintroducir fallback legacy hace fallar build/test.
- Devolver 201 con provisioning parcial hace fallar scenario.
- Crear dos ManufacturingOrders por retry hace fallar Gate B.
- Filtrar un campo de costo a Store hace fallar serialization assertion.
- Worker/outbox duplicado produce una sola projection/event effect.
- Sin DB/browser requerido, gate falla; nunca skip verde.

## Definition of Done

Gate A y Gate B son autoridad ejecutable de readiness, corren en CI/deploy, cubren fresh+upgrade+malicious+failure paths y permiten continuar el roadmap con una base organizacional probada en lugar de asumida.
issues.title: [P0][ORG-E2E] Mandatory Foundation and Sales Network readiness gates

issues.body:
# Granete for SketchUp Excellence v2

## Objective

Turn the validated Granete for SketchUp technical foundation into a professional, differentiated and commercially operable authoring product that is fully connected to the Go backend and React application without duplicating business/manufacturing truth.

> **SketchUp owns authoring and host interaction. Granete owns business identity, catalog resolution, manufacturing truth, revisions, release and machine outputs. React owns administration, project/revision visibility and explicit business commands.**

This META coordinates the product/host and cross-surface excellence program. It does not replace:

- #290 portfolio umbrella;
- #384 Project Digital Thread;
- #413 native host representation;
- #446/#462 Organization Foundation and gates;
- #401 material-aware resolution.

## Canonical authority

## Objective

Deliver the host/UX portion that was not fully realized by the domain baseline of #349: let users select managed internal components in SketchUp and add/move/duplicate/remove supported internals through semantic authoring commands, while Granete remains the sole authority for resolved geometry, relationships and machining.

Tracks #465, #290 and historical baseline #349/#356.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/sketchup-plugin-excellence.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-authoring-interaction-contract.md`
- `docs/sketchup-excellence-execution-plan.md`
- `docs/architecture/parametric-furniture-library.md` + ADR-0002
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-native-entity-model.md` + ADR-0004
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`
- `docs/sketchup-manufacturing-contract.md`
- #356 relationships/joint-driven machining
- #347 authoritative preflight

## Problem / closure boundary of #349

#349 established the universal parametric library/domain capability and the architectural contract for controlled internal authoring. This issue owns the missing **SketchUp host interaction** required for a professional product. Do not reopen or duplicate the seven domain primitives; consume them.

## First supported authoring slice

Use one canonical cabinet with:

- left/right side;
- bottom/top;
- back;
- one door;
- one movable shelf;
- ability to add a second shelf from the same reusable component definition;
- explicit relationships/joinery to both sides.

The UX must support, at minimum:

```text
select shelf
→ inspector identifies concrete componentInstanceId
→ move shelf by precise mm or constrained viewport gesture
→ submit authoring intent
→ Granete re-resolves complete furniture
→ atomic native rebuild
```

and:

```text
+ Add internal → Shelf
→ choose constrained position
→ allocate a new component occurrence/intent identity according to the current authoring contract
→ Granete resolves relationships + machining
→ rebuild
```

plus duplicate/remove equivalents.

## Interaction model

### Selection

- clicking/drilling down to a managed board must expose its semantic context;
- top-level furniture remains the main unit, but child selection is first-class for supported authoring;
- selection is resolved by metadata/InstancePath, not display name.

### Commands

Commands must be semantic, e.g. domain-equivalent forms of:

- `MoveComponentIntent`;
- `AddComponentIntent`;
- `DuplicateComponentIntent`;
- `RemoveComponentIntent`;
- `ChangeJoineryIntent` where allowed.

Exact API/type names may follow existing domain conventions, but a command must never persist raw derived hole coordinates as truth.

### Positioning

Support both:

- precise numeric input in mm;
- viewport manipulation constrained to the allowed authoring axis/range.

The client may calculate transient cursor/snap preview. The accepted geometry comes only from the resolved result.

### Rebuild

Every successful mutation:

- obtains a valid resolved layout before destructive host mutation;
- preserves top-level furniture identity/world transform;
- rebuilds/rebinds native child ComponentInstances atomically;
- updates metadata only after accepted state;
- produces one coherent SketchUp undo action.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selecting a shelf shows that shelf, its owning furniture and allowed actions without confusing `componentDefinitionId` with `componentInstanceId`.
- [ ] Moving a shelf updates authoring intent and causes only dependent relationship/machining changes server/domain-side.
- [ ] Adding a second shelf may share `componentDefinitionId` but has a distinct non-colliding `componentInstanceId`.
- [ ] Removing one shelf removes only its dependent relationships/machining.
- [ ] Duplicating one shelf does not duplicate the first shelf's occurrence identity or relationship IDs.
- [ ] Unsupported movement axis/range is prevented or rejected with actionable feedback.
- [ ] A failed resolve leaves previous hierarchy/metadata intact.
- [ ] A successful edit is one undoable action.
- [ ] Ruby/JavaScript contains no joint/drilling formula table.
- [ ] Real-host smoke covers select → move → rebuild and add → undo.

## Negative proof required

Tests fail if:

- child identity is inferred from name/geometry/persistent_id;
- move directly edits faces/pushpull as final productive state;
- raw CNC coordinates become editable authoring truth;
- two shelves share the same `componentInstanceId`;
- deleting a shelf leaves orphan derived machining;
- failed remote/domain resolution clears or partially rebuilds the furniture;
- only a pure domain function is implemented while no host UX exists.

## Explicit non-goals

- arbitrary free-form CAD conversion;
- universal constraints for every furniture type in V1;
- persistent Project/Design identity before #384 prerequisites;
- direct editing of derived ManufacturingFeatures.

## Definition of Done

On real SketchUp, the canonical cabinet supports selecting an internal shelf, moving it precisely, adding a second one, duplicating/removing a supported internal and undoing each operation, while Granete re-resolves relationships/machining and no manufacturing rule is duplicated in the plugin.

## Objective

Deliver the SketchUp host/UX portion of the hardware baseline established by #350: users can select, move, configure and substitute supported hardware through `HardwarePlacement` authoring intent while Granete re-resolves dependent machining and preserves provenance.

Tracks #465, #290 and historical baseline #350/#356.

## Hard prerequisites

- #415 native ComponentInstance renderer ✅
- #404 material-aware atomic rebuild ✅
- #350 domain/contract baseline ✅
- #356 relationship/machining model ✅
- #347 authoritative preflight ✅

#467 is not a hard prerequisite for every hardware action, but shared selection/inspector and mutation infrastructure should be reused rather than duplicated.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/sketchup-plugin-excellence.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-authoring-interaction-contract.md`
- `docs/sketchup-excellence-execution-plan.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`
- `docs/architecture/parametric-furniture-library.md`
- `docs/architecture/manufacturing-feature-model.md`
- `docs/sketchup-manufacturing-contract.md`
- #350 and #356

## Problem / closure boundary of #350

#350 delivered the domain/contract semantics for placement identity, host binding, provenance and machining isolation. This issue owns the missing **professional SketchUp interaction**. Do not create a second hardware model in Ruby.

## First supported slice

Use one door with:

- two hinges;
- one handle;
- one nearby shelf relationship capable of producing a real drilling conflict.

Required flows:

```text
select hinge
→ inspector shows hardware definition + concrete placement
→ move along allowed host-face axes / enter offsets
→ submit HardwarePlacement intent
→ Granete re-resolves hinge machining
→ unrelated shelf machining remains unchanged
→ atomic rebuild + preflight refresh
```

and:

```text
select hardware
→ Replace
→ choose compatible HardwareDefinition
→ Granete validates host/compatibility/profile
→ re-resolve geometry + machining + BOM consequences
→ commit one undoable action
```

## Required behavior

### Selection and inspector

Expose:

- `hardwarePlacementId`;
- `hardwareDefinitionId`/catalog reference;
- host `componentInstanceId`;
- face/anchor semantic context;
- offsets/rotation/handedness that are actually authorable;
- whether placement is `manual` or `derived`.

Derived placements must not be presented as freely editable manual coordinates.

### Move/edit

- allow precise mm offsets and constrained viewport movement where supported;
- client may show transient preview only;
- server/domain owns accepted resolved placement and machining;
- unsupported face/host/range fails with remediation.

### Substitution

The selector must filter or clearly classify:

- compatible;
- conditionally compatible / requires change;
- incompatible.

Compatibility must come from catalog/domain capability, not UI hardcoding by brand/model name.

### Conflict loop

A hinge moved into conflict with shelf machining must:

- produce an authoritative preflight issue;
- be navigable through #466;
- allow correction by moving the hinge or supported related authoring intent;
- never silently delete unrelated machining.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selecting a manual hinge resolves exact `hardwarePlacementId` and host `componentInstanceId`.
- [ ] Moving the hinge updates placement intent, not drilling coordinates directly.
- [ ] Only hinge-dependent machining changes when shelf intent is unchanged.
- [ ] A derived hardware placement cannot be edited as if it were a manual placement.
- [ ] Replacing a hardware definition recalculates visual asset/BOM/machining as returned by Granete.
- [ ] Incompatible substitutions are blocked with actionable reason.
- [ ] Failed resolution keeps previous hierarchy/metadata intact.
- [ ] Successful edit/substitution is one undoable action.
- [ ] Preflight issue/navigation integrates with #466.
- [ ] Real-host smoke covers move + conflict + fix and one substitution.

## Negative proof required

Tests fail if:

- hardware is located by name instead of placement identity;
- host binding uses only `componentDefinitionId`;
- Ruby contains drilling formulas;
- moving a hinge changes shelf-derived machining without a related intent change;
- derived placement can be dragged freely as manual truth;
- incompatible hardware is accepted because visual geometry fits;
- only a domain helper is implemented while the host editor is absent.

## Explicit non-goals

- universal hardware catalog coverage in the first slice;
- direct CSG/hole editing;
- machine-specific postprocessing;
- billing/pricing UI beyond displaying consequences supplied by Granete.

## Definition of Done

On real SketchUp the user can select a supported hinge/handle, edit a manual placement, replace it with a compatible catalog hardware definition, see Granete recalculate dependent machining and resolve a real conflict without duplicated manufacturing logic or collateral changes.

## Objective

Replace the current insert-at-origin + generic Move-tool handoff with a professional SketchUp placement workflow: ghost preview, semantic snapping, orientation feedback, precise offsets and repeat placement, while keeping placement as authoring/spatial intent rather than manufacturing calculation.

Tracks #465 and #290.

## Hard prerequisites

- #415 native top-level Furniture ComponentInstance ✅
- #414 authoritative child transforms ✅

Project-owned placement of existing FurnitureInstances later consumes #389; this issue must not create parallel Project identity.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/sketchup-plugin-excellence.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-authoring-interaction-contract.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-native-entity-model.md`

## Required flows

### Insert preview

```text
choose furniture
→ ghost/preview follows cursor
→ infer SketchUp point/face normally
→ show orientation and snap candidate
→ click to place
→ accepted top-level transform stored as authoring/spatial state
```

### Semantic furniture snap

For supported furniture, offer non-destructive snap suggestions such as:

- side-to-side furniture alignment;
- wall/face alignment;
- floor/base plane placement;
- configurable gap/offset;
- rotate/flip orientation before commit.

Semantic snap rules are authoring conveniences, not manufacturing rules.

### Precise placement

Allow numeric mm offset/distance after selecting a snap or reference, without exposing quaternions/world matrices as the normal workflow.

### Repeat placement

Allow rapid placement of the same definition/preset without re-opening the entire library. In connected Project mode later, every new physical unit must still receive distinct server-owned FurnitureInstance identity via #390.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New furniture no longer requires spawning at origin as the primary user flow.
- [ ] Preview never mutates productive metadata until placement is committed.
- [ ] Cancel leaves zero managed residue/definitions.
- [ ] Wall/face and furniture-side snap work on a canonical room fixture.
- [ ] User can rotate/flip before placement and enter a precise mm offset.
- [ ] Placement changes only top-level spatial transform; child productive geometry remains local/authoritative.
- [ ] Repeat placement creates distinct host instances and, once #390 is active, distinct business identities.
- [ ] One placement = one undo action.
- [ ] Real-host smoke verifies preview/cancel/place/undo and at least two snap modes.

## Negative proof required

- no manufacturing dimension is derived from wall geometry;
- no world-AABB baking into part definitions;
- cancel cannot leave hidden managed entities;
- repeat placement cannot reuse a connected `furnitureInstanceId`;
- snap cannot silently alter cabinet width/depth/material.

## Definition of Done

A user can browse a furniture item, place it directly where intended with preview/snapping/precise offset, rotate it before commit and quickly repeat placement, with no origin-first workaround and no manufacturing truth moved into SketchUp.

## Objective

Visualize Granete-resolved manufacturing features inside SketchUp as read-only inspection overlays so designers can understand drilling, grooves, pockets, edge treatment and their semantic provenance without turning SketchUp geometry into manufacturing authority.

Tracks #465 and #290.

## Hard prerequisites

- #347 authoritative preflight ✅
- #356 relationship/joint provenance ✅
- #350 hardware provenance baseline ✅
- #415 native managed hierarchy ✅

#466 should be reused for issue navigation and review state.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/sketchup-plugin-excellence.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-authoring-interaction-contract.md`
- `docs/architecture/manufacturing-feature-model.md`
- `docs/sketchup-manufacturing-contract.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`

## Required UX

Add a manufacturing inspection mode, scoped to selected furniture/part where possible:

```text
Select managed part
→ Ver fabricación
→ overlay resolved ManufacturingFeatures
→ click feature
→ detail + provenance
→ navigate to source authoring context
```

Supported first visual vocabulary should cover a representative subset such as:

- drilling points/cylinders;
- groove/dado/slot paths;
- pocket/cutout bounds where already represented by the neutral model;
- edge-band indicators;
- face/orientation markers.

The exact geometry is visualization only.

## Provenance detail

For each resolved feature, show domain-provided information such as:

- feature/operation type;
- dimensions/diameter/depth where relevant;
- target face;
- source kind `relationship | joint | manualHardwarePlacement`;
- source identifiers;
- host `componentInstanceId`;
- machine capability warning when available.

Provide navigation to the source authoring entity when possible:

- joint/relationship → owning components;
- manual hardware placement → hardware editor;
- part → contextual inspector.

## Rendering rules

- overlays must be ephemeral or clearly namespaced non-productive visualization;
- never persist overlay geometry as BOM/CNC truth;
- never scan overlay faces/edges to recreate operations;
- allow hide/show and scope filtering;
- keep viewport usable for representative project sizes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A selected board can show its resolved drilling/groove/edge features in the correct local/world pose.
- [ ] Feature selection shows source provenance supplied by Granete.
- [ ] Manual hinge drilling links back to the exact `hardwarePlacementId`.
- [ ] Shelf joint drilling links to the exact relationship/joint context.
- [ ] Overlay can be toggled off with zero change to productive managed hierarchy.
- [ ] Rebuild/re-resolve refreshes overlays; stale overlay is never presented as current without warning.
- [ ] No overlay entity enters DesignRevision semantic manifest/BOM by scanning.
- [ ] Real-host smoke validates pose under moved/rotated furniture.

## Negative proof required

Tests must fail if:

- Ruby derives hole coordinates from hardware name/role;
- overlay geometry becomes authoring/manufacturing truth;

- feature provenance is empty/ambiguous when domain says it is derived;
- arbitrary user geometry is included as a ManufacturingFeature.

A designer can inspect how Granete intends to manufacture a selected managed part, understand where each representative operation comes from, navigate back to the responsible authoring context and turn the visualization off without any mutation of manufacturing truth.

## Objective

Enable safe bulk editing of multiple managed furniture instances in SketchUp for shared authoring properties such as material roles, supported parameters and hardware systems, with explicit impact preview and no client-side manufacturing calculations.

Tracks #465 and #290.

## Hard prerequisites

- #404 material-aware atomic rebuild ✅
- #415 native hierarchy ✅
- #403 material binding semantics ✅

For durable project/room-wide scopes, Gate A #462 and the corresponding #384 Project/Design persistence are prerequisites. Before that, this issue may implement multi-selection scope only within the current open model/working authoring context.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/sketchup-plugin-excellence.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-authoring-interaction-contract.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`
- `docs/architecture/material-aware-furniture-resolution.md`
- #384 for any durable project scope

## Required UX

When multiple Granete furniture instances are selected, show a batch inspector that distinguishes:

- common editable values;
- mixed values;
- unsupported properties for one or more selected items;
- impact scope and affected count.

First supported operations:

- change one material-binding role where the selected furniture supports that role;
- change a shared dimension/parameter only when the definition contract marks it compatible;
- change a supported hardware configuration after #468 infrastructure exists.

Before apply, show an impact summary from resolved/domain results where available, such as furniture count, parts/hardware affected and blockers.

## Mutation semantics

- batch apply is explicit;
- every furniture is re-resolved through Granete;
- failure policy must be explicit: prefer all-or-nothing for one user batch command unless the domain exposes a reviewed partial-success contract;
- no UI loop may report success for 7 items when only 5 were accepted;
- one batch action should be one coherent undo action in SketchUp where host semantics allow.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Multi-select of managed furniture exposes a batch inspector without losing individual identities.
- [ ] Mixed values are shown as mixed, never as an arbitrary first value.
- [ ] Material role change affects all and only compatible selected furniture.
- [ ] Unsupported role/parameter is excluded or blocks with clear reason; no silent skip.
- [ ] A failed batch does not leave half the selection rebuilt if the chosen contract is atomic.
- [ ] UI does not calculate BOM/price/manufacturing impact itself.
- [ ] Durable `project_default`/room scopes are not claimed before #384 provides persistence.
- [ ] Real-host smoke covers 3 furniture items with at least one mixed-value state and undo.

## Negative proof required

- do not use `selection.first` as the batch source of truth;
- no first-item value may overwrite mixed values silently;
- no project-wide material default stored only in session/local metadata may be presented as durable;
- no partial failure may be rendered as total success.

## Definition of Done

A user can select several managed furniture instances and safely apply at least one shared material role and one compatible parameter with honest mixed-state UI, authoritative re-resolution, coherent rollback/undo and no false project persistence.

issues.body:
## Objective

Create one reusable semantic selection/context foundation for Granete for SketchUp so preflight navigation, direct internal authoring, hardware editing, manufacturing inspection and batch UX all identify the same managed entity hierarchy and expose actions from capabilities rather than implementing separate name/type heuristics.

Tracks #465 and #290.

## Hard prerequisites

- #415 native managed ComponentInstance hierarchy ✅
- #346 semantic metadata/identity baseline ✅

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/sketchup-plugin-excellence.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-authoring-interaction-contract.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-interaction-model.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-native-entity-model.md`

## Why this is a shared P0 foundation

#466, #467, #468 and #470 all need to answer the same questions:

```text
What exactly is selected?
Which FurnitureInstance owns it?
Which stable Granete IDs identify it?
What authoring actions are legal here?
How do we recover after child host regeneration?
```

If each feature implements this independently, identity drift and host-specific heuristics are almost guaranteed.

## SelectionContext contract

Define/reuse one canonical internal contract equivalent to:

```text
SelectionContext
  kind = furniture | aggregate | part | hardware | unmanaged
  furnitureInstanceId?
  furnitureInstanceRef?        # compatibility only
  furnitureDefinitionId?
  componentInstanceId?
  componentDefinitionId?
  catalogComponentId?
  hardwarePlacementId?
  hardwareDefinitionId?
  hostComponentInstanceId?
  projectId?
  designId?
  baseRevisionId?
  hostLocator?                 # technical only
  semanticPath?
  capabilities
```

Exact representation may be Ruby objects/DTOs appropriate to the current architecture, but semantic responsibilities and ID separation are mandatory.

## Entity resolution

- inspect nested `ComponentInstance`s, not only `selection.first` as top-level furniture;
- recover owning furniture via InstancePath/metadata;
- resolve semantic identity from Granete metadata;
- names/GUID/persistent_id may help locate a current host entity but are never identity authority;
- support rebuilding child host entities while preserving semantic navigation when contract identity remains stable;
- unmanaged user geometry returns `kind=unmanaged`, never a guessed Granete part.

## Capability-driven inspector

The context must expose/derive legal actions from definition/domain capability, not hardcoded furniture names/roles.

Representative capabilities:

### Furniture

- edit parameters/materials;
- duplicate/delete where allowed;
- run/review preflight;
- inspect manufacturing.

### Part/internal

- move within constraint;
- duplicate/add related internal/remove;
- change joinery where explicitly supported;
- inspect manufacturing.

### Hardware

- manual vs derived;
- move/rotate/handedness where allowed;
- replace compatible definition;
- inspect machining.

Unsupported actions are absent/disabled with explanation; the client must not infer legality from `slotId` strings.

## Inspector UX

- furniture selection shows furniture-level properties/actions;
- drill-down/nested selection shows part or hardware context while retaining owning furniture breadcrumb;
- user can return to owning furniture context;
- selection changes update one central state model consumed by #466/#467/#468/#470;
- copy UI Spanish, identifiers internal English.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selecting top-level furniture produces `kind=furniture` with correct Granete identity.
- [ ] Selecting a managed shelf produces `kind=part`, exact `componentInstanceId`, reusable `componentDefinitionId` and owning furniture context.
- [ ] Selecting manual hardware produces `kind=hardware`, exact placement and host occurrence IDs.
- [ ] Derived hardware is identified as derived and does not expose manual-edit capability.
- [ ] Rename does not change SelectionContext identity.
- [ ] Move/rotate top-level furniture does not change SelectionContext identity.
- [ ] Child regeneration can recover the same semantic context using Granete identity rather than stale host locator alone.
- [ ] Arbitrary user ComponentInstance/Group remains unmanaged.
- [ ] #466/#467/#468/#470 can consume this foundation without their own parallel selection models.
- [ ] Real-host TestUp covers top-level, nested part, hardware, rename, rebuild and unmanaged selection.

## Negative proof required

Tests fail if:

- part identity is inferred from name, dimensions or persistent_id;
- selecting two different shelves sharing one `componentDefinitionId` collapses them to one context;
- Group merely responding to `#definition` is treated as native managed entity without metadata/type rules;
- hardware host binding loses concrete occurrence identity;
- each downstream feature defines its own incompatible selection payload.

## Explicit non-goals

- Project persistence (#384);
- authoring mutation commands (#467/#468);
- preflight calculation (#347);
- ManufacturingFeature rendering (#470).

## Definition of Done

One real-host-tested SelectionContext/capability foundation drives the contextual inspector and is explicitly reused by downstream excellence features, with stable Granete identity and no name/GUID/geometry-based authority.

issues.body:
## Problem

`POST /api/furniture/authoring/resolve` v1 resolves the canonical #467/#468 first slices from a versioned body, but the current Go catalog model exposes only the legacy `Module` dimension projection (`widthMm`, `heightMm`, `depthMm`). The richer TypeScript `FurnitureDefinition.parameters` contract (`number|string|boolean|enum`, defaults, min/max/step/options) is not yet persisted or projected by the Go catalog.

Accepting arbitrary scalar keys today would be worse than rejecting them: the server would echo authoring intent that does not affect authoritative geometry/manufacturing truth. Hardcoding every future parameter in the transport would recreate the ad-hoc API problem #477 removed.

## Requested outcome

Add one server-authoritative, versioned parameter-definition projection that the rich authoring resolver and catalog endpoint share.

The projection must support:

- parameter identity and type: `number|string|boolean|enum`;
- default, required/optional semantics;
- numeric `min|max|step` and integer/count constraints;
- enum options and boolean validation;
- definition revision/hash participation so the same pinned request cannot resolve against changed parameter rules;
- evaluated normalized parameters returned by the resolver;
- Go ↔ TypeScript parity fixtures generated from the same definition contract;
- migration/upgrade behavior for existing modules whose only parameters are width/height/depth.

## Current evidence

- TypeScript already defines `FurnitureDefinition.parameters` in `packages/domain/src/smartFurnitureDomain.ts`.
- Go `domain.Module` exposes dimensions and presets but no generic typed parameter-definition list.
- PR #481 therefore validates only the authoritative dimension projection. Its component/relationship/hardware authoring first slices remain usable, but the endpoint must not claim universal parameter-family support until this issue lands.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The catalog API returns a versioned typed parameter definition for each furniture definition.
- [ ] The catalog revision/hash covers parameter schema and defaults.
- [ ] Authoring resolve validates provided parameters against that definition rather than a handler key allowlist.
- [ ] Defaults are evaluated server-side and returned in `normalizedSnapshot.parameters`.
- [ ] Unknown, wrong-type, out-of-range, invalid-step and invalid-enum values produce stable structured codes.
- [ ] Shared Go/TypeScript fixtures cover number, integer/count, boolean, enum and string values.
- [ ] Changing only a parameter rule changes the required definition/catalog pin.
- [ ] Existing width/height/depth modules preserve current layout parity.

## Negative proof

Tests fail if an unknown parameter is silently accepted, if a valid definition-owned parameter requires a handler code change, if the client becomes authority for defaults/ranges/options, or if a parameter-rule change can reuse the prior catalog pin.

## Scope boundary

This issue does not add Project `FurnitureInstance` persistence (#385), SketchUp UI interactions (#467/#468), or arbitrary Ruby-side parameter evaluation. It blocks broad typed-parameter authoring families, not the already-scoped shelf/hardware first slices of #467/#468.

issues.body:
## Objective

Unify the HTTP contracts used by Granete for SketchUp, the Go backend and the React application under one executable, generated and drift-checked API authority, without replacing the semantic authoring contract delivered by #477 or creating Digital Thread persistence before Gate A.

Tracks #465, #384, #448 and #290.

## Why this is required

Organization/Auth surfaces already use generated OpenAPI contracts, while the furniture family currently evolves through a parallel combination of Go wire structs, TypeScript contracts/JSON Schema and Ruby parsers:

```text
GET  /api/furniture/definitions
GET  /api/furniture/definitions/{definitionId}/layout
POST /api/furniture/authoring/resolve
```

#477 made the rich authoring payload semantically shared and versioned, but those HTTP endpoints are not yet part of the same generated API boundary consumed by React and enforced by the repository OpenAPI drift gate. That gap will become dangerous when Project Furniture, DesignRevision, publication and reconciliation arrive.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/sketchup-backend-web-integration-excellence.md` once merged
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-plugin-excellence.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-authoring-interaction-contract.md`
- `docs/sketchup-manufacturing-contract.md`
- `docs/architecture/project-design-digital-thread.md`
- ADR-0001, ADR-0003 and ADR-0006
- #448 generated OpenAPI/error/idempotency conventions
- #477 `granete.sketchup-authoring-resolve.v1`

## Hard prerequisites

- #448 generated contract foundation ✅
- #477 rich authoring resolve contract ✅

Persistent `FurnitureInstance`, `Design` and `DesignRevision` operations remain gated by Foundation Gate A #462 and their owners #385–#395. This issue may deliver the stateless/current furniture API contract before Gate A.

## Canonical contract decision

Keep OpenAPI modular internally if needed, but generate and verify one coherent public API surface. A valid implementation may use:

```text
contracts/openapi/
  granete-api.v1.yaml              # assembled/generated authority
  organization.v1.yaml
  furniture-authoring.v1.yaml
  project-design.v1.yaml           # added incrementally after Gate A
  shared/
    errors.yaml
    identity.yaml
    concurrency.yaml
```

File organization is an implementation choice. Semantic ownership is not.

The existing JSON Schemas for rich authoring remain authoritative for their closed payload shapes and are referenced/reused by OpenAPI rather than manually restated with a second incompatible model.

## Required scope

### Current furniture endpoints

Add generated/validated contracts for at least:

- `GET /furniture/definitions`;
- `GET /furniture/definitions/{definitionId}/layout`;
- `POST /furniture/authoring/resolve`;
- any explicit preflight endpoint/projection consumed by #466, or document the exact preflight projection returned by authoring resolve.

### Shared generation

- Generate TypeScript operations/types for React and shared clients.
- Generate or validate Go public types/handler binding where supported by the current generator.
- Keep Ruby behind a strict contract adapter consuming the same schema IDs, versions and fixtures; do not hand-maintain a divergent payload.
- CI fails on uncommitted generation or OpenAPI/JSON-Schema drift.
- Runtime boundary rejects malformed server responses before React or SketchUp mutates state.

### Error and correlation model

Reconcile the API error envelope and authoring `ContractIssue` model explicitly:

- stable `code`;
- localized `message` as presentation copy, never behavioral authority;
- `requestId`;
- `messageId`/correlation where the authoring envelope owns it;
- `retryable`;
- bounded `details`;
- semantic entity/path/remediation for preflight/authoring issues.

Do not force every domain issue into an unrelated generic field-error shape; define the relationship intentionally.

### Version and capability negotiation

Expose enough server capability/version information for clients to decide safely before host mutation, including:

- supported authoring schema versions;
- plugin/API compatibility range where applicable;
- feature capabilities needed by #466–#474;
- explicit unsupported/incompatible response.

Unknown versions fail closed.

### Security boundary

- SketchUp authorization uses explicit least-privilege capabilities coordinated with #460.
- No bearer session token in query strings.
- React and SketchUp may share contracts, not credentials.
- Persistent Design commands later consume ETag/baseRevision/idempotency conventions from their owning APIs.

## React integration

React must consume generated clients for:

- definition/parameter preview and validation;
- exact layout/resolve previews used by catalog authoring;
- Project/Design read models when their owning issues land.

React must not copy manufacturing or reconciliation rules from Go/TS domain projections merely to avoid calling the authoritative boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Current furniture definition, layout and authoring resolve endpoints exist in the generated API authority.
- [ ] OpenAPI references/reuses the versioned authoring JSON Schema instead of restating an incompatible shape.
- [ ] TypeScript generated client can call all current furniture endpoints without handwritten `fetch`/casts.
- [ ] Go responses and generated/runtime validators agree on valid and invalid fixtures.
- [ ] Ruby consumes the same schema identity/version and shared corpus.
- [ ] CI detects drift in spec, generated code and referenced schemas.
- [ ] Error behavior is code-driven and preserves structured preflight/authoring context.
- [ ] Capability/version mismatch is rejected before SketchUp host mutation.
- [ ] Current stateless resolve remains deterministic and creates no Project business records.
- [ ] The contract can be extended for #385–#395 without introducing a second Design authoring model.

## Negative proof required

Tests/review must fail if:

- React calls furniture endpoints through handwritten casts or a parallel DTO;
- OpenAPI and `sketchupAuthoringResolve.schema.json` describe different payloads;
- Ruby accepts a schema/version rejected by Go/TypeScript;
- endpoint behavior depends on localized message text;
- a version mismatch reaches `FurnitureBuilder` or mutates metadata;
- a web JWT is accepted as a SketchUp credential merely because the payload is valid;
- a temporary `SketchUpProject`/local business identity is added to bypass #384/Gate A.

## Definition of Done

Furniture, authoring and future Design API surfaces have one generated/drift-checked public contract, share exact versioned schemas and errors across Go, TypeScript and Ruby, are consumable by React without manual DTOs, and preserve the boundary that SketchUp owns interaction while Granete owns business/manufacturing truth.
issues.title: [P0][SU-API-2] Canonical generated furniture, authoring and Design API contract

issues.body:
## Objective

Expose the typed, versioned furniture parameter-definition model delivered by #483/#486 as a complete React catalog-authoring workflow, so workshops can create and maintain parameters and semantic bindings that SketchUp consumes without editing JSON, relying on fixed `width/height/depth` fields or duplicating resolve rules in the browser.

Tracks #465, #401, #349 and #290. Coordinates with #496.

## Problem

The backend/domain/SketchUp stack now supports definition-driven parameters such as:

```text
number | string | boolean | enum
```

with defaults, required/type/range/step/options validation and semantic consumers such as `componentQuantity` and `componentCondition`. SketchUp can render and submit those controls, but the React application does not yet provide an authoritative editor for the definition/binding model.

Without this issue, the feature remains operationally incomplete:

```text
backend can persist it
SketchUp can consume it
React cannot safely author/manage it
```

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/sketchup-backend-web-integration-excellence.md` once merged
- `docs/architecture/parametric-furniture-library.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-authoring-interaction-contract.md`
- `docs/architecture/material-aware-furniture-resolution.md`
- `docs/architecture/domain-model.md`
- #483/#486 typed parameter delivery
- #477 rich authoring resolve
- #496 generated furniture API contract

## Hard prerequisites

- #477 rich authoring resolve ✅
- #483/#486 typed parameter definitions and bindings ✅
- #448 generated API foundation ✅
- #496 for the final generated React transport/runtime boundary

UI discovery and component design may start before #496 closes, but production data access must consume the generated contract.

## Ownership boundary

React owns catalog administration and explainable preview. Granete domain/backend owns definition validity and resolved consequences.

React must not implement its own interpretation of:

- component quantity/condition semantics;
- relationship materialization;
- machining effects;
- hardware compatibility;
- manufacturing readiness;
- definition hash/catalog pin behavior.

## Required UX

Add a first-class section inside the FurnitureDefinition/module editor:

```text
Parámetros
├── Lista y orden
├── Crear parámetro
├── Editar definición
├── Vinculación semántica
├── Valores predeterminados
├── Presets que lo utilizan
└── Probar resolución
```

### Parameter list

Show at least:

- label and technical `name`;
- type;
- category;
- default value;
- required/optional;
- unit;
- binding/consumer summary;
- usage count in presets/definitions where available;
- valid/invalid status with remediation.

### Parameter editor

Support the complete current contract:

- `number`, including min/max/step/integer/unit;
- `string`, including `maxLength`;
- `boolean` preserving explicit `false`;
- `enum`, including ordered allowed options;
- `sortOrder`;
- label/help copy in Spanish;
- authoring category;
- default and required semantics;
- metadata-only declaration where explicitly supported.

Do not silently trim away meaningful empty-string/false values.

### Semantic binding editor

Expose only reviewed binding kinds from the backend contract, including their exact targets and ambiguity rules. The UI must:

- select concrete catalog components/relationships from authoritative IDs;
- explain the effect in user language;
- detect incompatible targets;
- show ambiguity instead of selecting the first component;
- never bind by display name, array index or geometry;
- prevent a metadata-only parameter from carrying a behavioral binding.

### Safe evolution

Before destructive or incompatible edits, show impact such as:

- presets using the parameter;
- defaults that will change;
- definitions/models requiring migration or refresh;
- whether the change affects the definition hash/catalog revision;
- whether an existing parameter name is reserved or referenced.

Use optimistic concurrency. A stale editor must not overwrite a newer definition.

### Authoritative preview

Provide a preview/test action that:

```text
current draft definition + sample parameter values/material choices
→ authoritative resolve through #496/#477
→ resolved component count/layout/preflight summary
```

The browser may render a 3D/read-only preview from the accepted result, but does not calculate manufacturing consequences.

## Integration with SketchUp

An E2E fixture must prove:

```text
create/edit parameter in React
→ publish/current catalog revision changes
→ SketchUp refreshes the definition
→ inspector renders the correct control
→ submit value
→ Go accepts/resolves it
→ React can later read the same normalized definition
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] React can create/edit/order every currently supported parameter type.
- [ ] Explicit `false` and empty strings round-trip correctly.
- [ ] Numeric constraints, enum options and string limits match backend validation exactly.
- [ ] Binding targets use stable IDs and expose ambiguity/incompatibility honestly.
- [ ] Reserved dimensions cannot be redefined inconsistently.
- [ ] Metadata-only parameters cannot carry behavioral bindings.
- [ ] Preset/reference impact is shown before incompatible edits.
- [ ] Stale writes fail with typed conflict and do not overwrite.
- [ ] Preview consumes authoritative resolve and displays structured issues.
- [ ] The exact definition authored in React is consumed by SketchUp without a parallel transformation model.
- [ ] Tests cover keyboard/accessibility, contract errors, stale conflict and cross-organization isolation.

## Negative proof required

Tests/review fail if:

- React writes raw JSON as the primary production workflow;
- the UI infers behavior from parameter names such as `shelfCount`;
- a binding chooses the first matching component on ambiguity;
- browser-only validation accepts a definition rejected by Go;
- changing a parameter mutates an old published/catalog-pinned definition silently;
- `false` or `""` is treated as missing;
- SketchUp needs a special hand-written adapter for a definition created by React.

## Definition of Done

A workshop administrator can author, validate, preview and evolve typed furniture parameters and semantic bindings entirely from the React application; the same generated/versioned definition is resolved by Go and consumed by SketchUp with no JSON editing, duplicated semantics or contract drift.

issues.body:
## Objective

Create the shared SketchUp host-interaction framework that #466, #467 and #468 must reuse for modular HtmlDialog state, request correlation, semantic authoring mutations, atomic native rebuild, rollback/undo and explicit degraded-state behavior.

Tracks #465, #474 and #290. Consumes #476 and #477.

## Why this foundation is needed now

The semantic foundations are complete:

- #476 provides one `SelectionContext` and capability-driven inspector;
- #477 provides one versioned rich authoring resolve contract;
- #404/#415 provide atomic native rebuild mechanics.

The next slices all need the same runtime loop:

```text
selection/context
→ capture authoring intent
→ submit authoritative resolve
→ reject stale/late result
→ validate accepted contract
→ apply one atomic SketchUp operation
→ update metadata/selection/preflight
→ commit or abort
```

If #466, #467 and #468 each implement their own bridge/state/rollback flow, Granete will acquire three subtly incompatible host clients despite sharing the same semantic contract.

## Mandatory authority

- `docs/architecture/sketchup-backend-web-integration-excellence.md` once merged
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-plugin-excellence.md`
- `docs/architecture/sketchup-authoring-interaction-contract.md`
- `docs/sketchup-excellence-execution-plan.md`
- `apps/sketchup-extension/AGENTS.md`
- #476 SelectionContext
- #477 rich authoring resolve
- #474 degraded/offline safety

## Hard prerequisites

- #404 atomic material rebuild ✅
- #415 native renderer ✅
- #476 semantic selection context ✅
- #477 rich authoring resolve ✅

No Project/Design persistence is introduced here.

## Required architecture

### Modular HtmlDialog application boundary

Decompose the current monolithic dialog behavior into explicit modules/responsibilities without requiring a framework rewrite:

```text
bridge/
  callbacks + message validation
state/
  session, catalog, selection, mutation, preflight, degraded state
views/
  inspector, preflight, internal editor, hardware editor, status/errors
controllers/
  commands and orchestration
```

Exact paths are an implementation choice. Required outcomes:

- one source of dialog state;
- typed/validated messages at the Ruby↔JavaScript boundary;
- downstream views consume shared state, not global DOM variables;
- callbacks are registered once and disposed/recreated safely;
- Node harness can test modules without loading the whole production HTML as an opaque blob.

Do not migrate to React inside HtmlDialog unless separately justified; modular vanilla JavaScript is acceptable and likely simpler.

### `AuthoringMutationCoordinator`

Introduce one domain-neutral host coordinator (exact name may follow conventions) responsible for:

1. snapshotting the exact semantic target/current accepted state;
2. allocating correlation/message identity;
3. entering `resolving` state;
4. submitting through #477;
5. rejecting malformed, stale, superseded or wrong-context responses;
6. preparing assets/definitions before destructive mutation;
7. opening one SketchUp operation;
8. applying/rebinding the complete accepted hierarchy;
9. writing accepted metadata only after successful apply;
10. restoring semantic selection/context;
11. refreshing/invalidating preflight and overlays;
12. committing or aborting coherently.

Feature-specific commands such as move shelf or replace hinge plug into this coordinator. They do not clone it.

### Interaction state machine

At minimum model explicit states equivalent to:

```text
idle
selecting
editing_intent
resolving
applying_host_mutation
committed
rejected
unavailable
stale
cancelled
```

Late result from an old selection/command cannot overwrite a newer accepted state.

### Degraded-state minimum

Pull forward the safety-critical part of #474 before editing features land:

```text
resolved_current
resolved_stale
unresolved_preview
offline_cached
sync_required
blocked_incompatible
```

This issue owns the state model and mutation guards. #474 continues to own complete cache/reconnect/pending-intent policy.

Rules:

- network/auth/license/schema failure is never rendered as ready/success;
- previous valid resolved hierarchy remains visible and marked honestly;
- no generic fallback becomes productive managed furniture;
- authoring action is disabled or queued only when an explicit reviewed contract allows it.

### Error taxonomy

Map structured codes to stable categories:

- authentication/session;
- license/capability;
- network/unavailable;
- stale/conflict;
- invalid authoring input;
- catalog reference;
- manufacturing blocker;
- incompatible plugin/API;
- host apply/rollback failure.

Behavior uses codes/state, not localized text.

## Required consumers

- #466 preflight review/navigation uses shared state and correlation.
- #467 internal authoring uses the mutation coordinator.
- #468 HardwarePlacement editing/substitution uses the same coordinator.
- #470 overlay invalidation consumes the common accepted-state fingerprint/version.
- #471 batch operations must reuse or explicitly extend the coordinator's atomicity contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dialog state/bridge is modular enough that #466–#468 add views/controllers without duplicating global state.
- [ ] One coordinator executes all managed authoring mutations.
- [ ] A rejected resolve never starts a SketchUp operation.
- [ ] A Ruby exception during apply aborts and preserves the previous valid hierarchy/metadata.
- [ ] A superseded/late response cannot overwrite a newer command.
- [ ] Selection is restored by semantic identity after regeneration where possible.
- [ ] Every successful edit is one coherent SketchUp undo action.
- [ ] Preflight/overlay state becomes stale or refreshes after accepted manufacturing-affecting changes.
- [ ] Network/auth/license/schema states remain distinct and fail closed.
- [ ] Test/dev generic fallback cannot appear as productive connected furniture.
- [ ] Unit/Node/Ruby tests and real-host TestUp prove resolve rejection, host exception, cancel, undo and late-response behavior.

## Negative proof required

Tests/review fail if:

- #467 and #468 each introduce separate resolve/rebuild coordinators;
- callback registration duplicates after dialog close/reopen;
- localized message text controls rollback or retry;
- a late response applies to a different current selection;
- current geometry is deleted before authoritative resolve succeeds;
- failure leaves mixed old/new metadata or children;
- offline fallback is marked ready/manufacturable;
- only pure unit stubs are used for behavior that depends on SketchUp operation/undo semantics.

## Definition of Done

Granete for SketchUp has one modular, real-host-tested interaction runtime that safely carries every professional authoring command from semantic intent to authoritative resolve and atomic host commit, with coherent rollback, undo, correlation and degraded-state guarantees reused by #466–#471.

### Descripción del problema
En el editor de Estructuras (`StructureEditorComponentsPanel`), al redefinir las fórmulas de posición (p. ej. en el eje Z / altura), dimensiones o rotación de un componente mediante la sección 'Avanzado: fórmulas y rotación' (`InstanceOverridesEditor`), la vista 3D en vivo y el modal `Structure3DModal` no reflejaban ningún cambio en la placa.

### Causa raíz
En `packages/ui/src/structures/structure3dPreview.ts`, la función `resolveStructure3DPreview` mapeaba `draft.components` a la estructura sintética temporal `tempStructure` copiando únicamente `componentId`, `quantity` y `placementOverride`, omitiendo `overrides: c.overrides`. Por este motivo, el motor de resolución `resolveComposedModule` recibía `overrides: undefined` y recurría siempre al pose por defecto del catálogo.

### Solución
- Pasar `overrides: c.overrides` en `resolveStructure3DPreview`.
- Agregar pruebas unitarias en `packages/ui/src/structures/structure3dPreview.test.ts` verificando tanto el override de altura preservando la ubicación default como el caso de ubicación `custom` con overrides completos.
