## Objetivo

Evoluciona el `ReconciliationResult` de #393 (PR #549) hacia clases semánticas accionables y agrega el flujo explícito de re-quote. Closes #394.

## Qué implementó

### Clasificación de impacto (dominio puro, `domain/reconciliation_impact.go`)
- Grupos **no exclusivos** `commercial` / `manufacturing` / `spatial` por FurnitureInstance, consumiendo el resultado EXACTO de #393 (nunca recompara snapshots → imposible divergir de la reconciliación).
- Política central única `ClassifyDifferencePath`: definition/version/parameters/materials → commercial+manufacturing (V1: inputs que determinan la resolución de BOM; el fingerprint resuelto llega con #395); `transform.*`/`room` → spatial-only; **paths desconocidos → fail-closed commercial+manufacturing**.
- Por status: `modeled_not_quoted` → commercial+manufacturing; `quoted_not_modeled` → commercial only; `synced`/`removed`/`conflict` → sin impacto per-item.
- `requiresRequote` se **deriva** de impactos comerciales (nunca flag user-set); `conflict` ⇒ `requiresResolution=true`, `canRequote=false`.
- Evidencia espacial: `CommercialItemSnapshot` gana `Transform`/`RoomID` opcionales (in-memory, jamás persistidos — §20). `Reconcile` compara espacial **sólo con evidencia en ambos lados** (#393 §42 preservado: ni transform comercial ni espacial inventado).

### Re-quote explícito
- `POST /api/projects/{projectId}/quote-revisions:requote` (contract generado, `RequireIdempotency("quote.requote")` — retry repele la misma revisión, `RoleCanMutateProjects`).
- Request con IDs **exactos** (`baseQuoteRevisionId`, `designRevisionId`) + selección opcional `includeFurnitureInstanceIds`. El backend **recomputa** reconciliation+classification server-side (§31/§32): los valores derivan sólo de las revisiones exactas.
- Storage `RequoteProjectQuote`: una transacción — snapshots exactos → reconcile → build → `CreateQuoteRevision` de #393 (Status=draft, SourceType=requote, atomicidad + concurrency fail-closed heredadas) → audit `quote_revision_created_from_design` en la misma tx.
- Migration **000117**: `base_quote_revision_id` + `source_design_revision_id` con FKs compuestas al mismo proyecto (provenance cross-project estructuralmente imposible) e inmutables por trigger. Fresh + upgrade probados.

### Reglas del draft (§§20–24)
- `synced` → quote verbatim; `modified` comercial seleccionado → valores del diseño con la **misma identidad**; spatial-only → quote verbatim; `modeled_not_quoted` seleccionado → incorporado con la MISMA identidad (sin acuñar FI nueva); `quoted_not_modeled` → se conserva (unidad vendida jamás se borra); `removed` → verbatim con lifecycle terminal.
- Transform/room/locators técnicos nunca entran al snapshot comercial.
- Q3 accepted queda **byte-idéntico** (test persistido: row + status + items).

## Negative proofs

- Mover un mueble **nunca** crea una revisión comercial: dominio (spatial-only → `ErrRequoteNoCommercialChange`) + PostgreSQL real (diseño movido reconcilia `synced` y el requote se rechaza).
- Base stale → `ErrQuoteRevisionConflict` (409), sin Q5 silencioso.
- `conflict` bloquea requote (fail-closed).
- Paths desconocidos clasifican fail-closed.
- Snapshot sin evidencia espacial + diseño con transform → `synced`, cero impacto.

## Contrato

- `contracts/reconciliationImpact.json`: fixture determinista con el escenario demo completo (FI-001 synced, FI-002 width commercial+manufacturing, FI-003 moved spatial-only, FI-004 modeled_not_quoted) consumido por `TestReconciliationImpactContract` con prueba de determinismo.
- El response de reconciliation (#393) gana `impact` por diferencia/item/resumen (aditivo) — una sola autoridad de clasificación; la UI no bifurca reglas.

## Invariantes (I1–I14)

I3/I4 inmutabilidad (Q3 intacto + trigger provenance), I7 reconciliation detecta/no muta, I10 espacial fuera del snapshot comercial, identidad preservada en requote.

## Verificación

- `go test ./...` verde contra PostgreSQL real (migración 00117 aplicada por RunMigrations en suite).
- `go vet` limpio; `gofmt` en archivos nuevos.
- `pnpm openapi:generate` + `openapi:check` verdes (Go + TS).
- `pnpm typecheck` verde; `pnpm test` verde (3524 tests).
- Ledger F209 + `progress/implementation_394_dt10.md` + `progress/current.md` actualizados.

## Layers (#394 checklist)

- [x] domain
- [x] Go API/storage/RLS
- [x] generated OpenAPI/JSON Schema
- [ ] React UI/server state (no existe UI de reconciliación aún; el contract ya expone el impacto — tracker #396)
- [ ] Ruby adapter/host (no aplica a este slice)
- [ ] HtmlDialog/interaction (no aplica)
- [x] shared parity/golden (contract fixture)
- [ ] real-host TestUp (no aplica)
- [ ] browser + real PostgreSQL E2E (tracker #398)
- [ ] real machine/software readback (no aplica)
- [x] docs/ledger/readback

## Summary

### Architectural Rules & Invariants
- **I10 Invariant (Read-Only Deterministic Reconciliation):** `reconcile(QuoteRevision, DesignRevision)` is a pure read-only comparison returning a structured `ReconciliationResult`. It performs ZERO mutations to the quote, quote lines, design, working copy, design revisions, or furniture instances. Verified with explicit PostgreSQL immutability negative proofs (`TestReconciliation_ImmutabilityNegativeProof`).
- **Explicit Revision Rule (§§2, 17, 22):** The API requires exact, explicit revision IDs (`quoteRevisionId` and `designRevisionId`). Implicit references such as 'latest', 'active', or 'current' are strictly disallowed.
- **Physical Join Key (§3):** Comparison joins physical instances strictly by `FurnitureInstance.id`. Matching by catalog definition, name, dimensions, or similarity is strictly forbidden. Negative Proof E confirms that identical-looking units with different identities are correctly classified as `quoted_not_modeled` and `modeled_not_quoted`, never `synced`.
- **Quantity > 1 (§4):** Materialized units are evaluated individually at the physical unit level, enabling partial placement tracking in 3D authoring.

## Summary

Implements **#391 `[P0][DT-7] Detect and resolve duplicated managed furniture identity in SketchUp`**.

When a user copies, pastes, or performs Move+Copy of a managed furniture component in SketchUp, this PR ensures that physical duplication is immediately detected and resolved via authoritative backend identity allocation, preventing identity collision or corrupt model state.

## Highlights

1. **Contracts & API**:
   - Added `POST /projects/{projectId}/furniture-instances/{instanceId}:duplicate` endpoint to OpenAPI contract.
   - Idempotency key pattern: `dup:{projectId}:{designId}:{sourceInstanceId}:{copiedPersistentId}`.
   - Origin stamped as `duplicate`, with `origin_furniture_instance_id` pointing to the source instance.
   - Client generated with `scripts/generate_openapi.py`; zero OpenAPI contract drift.

2. **Backend (Go)**:
   - Store interface updated with `DuplicateFurnitureInstance(ctx, DuplicateFurnitureInstanceCommand) (*domain.FurnitureInstance, error)`.
   - PostgreSQL storage implements transaction-safe duplication verifying tenant context, project matching, and foreign key integrity.
   - Handler `HandleFurnitureInstanceDuplicate` with role guard (`can_manage_designs`), input validation, and extension token authorization pattern.
   - Unit tests covering happy path, idempotency replay, role denial, UUID validation, and error scenarios. Real PostgreSQL integration tests in `internal/storage`.

3. **SketchUp Extension (Ruby)**:
   - `ProjectFurniture::Service`: added `duplicate_furniture_instance(project_id, instance_id, idempotency_key:)`.
   - `DuplicateResolver`: scans duplicates, discriminates original vs copy using authoritative `technical_client_locator` evidence from `DesignWorkingCopy`, calls backend to allocate new ID, rewrites copy metadata atomically while leaving original untouched, and synchronizes updated `DesignWorkingCopy`.
   - `EntitiesObserver`: attaches to `active_model.entities` and observes `onElementAdded`, dispatching to `DuplicateResolver` under a reentrancy guard.
   - Offline / Network Failure handling: marks copied entity with `duplicateStatus = 'unresolved'` without deleting local geometry; blocks publish precheck.
   - Reopen rescan: `rescan_and_resolve` re-evaluates duplicate sets on model load.
   - Publish precheck API: `validate_managed_furniture_identity` / `validate_model` (#391 DT-7 §21-22) fails loud if duplicates or invalid identities exist.

## Evidence & Verification

- **Ruby Extension Tests**: `bundle exec rake unit` -> 372 runs, 3064 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors.
- **Backend Tests**: `go test ./internal/api ./internal/storage` -> All passed (handler unit tests + PostgreSQL integration tests).
- **OpenAPI Drift**: `pnpm openapi:check` -> 0 drift, negative proofs passed.
- **TypeScript**: `pnpm typecheck` -> 7 workspace projects typechecked clean.
- **Monorepo Tests**: `pnpm test` -> 33 test files, 411 tests passed.

## Summary

Implements #390 (DT-6: Catalog → Backend FurnitureInstance → SketchUp → DesignWorkingCopy).

When a user selects and configures a furniture item in the SketchUp extension catalog:
1. Backend creates the authoritative `FurnitureInstance` identity first (`origin = 'design'`) via `POST /api/projects/{projectId}/furniture-instances` with `Idempotency-Key`.

When editing a structure in `StructureEditorComponentsPanel`, defining custom formulas for position (e.g. height in Z axis), dimensions, or rotation in 'Avanzado: fórmulas y rotación' did not reflect on the live 3D preview or in `Structure3DModal`.

## #389 Result

**Status: COMPLETE**

Closes #389 · tracks #384 · Quinto slice del Digital Thread (DT-5) sobre #388 (DT-4, mergeado).

### Project Furniture panel

- Tab nueva **"Proyecto"** en el dialog de SketchUp, fuente claramente separada del Catálogo/Biblioteca (digital-thread §13). Estados distintos: `Sin conectar` (CTA a Estado), cargando, error tipado (`stale_base`/`design_archived`/sin sesión/sin permiso/servidor no disponible), vacío honesto y lista **Pendientes (n) / Colocados (n)**.
- El proyecto proviene siempre del ModelBinding #388 — nunca de una selección manual paralela. El panel refresca al cambiar de documento activo y al cambiar el binding.
- Cada unidad = una card: nombre legible, dimensiones mm, "Unidad n de N" cuando hay idénticos, y la referencia corta como línea secundaria (IDs Granete = diagnóstico, no ruido).

### Project units

- **pending/placed** se deriva por `furnitureInstanceId` intersectando la lista autoritativa del proyecto con el DesignWorkingCopy actual (§5 del issue: sin enum global de estado).
- **quantity handling:** qty=3 ⇒ FI-001/FI-002/FI-003 como 3 filas individuales, cada una con su `Colocar`; agrupadas visualmente por definición pero individualmente seleccionables y trazables.

### Existing placement

`Colocar FI-001` → revalidación autoritativa del binding (fail-loud en stale/archived) → unidad resuelta desde la lista server-side → resolución de composición server-side (resolución rechazada aborta, sin geometría local adivinada) → jerarquía nativa #415 reutilizando `FurnitureBuilder` → metadata → **GET → merge by id → PUT completo** del working copy. **No se crea otro FurnitureInstance en ningún paso** (proof A: el journal del transport no contiene ningún POST a furniture-instances).

### Business identity

- **FurnitureInstance.id:** llega del backend y se estampa verbatim como `identity.furnitureInstanceId` (autoridad). Sobrevive Quote → placement → working copy → reopen.
- **SketchUp locator:** `persistent_id` viaja como `technical_client_locator` separado del business id (probado: locator ≠ identity).
- **legacy instanceRef/project_ref:** `instanceRef` **aliasa el mismo valor** del `furnitureInstanceId` en entidades colocadas por #389 — locator técnico de compatibilidad para búsqueda/inspector, nunca una segunda identidad (convergencia §12 documentada en el doc canónico). `projectRef` permanece como locator local legacy.

### Design WorkingCopy

- El item colocado lleva `furniture_instance_id`, `furniture_definition_id`, parameters (defaults del catálogo sobrescritos por las dimensiones citadas del `display` server-side), `material_choices`, transform y locator técnico. No se publica DesignRevision (#392).
- **Merge seguro (§14):** el PUT lleva el estado completo deseado — un working copy con FI-002 + place FI-001 resulta en ambos (proof G). Los campos de items existentes son estado del servidor y no se sobrescriben.

### Transform

- Contrato client-agnostic `translation_mm`/`rotation_deg`; pulgadas⇄mm SOLO en `TransformContract` (roundtrips probados: identidad, 1000 mm en X, 90° sobre Z con re-construcción). El placement inicial serializa como transform cero; el re-sync de movimientos posteriores llega con la publicación (#392).

### Failure / rollback behavior

- Orden canónico: resolve → insert local (una operación undoable) → PUT working copy → **si el backend falla: `rollback_placement`** (destruye hijos → entity → purge scoped de definiciones generadas) + `sync_failed` loud. Nunca queda una inserción local presentada como exitosa (proof H).
- `already_placed` ⇒ focus del root existente, sin segundo root ni rewrite del working copy (proof D). Dos roots con el mismo id ⇒ `duplicate_detected`, bloqueo loud (preview #391), sin crear identidad.

### Security / tenancy

- Credential de extensión deny-by-default (#460 SEC-6): grants exactos citando #389 — GET furniture-instances, GET working-copy y la **única** superficie PUT del credential (working-copy). RLS + scope autoritativo: una unidad de otro proyecto/org simplemente no está en la lista (proofs E/F); un `.skp` manipulado no obtiene nada.

### Negative proofs

A (no crea business object: journal sin POST) · B (identidad por ID: 3 idénticas ⇒ 3 identidades; place FI-001 sólo estampa FI-001) · C (qty=3 ⇒ 3 unidades) · D (already placed sin duplicados) · E (cross-project `not_found`) · F (cross-org 403 sin inserción local) · G (working copy preservado) · H (backend failure ⇒ rollback local + error) · I (reopen: identidad re-resuelta desde store nuevo).

### Real-host verification

`TC_ProjectFurnitureSmoke` (TestUp contra el RBZ instalado): placement estampa identidad en jerarquía nativa (`ComponentInstance` + partes anidadas), save/close/reopen re-resuelve la identidad sin duplicados, copy/paste reporta los 2 roots como estado inválido, dos unidades de la misma definición mantienen definiciones aisladas.

### Verification

```text
[✓] bundle exec rake verify        — syntax + rubocop (0 offenses) + unit 342 runs/2858 assertions + boundary 3 runs + RBZ sha256 verified
```

## Slice

**#388 (DT-4) — Bind SketchUp models to Project/Design identity** — el primer slice del vertical `Backend Design ↔ SketchUp`. Prerequisites completos (Gate A #462 ✅, #385 ✅, #387 ✅ / migration 000113); hard prerequisite de #389, #390 y del runtime de #499. Tracker #384.

## Qué hace

```text
Web/Backend (Design + WorkingCopy + Revision)
        ↕  POST binding:validate (autoritativo, stateless, no-store)
SketchUp: com.granete.project → {projectId, designId, baseRevisionId, schemaVersion}
```

Un modelo SketchUp se conecta a **un** Project/Design exacto mediante validación autoritativa del backend. El `.skp`, su path, `model.guid`, `persistent_id` y nombres **nunca** son identidad de negocio.

### Backend
- `POST /api/projects/{projectId}/designs/{designId}/binding:validate` — OpenAPI generado (#496), schemas `ModelBindingValidation` (state `valid|design_archived`, summaries org/project/design, working-copy base autoritativo + número, capabilities derivadas de los mismos gates que working-copy/publish).
- `GetModelBindingContext` — design debe pertenecer al project exacto; missing/foreign/cross-org ⇒ **404 uniforme** bajo RLS (app role, sin BYPASSRLS); base revision provista debe existir y pertenecer al design (nunca re-base silencioso).
- Extension credential (#460 SEC-6 deny-by-default): grants exactos citando #388 — `binding:validate` POST (stateless, sin business records), `GET /api/projects`, `GET /api/projects/{id}/designs` (picker). Todo lo demás sigue 403 (negative proofs actualizadas).

### SketchUp (`Connection::ModelBinding`)
- **Store**: envelope JSON versionado `granete.project-binding.v1` en `com.granete.project`; write en una operación undoable standalone; corrupt metadata ⇒ estado `invalid`, nunca un binding adivinado.
- **Contract**: parser fail-closed espejo del DTO generado.
- **Service**: errores tipados por clase (401/403/404/red), sin parsing de mensajes.
- **State**: `unbound | connected | stale_base | design_archived | invalid | incompatible | unauthenticated | unauthorized | unreachable` — todos distintos en el dialog.
- **Connector** (única writer): bind valida primero y escribe el base **autoritativo**; `rebind_required` explícito conservando el binding anterior; `incompatible` fail-loud por schema_version; `adopt_authoritative_base` como remediación explícita de drift; retry del mismo target = mismo binding.
- **Dialog**: card "Modelo / Diseño" con picker proyecto→diseño desde listas autoritativas, revisión de rebind (actual vs target) y acciones Validar/Actualizar base.

### Contrato compartido
`contracts/sketchupModelBinding.contract.json` — golden generado desde las respuestas del handler Go (`UPDATE_MODEL_BINDING_GOLDEN=1`), consumido fail-closed por Ruby. Regla pineada: **non-200 nunca escribe binding metadata**.

## Identity guarantees
- `FurnitureInstance.id` sigue siendo la única identidad física (no tocada aquí).
- `Design.id`/`baseRevisionId` provienen **sólo** de la respuesta del servidor.
- Locator técnico de SketchUp (`persistent_id`, GUID, nombre) nunca es binding key.
- `instanceRef`/`project_ref`: alias/locators locales documentados; convergencia con `furnitureInstanceId` en #389.

## Security / tenancy
- Request corre dentro del tenant tx del middleware; RLS fail-closed; org-less token sin acceso business.
- Cross-org/cross-project/foreign-revision ⇒ 404 indistinguible (`TestDesigns_ModelBindingContext`).
- Sin secrets en URLs/logs; no-store en la respuesta de validación; sin nueva persistence (endpoint read-only).

## Retry / concurrency
- bind idempotente por mismo target (mismo envelope, sin duplicados).
- `stale_base` derivado contra el base autoritativo → conflicto explícito + adopción explícita (nunca overwrite silencioso).
- Working-copy writes siguen con su concurrency fail-closed de #387 (este slice no escribe working copies).

## Verification
- `go test ./...` verde (PostgreSQL real) — incl. storage binding context (valid/base matching/foreign revision/cross-project/cross-org/archived), 8 handler tests, boundary del extension token.
- `pnpm openapi:check` sin drift · `pnpm typecheck` verde · `pnpm test` verde (411 web).
- `rake verify` verde: rubocop limpio, 324 unit runs (19 binding + 5 contract), boundary, RBZ sha256 verificado; JS harness del panel 9/9.
- TestUp `TC_ModelBindingSmoke`: roundtrip + save/close/reopen + copia renombrada conserva binding + corrupt ⇒ invalid (real-host, RBZ instalado).
- `git diff --check` limpio.

## Invariants (I1–I14)
I1/I2 (Project owns identity) · I7 (identity ≠ technical ID) · I12 (revisions immutable — endpoint read-only). Documentado en `progress/implementation_388_dt4.md` y §12 del digital-thread.

#389 placement/panel · #390 inserción conectada · #391 duplicados · #392 publish/artifacts · #393 reconciliation · #394 requote · #397 adopción SKP · #499 pairing grant/deep-link (este slice reusa la device credential SEC-6 existente) · hardware/Blum · machining · DXF · ProductionRelease.

prs.body:
Closes #386 · tracker #384 · F205

## Qué hace

`QuoteLine.quantity` sigue siendo **agrupación comercial**; cada unidad física ahora tiene su propia identidad explícita linkeada a la línea. El sistema puede responder de forma autoritativa **qué FurnitureInstances representa una QuoteLine**, y esas identidades quedan disponibles para #387/SketchUp sin crearse de nuevo (quote-first flow de la demo).

## Representación normalizada (decisión)

No existe aún un agregado `Quote`/`QuoteRevision` persistido (auditado). Usando la libertad de §4 del contrato digital-thread ("los nombres físicos de tablas pueden adaptarse al storage actual"), la relación se ancla en el modelo comercial real de hoy **sin crear un modelo paralelo** (anti-pattern 4):

- **QuoteLine** = `project_items` (id estable, module, quantity)
- **QuoteRevision aceptada** = `projects.status ∈ {accepted, produced}`

Tabla `quote_line_furniture_instances` (migration 000112): `(organization_id, project_id, quote_line_id, furniture_instance_id UNIQUE, created_at)`. Cuando la familia revisionada de SalesQuote aterrice, añade su FK de revisión y migra el ancla con autoridad explícita — el contrato conceptual no cambia.

## Invariantes preservadas (requerido por el issue)

- **I2 — una unidad física, una identidad**: `quantity=N` materializa N `FurnitureInstance` únicos asignados por la BD (`origin='quote'`, reutilizando `CreateFurnitureInstance` de #385 con su validación y audit por unidad). El comando `:materialize` **no acepta ningún input de identidad** del cliente (sin body) — imposible derivar identidad de line id, quantity, definition, orden o nombre. Negative proof explícito: el test de qty 3 exige 3 IDs únicos y fallaría si una implementación reusara el QuoteLine id para todas las unidades.
- **I3 — QuoteRevision owns commercial truth / aceptada es inmutable**: la materialización es inmutable tras aceptación en **tres capas**: (1) error tipado `ErrQuoteRevisionAccepted` → 409 CONFLICT en ambas direcciones; (2) policies RLS INSERT/DELETE exigen `app_project_quote_mutable(project_id)` (draft/quoted) + `organization_id = app_current_organization_id()` — ni siquiera SQL directo con rol app puede añadir/quitar links de un proyecto aceptado; (3) no hay mutación oculta: los cambios posteriores requieren nueva revisión.
- **I10 — reconciliation detects, no mutates**: nada aquí muta silenciosamente cotización o diseño. El decrease sólo actúa en draft y sobre unidades sin historia durable; el increase nunca reemplaza identidades. Los datos quedan listos para #392 (relación activa + lifecycle), sin implementarla.

## Semántica de quantity

- **qty 1** → exactamente 1 identidad (probado).
- **qty >1** → N identidades distintas aunque configuralmente idénticas (probado).
- **Idempotencia**: convergencia (segunda corrida = no-op con listas vacías) + receipts HTTP durables (misma `Idempotency-Key` → replay exacto) + **advisory lock por línea** → comandos concurrentes con keys distintas convergen a exactamente `quantity` (probado).
- **Increase** 2→4: preserva los 2 IDs existentes, crea sólo 2 nuevos (probado, orden estable por `created_at,id`).
- **Decrease** 4→2 (draft): retira las unidades **más nuevas** con lifecycle terminal `cancelled` (v+1, nunca DELETE físico, identidad sobrevive) + unlink; increase posterior crea IDs NUEVOS — **nunca recicla** (probado). Historia durable: hook `quoteLineInstanceDurableHistory` (hoy: aceptación + origin≠quote) documentado como punto de extensión #387+ (DesignRevisionItem, revisiones aceptadas, producción).
- **Eliminar una línea materializada** vía PUT de proyecto / RemoveProjectItem → error tipado `ErrQuoteLineStillMaterialized` (409), fail-loud; el PUT normal que conserva IDs de items sigue funcionando (probado). Backstop estructural: FK deferible falla en COMMIT si una línea materializada desaparece.

## Seguridad / RLS

- Clasificación `explicitly-shared` + inventory + trigger de ownership + FORCE RLS desde la primera migración.
- **Cross-project estructuralmente imposible**: FKs compuestas `(quote_line_id, project_id)` y `(furniture_instance_id, project_id)` + unique indexes `(id, project_id)` en ambas tablas padres (probado incluso por SQL admin).
- **Cross-org**: SELECT sin filtro no cruza orgs; INSERT cross-org / org equivocada → WITH CHECK; DELETE cross-org → 0 filas; grants `SELECT, INSERT, DELETE` **sin UPDATE** (link = hecho inmutable).
- **Unicidad acotada a la representación viva (fix de revisión)**: `UNIQUE(furniture_instance_id)` global habría convertido "una unidad ↔ una línea" en invariante del Digital Thread sobre TODA la historia, bloqueando revisiones futuras (Q1 aceptada Line A → FI-001 debe convivir como historia con Q2 vigente Line B → FI-001). Ahora: columna `state ('current'|'superseded')` + índice unique parcial `(furniture_instance_id) WHERE state='current'`; el rol app sólo puede INSERTar links `current` (RLS WITH CHECK) — el supersede será el comando audito de la familia de revisiones. Probado: coexistencia `superseded`+`current` para la misma instancia (escenario Q1/Q2), rechazo de una segunda link `current`, rechazo de INSERT `superseded` por rol app.
- **Owner-only mutations**: la contraparte manufacturing lee el proyecto compartido pero no puede materializar (403) ni linkear/deslinkear (policy).
- Audit durable `quote_line_furniture_materialized` (con ids created/cancelled/unlinked exactos) + `furniture_instance_created` por unidad, en la misma transacción tenant.

## API (OpenAPI generado, sin DTO paralelo)

- `GET /api/projects/{projectId}/quote-lines/{quoteLineId}/furniture-instances`
- `POST /api/projects/{projectId}/quote-lines/{quoteLineId}:materialize` (Idempotency-Key, sin body)
- Schemas `QuoteLineFurnitureInstance` / `MaterializeQuoteLineFurniture` + clientes TS/Go regenerados (`pnpm openapi:generate`).

## Verificación (todo sobre PostgreSQL real, rol app real)

- `GOFLAGS='-p=1' go test ./...` verde incl. suites nuevas: `TestQuoteLineFurniture_MigrationFreshAndUpgrade` (fresh + upgrade 111→112), `_MaterializationLifecycleAndAudit`, `_ConcurrentMaterializationConverges`, `TestTenantRLS_QuoteLineFurnitureDirectSQLCrossOrg`, `TestQuoteLineMaterializeHTTP_Postgres`, handler unit tests.
- `pnpm openapi:check` (sin drift) · `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm test` (3542 tests monorepo) · `git diff --check`: verde.
- **`scripts/foundation-gate-a.sh`: PASS — 34/34** (incluye pilot gate con contenedor fresco sin skips y browser gate real).

### Notas

- **Fix contenido preexistente** desbloqueado por este trabajo: `loadProjectItems` ejecutaba las queries de choices con el result set de items abierto → `conn busy` dentro de la tx de tenant que AuthMiddleware aplica a toda request (GET detalle de proyecto estaba roto por ese camino). Ahora bufferea los items antes de cargar choices.
- Acoplamiento ambiental preexistente en tests (verificado idéntico en `origin/main`, sin relación con este PR): `internal/config` exige `DATABASE_URL`+`MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL` separados; 4 tests legacy de hardware/material migran vía `DATABASE_URL` de superuser.

## No implementado (explícito)

- #387 Design / DesignRevision / DesignRevisionItem / working copy / publish
- #388 re-quote / link de instancias existentes
- SketchUp (Ruby/plugin/HtmlDialog/pairing/persistent_id/placements)
- #392 reconciliation (`quoted_not_modeled` etc.) — sólo quedan los datos
- release, machining, DXF, hardware/Blum, Gate B, SEC-8/9, Sales Network

## Siguiente

#387 Design / DesignRevision consumiendo exactamente estos `FurnitureInstance.id`.

prs.body:
Closes #385. Tracks #384.

## Qué implementa

Primera familia persistente de negocio posterior a Gate A: `furniture_instances`, la identidad estable de negocio de cada unidad física pretendida de mueble, perteneciente a exactamente un Project (ADR-0003).

```text
Project → FurnitureInstance (id estable, asignado por la BD)
```

### Persistencia (migration `000111`)

- `id` (UUID generado por la BD), `organization_id` (= `projects.organization_id`), `project_id`, `furniture_definition_id?` (FK `modules` `ON DELETE SET NULL`: la definición es procedencia, no identidad), `origin` (`quote|design|manual|import|duplicate`), `origin_furniture_instance_id?`, `lifecycle_status` (`active|removed|cancelled`, terminales), `version`, timestamps.
- Sólo identidad/procedencia/lifecycle: sin snapshots de configuración, transforms, BOM, pricing ni estado productivo (§5 del contrato digital-thread).
- RLS desde la primera migración: clasificación `explicitly-shared` (como `project_items`), policy `project_explicit_organizations` (`app_can_access_project` read / + `app_shared_child_matches_project` write), FORCE RLS, trigger `protect_shared_child_ownership` (project/org inmutables), índice organization-first, registro en `rls_policy_inventory`.
- Grants runtime `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` — sin `DELETE`: la identidad nunca se recicla; sólo la cascada del proyecto elimina filas.

### Storage / API

- `CreateFurnitureInstance` / `GetFurnitureInstanceByID` / `ListFurnitureInstancesByProject` / `RemoveFurnitureInstance` bajo transacción tenant (`WithinTenantTx`/AuthMiddleware), con scope SQL explícito que espeja la policy RLS (defense-in-depth) y RLS real como cinturón.
- Eventos audit durables `furniture_instance_created` / `furniture_instance_removed` en la misma transacción (#461).
- Contrato generado (`pnpm openapi:generate`, sin DTO manual): `GET/POST /api/projects/{projectId}/furniture-instances`, `POST /api/furniture-instances/{instanceId}:remove` con `Idempotency-Key` durable e `If-Match` obligatorio; errores tipados existentes. Origin server-authoritative (`manual` en el endpoint público).

## Invariantes preservadas (I1–I14 relevantes)

| Invariante | Cómo se preserva y verifica |
|---|---|
| **I1** Project owns furniture identity | FK + trigger + policy + validación server-side; existe antes de cualquier design (test crea instancia en proyecto sin 3D). |
| **I2** Una unidad física, una identidad | ID asignado por la BD; el comando no tiene input de posición/nombre/dimensiones/persistent_id. Test: dos comandos idénticos → dos IDs distintos. |
| **I7** Identidad independiente de SketchUp | La tabla no tiene ningún campo SketchUp; el locator técnico vivirá en `DesignRevisionItem` (#387+). |
| **I9** Cambios de configuración preservan identidad | Por construcción: la fila no guarda configuración; no hay mega-snapshot mutable que pueda cambiar el ID. |

## Negative proofs (PostgreSQL real, rol app real)

- **Identidad**: dos unidades idénticas (mismo proyecto/definición/origen) → IDs distintos (`TestFurnitureInstances_IdentityLifecycleAndAudit`).
- **Cross-project**: provenance de duplicado apuntando a instancia de otro proyecto → rechazado server-side; remove de instancia ajena → rechazado.
- **Cross-org / RLS**: `TestTenantRLS_FurnitureInstancesDirectSQLCrossOrg` — SELECT deliberadamente sin tenant filter bajo rol app no ve la otra org; UPDATE cross-org 0 filas; DELETE sin privilegio; INSERT en proyecto ajeno o con org equivocada falla WITH CHECK; reasignar project/organization bloqueada por trigger.
- **Random Project UUID**: HTTP POST con UUID de otra org → 404 (invisible bajo scope del actor).
- **Retry**: misma `Idempotency-Key` → replay de la misma identidad; count en BD == 1 (`TestFurnitureInstancesHTTP_Postgres`).

## Migrations

- `000111` backwards-safe: tabla nueva + RLS + inventory; aplica fresh y sobre schema pre-#385 (upgrade fixture verificado). Sin backfill: no existe autoridad para reconstruir identidad histórica, legacy state se preserva sin inventar identidad.

## Verificación

- `go test -p 1 ./...` verde contra PostgreSQL real (verificado en árbol aislado = main + este diff, 0 fallos, incl. toda la suite Foundation/Gate A/pilotreadiness).
- `pnpm openapi:check` · `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm test` (1506/1506 UI tras rerun de un flake preexistente) · `git diff --check` — verde.
- Gate A (#462) sigue GREEN: este PR no toca ningún proof de Foundation.

## No implementado (explícito)

- #386 QuoteLine ↔ FurnitureInstance.
- #387 Design / DesignRevision.
- SketchUp (bindings, pairing, placement, persistent_id, plugin, Ruby).
- reconciliation, requote, ProductionRelease, machining, DXF.

## Nota operativa

Durante la verificación local encontré trabajo concurrente sin commit de otra sesión en el árbol (`internal/api/idempotency.go`, `internal/api/platform.go`, `tests/pilotreadiness/platform_test.go`) que hacía fallar `tests/pilotreadiness` (su nuevo test consume slots TOTP de `fx.a.admin` y cascadea a un 429 en `TestPilotReadiness_TeamCommands...`). Ese trabajo NO está incluido en este PR; la suite completa con main + sólo este diff pasa 0 fallos.

prs.body:
## SEC-7 — MFA, Step-Up Authentication & Sensitive-Action Security (#460 / F202)

Continúa #460 sobre la base integrada de SEC-6 (merge `f5d59a46`). Una sesión autenticada normal ya NO basta para operaciones security-sensitive:

```
authenticated → sensitive command → STEP_UP_REQUIRED (403 tipado) → MFA challenge
→ short-lived elevated authority (sid+user+scope, 10 min) → el mismo comando prospera
```

### Matriz de operaciones sensibles

| Operación | Ruta | Scope | Antes |
|---|---|---|---|
| SketchUp device enrollment approval | `POST /api/auth/devices/approve` | `device_enrollment` | authMW only |
| Platform support entry | `POST /api/platform/organizations/{id}/support-session` | `support_access` | platformMW only |
| MFA factor removal | `POST /api/auth/mfa/factors/{id}:remove` | `security_admin` | nuevo |
| Recovery codes regeneration | `POST /api/auth/mfa/recovery-codes:regenerate` | `security_admin` | nuevo |
| Membership role changes | `:change-roles` + `PUT /roles` | `organization_admin` | capability only |
| Org admin transfer | `:transfer-admin` | `organization_admin` | capability only |
| Membership offboarding | `:offboard` | `organization_admin` | capability only |
| Mass session revocation | `:revoke-sessions` | `organization_admin` | capability only |
| Org lifecycle | `:suspend/:reactivate/:begin-offboarding/:terminate` | `platform_admin` | platformMW only |
| Entitlements update | `PUT /organizations/{id}/entitlements` | `platform_admin` | platformMW only |
| Global account status | `:set-account-status` | `platform_admin` | platformMW only |
| Password change | — no existe endpoint — | `security_admin` al nacer (documentado en ADR §12) | n/a |

**Decisiones de política documentadas** (ADR-0007 §12): self-revoke de sesión propia, revocación de dispositivo propio, revocaciones single-session, membership suspend/reactivate, sectores e invitaciones quedan en su boundary de capability (bajo impacto o reversibles). Support END no está gated (terminar acceso es safety-positivo). MFA obligatoria para admins NO se fuerza aún (lockout en upgrade); `MFA_REQUIRED` es la mecánica de rollout y flips son decisión de SEC-8/9.

### Diseño

- **MFA model**: `auth_mfa_factors` — `pending → enabled → revokó`; pending no autoriza nada y expira terminalmente (15 min). `auth_mfa_recovery_codes` — 10 verificadores HMAC-SHA256 single-use. `auth_step_up_grants` — autoridad server-side (sid, user, scope, method, expiry). RLS platform-global self-or-platform + `rls_policy_inventory`.
- **TOTP**: RFC 6238 — SHA1/6 dígitos/30s/ventana ±1 (vectores del RFC en tests). Replay protection atómica por counter high-water (`last_used_counter < candidate`), incluso concurrente.
- **Cifrado**: AES-256-GCM con keyring dedicado `MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEYS` (`{"active_kid","keys":{kid:base64}}`) o single `MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY`; ≥32 bytes; boot fail-closed. Subkeys por propósito vía HKDF-SHA256 (AEAD TOTP ≠ HMAC recovery). Rotación: quitar kid fail-close su material.
- **Step-up**: TTL 10 min, capped al absolute expiry de la sesión; NUNCA JWT claim; grant joinea la sesión viva (revocación corta sin cleanup); S2 nunca hereda (sid distinto — proof); scopes aislados (proof); ver4 sin sid no eleva (proof). Org A→B mismo sid: el grant user/session-bound sobrevive su TTL (prueba identidad del humano) mientras la autorización final exige membership/role/capability vivos.
- **Boundary**: `RequireStepUp(scope)` corre después de auth/platform y ANTES del wrapper de idempotencia → el challenge no consume la `Idempotency-Key` (proof HTTP: retry con la misma key prospera y el replay subsiguiente devuelve el 200 almacenado, no el 403).
- **Errores tipados**: 403 (nunca 401 — ningún client lo confunde con expiración de access): `MFA_REQUIRED`, `STEP_UP_REQUIRED` (+`details.scope`), `STEP_UP_EXPIRED`, `MFA_INVALID`, `MFA_ENROLLMENT_EXPIRED`, `MFA_FACTOR_NOT_FOUND`, `MFA_RECOVERY_INVALID`. OpenAPI primero + regenerado sin drift (§30).
- **Invariant de autorización**: MFA prueba identidad, no añade roles. Authority = identidad ∩ membership/role/capability vivos ∩ client type ∩ step-up reciente.
- **Rate limiting**: token bucket por usuario+propósito (5 fallos, refill 1/min, éxitos no consumen) — brute-force floor in-memory; SEC-8 lo distribuye. Fallos auditados.
- **Audit**: `mfa_enrollment_started/enabled/removed`, `mfa_recovery_codes_generated/used`, `mfa_verification_failed`, `step_up_succeeded/failed` — sin códigos, URIs ni plaintext (proof de redacción).

### Web / Mobile

- `SecurityScreen` (`/security`, nav base todo rol): wizard enrollment (QR renderizado en memoria + clave manual en `<details>`), verificación, recovery codes one-time (copiar/guardar), regenerar y eliminar factor vía step-up. Secrets nunca tocan localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB (browser proof).
- `useStepUp` + `StepUpModal`: modal "Confirma tu identidad" ligado a la acción exacta; reintenta EXACTAMENTE ese comando con la MISMA Idempotency-Key; sin auto-retry global; hint `MFA_REQUIRED` → Seguridad. Wiring: DevicesScreen (approve), UsersScreen (roles/transfer/offboard/revoke-sessions), PlatformScreen (support/account status), OrganizationLifecyclePanel (lifecycle).
- Multi-tab: step-up server-side por sid — tabs de la sesión comparten la autoridad; BroadcastChannel jamás transporta material MFA (política `{type}`-only intacta).
- Mobile: 403 STEP_UP es `DomainError` con code y NUNCA entra al path de refresh (regression proof).

### Validación ejecutada

- `GOFLAGS='-p=1' go test ./... -count=1` — verde (2 corridas): crypto (round-trip/tamper/wrong-key/kid), vectores RFC 6238, enrollment lifecycle + expiración, replay CON concurrencia (8 racers = 1 ganador), recovery single-use CON concurrencia, TTL/binding/scope-isolation/revocación, RLS self-only, redacción de audit; HTTP pilot (PostgreSQL real): challenge→verificación→retry misma key + replay 200, enrollment expirado post-MFA denied, session replacement sin herencia, rate limit 429, management, redacción.
- `pnpm openapi:check` — sin drift · `pnpm typecheck` — verde · `pnpm test` — 3522 tests verdes (ui 1503, web 411, mobile 73, domain 1240, storage 182, excel 93, desktop 17).
- `scripts/organization-browser-gate.sh` — **PASS 15/15** incl. `mfa.spec.ts`: enrollment (QR+manual), recovery one-time, `STEP_UP_REQUIRED` → verificación → mismo comando prospera, sin secretos MFA en storage (localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB).
- `scripts/smoke-deploy.sh` — 31/31 (con `MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEYS` en compose y `.env.production.example`).
- `git diff --check` — limpio.

### Docs

ADR-0007 §12 (SEC-7) + status · organization-foundation-v2 §13 · `.env.example` + `.env.production.example` + `docker-compose.prod.yml` + gates · `feature_list.json` (F202) · `progress/current.md`.

---

```
SEC-6 integrado
SEC-7 implemented pending review
F202 still in_progress
#460 still open
SEC-8/9 untouched
NO MERGE
```

reviews.body:
SEC-7 REVIEW — CHANGES REQUIRED before merge

The overall architecture is strong and CI is green on the exact head, but I found two security blockers:

1) MFA factor addition bypasses existing MFA. `POST /api/auth/mfa/totp:begin` and the pending-factor verify route are protected only by normal `authMW`. If a user already has an enabled MFA factor, a stolen normal Web session can create a new pending TOTP secret controlled by the attacker, verify that secret, and then use the new factor to obtain `security_admin`/other step-up. Adding an additional factor must require a recent `security_admin` step-up (or equivalent strong re-auth) when >=1 enabled factor already exists. Preserve a deliberate first-factor bootstrap path for users with zero enabled factors. Add negative proof: user with existing MFA + normal session only -> cannot begin/complete second-factor enrollment; after valid security_admin step-up -> can enroll it. Ensure no TOCTOU gap between begin/verify and current enabled-factor state.

2) Failed MFA/step-up audit events are rolled back. In `EnableMFAFactor`, failed verification inserts `mfa_verification_failed` inside the same `WithinTenantTx` and then returns `ErrMFAInvalidCode`; in `VerifyMFAStepUp`, `stepUpFailure` inserts `step_up_failed` and then returns the typed error. Returning the error rolls back the transaction, so those failure audit rows do not persist. The existing audit test only checks that some MFA events exist and therefore misses this. Refactor so failed-attempt audit commits independently (or return a structured verification outcome and commit the audit before returning the public failure) without committing any security state that should roll back. Add PostgreSQL-real proofs asserting the exact failed event remains after invalid TOTP/recovery attempts and still contains no secret/code material.

Please keep the existing TOTP replay, recovery single-use, sid/scope-bound grants, support/device-enrollment gates, and idempotency ordering unchanged. No SEC-8 work, no merge.

SECOND REVIEW — CHANGES REQUIRED before merge.

The two previous blockers are fixed: (1) additional-factor enrollment now requires a fresh `security_admin` step-up on BOTH begin and verify once an enabled factor exists; (2) failed enrollment/step-up audits are written outside the rolled-back verification transaction and the PostgreSQL test now asserts the exact failure events survive.

I found two remaining gaps:

1) BLOCKER — the in-memory MFA brute-force limiter is concurrency-bypassable. `mfaBudgetExhausted()` only checks `Tokens() < 1` before verification, while `noteMFAFailure()` calls `Allow()` only AFTER an invalid code has already been verified. With burst=5, e.g. 20 concurrent invalid step-up requests can all observe >=1 token before any failure consumes budget, all reach TOTP/recovery verification, and only afterwards do some `Allow()` calls fail. The current sequential HTTP rate-limit test cannot prove the bound under concurrency. Make admission/consumption atomic enough that at most the configured burst of concurrent invalid verification attempts can reach the verifier per user+purpose (without charging successful attempts if you want to preserve that policy), or use a reservation/in-flight design. Add a concurrent proof (e.g. 20 racers, instrument verifier/HTTP outcome) showing the brute-force bound cannot be exceeded. Do not defer this correctness bug to SEC-8; SEC-8 may distribute the limiter, but SEC-7's local limiter must be internally correct.

2) DoD/UI gap — backend now safely supports adding an additional factor, but `SecurityScreen` hides the enrollment button whenever `hasFactors` is true and `begin()`/`confirmEnrollment()` do not route `STEP_UP_REQUIRED` through `useStepUp`. Therefore a legitimate user cannot actually add a second authenticator through Web, despite factor management being in SEC-7 scope. Add an “Agregar app de autenticación” action when factors already exist; run begin through `security_admin` step-up (and handle verify if the grant expires between begin and verify, preserving the pending enrollment and re-challenging rather than generic failure). Add UI tests for first-factor bootstrap vs second-factor step-up and expired-step-up-at-verify.

CI for exact head `9a5db170...` is green, but these are behavioral gaps not caught by current CI. Keep #460/F202 open and do not merge.

THIRD REVIEW — functionally ready; one small test/UX cleanup remains before I would merge for the SEC-7 bar we set.

The two previous blockers are fixed on exact head f0cc3762373add769402294640039bab121c31e9:

- MFA brute-force admission is now reserved before verification, so concurrent invalid requests cannot all pass the pre-check. The new concurrent proof exercises 20 racers and asserts exactly 5 verification failures (burst) and 15 HTTP 429 responses.
- Web enrollment now uses `useStepUp('security_admin', ...)` for BOTH begin and verify. Because the existing enrollment state is not cleared when `STEP_UP_REQUIRED/EXPIRED` is challenged inside `useStepUp`, a grant expiring between QR begin and verify re-challenges and retries the same pending factor instead of creating a replacement enrollment.

CI for the exact head is green.

Remaining small gap: the requested SecurityScreen regression proofs were not added. `SecurityScreen.test.tsx` still covers first-factor bootstrap, invalid verify, recovery regeneration and listing, but not (a) enabled factor -> Add/configure another authenticator -> STEP_UP_REQUIRED -> verify -> begin succeeds, nor (b) step-up expires between begin and pending-factor verify -> modal -> same factorId verify retries and succeeds. The production code is correct on inspection, so this is not an architectural/security redesign; please add those two UI tests (and ideally label the enabled-state button 'Agregar app de autenticación' rather than 'Configurar...' for clarity), push to this same PR, and do not change backend behavior. After that this should be a very short final readback/merge gate.

prs.body:
## SEC-6 — SketchUp Dedicated Device Credentials

Part of #460 (P0 SEC-ORG auth hardening), closes SEC-6.

### What this implements

SketchUp instances are not browsers — they cannot participate in the web session/cookie/MFA flow. This PR introduces a **device-credential enrollment system** that gates every SketchUp→API call behind an explicit, per-device approval by an authenticated admin.

### Flow

```
SketchUp boots → POST /api/auth/devices/enroll (→ enrollment_code, device_id)
              → polls GET /api/auth/devices/poll until approved or expired
Admin opens Settings → Devices, enters code → POST /api/auth/devices/approve
SketchUp polls, sees approved → POST /api/auth/devices/exchange → device_token (dv_…)
SketchUp calls API → POST /api/auth/token (device_token) → short-lived JWT
```

### Changes

**Backend (Go)**
- Migration 000108: `auth_devices` + `auth_device_enrollments` tables with RLS
- `internal/domain/device.go`: enrollment/device domain models, token generation
- `internal/storage/devices.go`: full storage layer (enroll, poll, approve, exchange, token)
- `internal/api/devices.go`: 5 handlers with idempotency, expiry enforcement and audit trail
- Routes wired under `/api/auth/devices/`

**SketchUp extension (Ruby)**
- `auth/device_provider.rb`: enrollment + approval polling loop, persists device_token in preferences
- `dialog_controller.rb` + `application.rb`: bootstraps DeviceProvider before loading UI
- `dialog.html`: enrollment pending state with code display

**Web (React/UI)**
- `DevicesScreen.tsx`: admin UI to approve a device by code
- Exposed in AppShell nav (`devices` route) and `routes.ts`
- RBAC: `manage:devices` capability on `admin` role

### Verification

- `pnpm test` — 411 tests ✅
- `pnpm typecheck` — all packages clean ✅  
- `go test ./...` — all packages ok (including `internal/storage`) ✅
- `pnpm openapi:check` — no drift ✅

## SEC-4B — Web in-memory access credential, cookie bootstrap/refresh, cross-tab serialization and removal of the localStorage bearer (#460 / F202)

Base: `main` @ `70583b3a` (SEC-4A integrado). **NO cierra #460** · F202 sigue `in_progress`.

### Backend
- `WebAccessTokenTTL = 15m` rolling desde el mint (`min(now+15m, auth_sessions.absolute_expires_at)`), nunca desde el origin.
- Cap estructural: todos los mints Web usan `IssueTransportTokenUntil`; Mobile mantiene 18h hasta SEC-5.

### Web
- `webAuthRuntime`: autoridad única del access credential en memoria (web|support|anonymous); cero bearer persistido.
- `webAuthClient`: bootstrap/refresh cookie bodyless + CSRF, retry una sola vez y sólo con misma identidad/scope; session replacement y scope-change purgan S1 antes de instalar S2 y no dependen de BroadcastChannel.
- `webSessionLock`: **únicamente `navigator.locks` en producción** (`granete:web-session-mutation`) para refresh/logout/select-org. No existe fallback lease localStorage ni IndexedDB. Si Web Locks no está disponible, la mutación falla cerrada y NO se ejecuta.
- `webSessionChannel`: señales `{type}`-only; nunca tokens por broadcast.
- `granete_token` / `muebles_token` / metadata legacy de auth se destruyen en boot; nunca se migran ni se envían.
- Support continúa memory-only y tab-local, separado de la cookie Web.

### Evidencia
- Go/PostgreSQL, TypeScript, OpenAPI y suites Web/Mobile verdes.
- Browser gate cubre bearer fuera de storage, cookie bootstrap en reload/new-tab, refresh concurrente sin `REFRESH_REUSED`, org switch multi-tab y logout multi-tab.
- Negative proofs adicionales: holder congelado conserva Web Lock (sin TTL/takeover), ausencia de Web Locks = fail closed, session replacement/scope change purgan S1 antes de S2 y no reintentan la request original cross-tenant.
- `scripts/smoke-deploy.sh` y `git diff --check` verdes.

### Estado

```text
SEC-4B implemented pending final review/merge
SEC-5/6/7/8/9 untouched
F202 still in_progress
#460 still open
```

prs.body:
## SEC-4A — Web refresh-cookie protocol, CSRF boundary and credential transport contract (#460 / F202)

Base: `3f29905b` (PR #530, SEC-3). Head: `8b1ac292`.

Backend-only slice: builds the server-side protocol SEC-4B needs to migrate Web to `short access token in memory + rotating refresh credential in a Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie`, **without touching the React frontend** (Web keeps working with `granete_token` until SEC-4B).

### Transport contract

| Flow | credential in | access out | refresh out |
|---|---|---|---|
| login web | email/password | JSON token | **Set-Cookie only** |
| login mobile | email/password | JSON token | JSON body (unchanged until SEC-5) |
| login sketchup | email/password | JSON token | — |
| invitations:accept (web onboarding today; mobile has no caller) | token+password | JSON token | **Set-Cookie only** |
| refresh mobile | JSON body `{refresh_token, transport:"mobile"}` | JSON | JSON rotated |
| refresh web | **bodyless** cookie + CSRF | JSON | **Set-Cookie rotated** |
| refresh sketchup/support | bodyless bearer (finite bridge, now transport-restricted) | JSON | — |
| logout mobile | JSON body | — | 200 |
| logout web | **bodyless** cookie + CSRF | — | 200 + cookie cleared |
| logout no credential | — | — | 200, no session/family mutation, **no Set-Cookie** (mutation-free, idempotent, enumeration-safe) |

Body + web cookie together is rejected as **credential mixing** (fail closed). The no-body bearer bridge is now denied for web/mobile bearers (web/mobile own SEC-2A families; SketchUp/support keep it until SEC-6).

### Security properties

- Cookie `granete_web_refresh`: `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/auth`, host-only, `Secure` by default (zero value = secure), expiry = `auth_sessions.absolute_expires_at` — **never now+TTL on rotation**; the composite FK chain (sessions ← families ← credentials) makes the bound a structural DB invariant. Rotation = the same `RotateAuthRefreshCredential` (lock → live validation → R2 → consume R1 → audit → commit); `Set-Cookie` is written only after commit. Strict reuse detection untouched.
- **CSRF boundary** for cookie-authenticated refresh/logout: exact allowed `Origin` (CORS allowlist, never wildcard) AND `X-Granete-CSRF: 1` exact; uniform 403 without revealing which check failed. A cross-site form can set neither.
- **CORS**: `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` only next to the exactly reflected origin; foreign origins get neither header; `X-Granete-CSRF` added to `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`.
- **Fail-closed config**: `GRANETE_ENV` (`docker-compose.prod.yml` pins `production`, not overridable) + `WEB_REFRESH_COOKIE_SECURE=auto|true|false` (`auto` = Secure unless every CORS origin is loopback HTTP — local gates); any insecure resolution under production **refuses to boot**.
- **No secret in Web JSON**: login/refresh/invitation web responses carry no `refresh_token`; they add server-clock `access_expires_at` / `absolute_session_expires_at` (same arithmetic as minting via `auth.AccessTokenExpiry`) so SEC-4B never decodes JWTs client-side.
- **Cookie-mutation semantics (post-review)**: an internal refresh 5xx preserves the existing Web refresh cookie — the transaction rolled back and R1 remains valid; an internal logout 5xx preserves the cookie and server state so the logout can be retried; the Web logout clears the cookie only AFTER successful revocation/commit; a credential-less logout is mutation-free (no revocation, no Set-Cookie) and cannot be used for logout-CSRF through cookie deletion; the CSRF denial uses one uniform public 403 response.
- **Log redaction** proven: slog capture across login/rotation/replay/logout including an injected PostgreSQL failure — no cookie value, no `grt_refresh_v1.` material.
- select-org creates **no second family**: same sid/family, in-place scope update; cookie refresh after A→B returns B-scoped access (proof included).
- No lifetimes were changed; short Web access TTL belongs to SEC-4B.

### OpenAPI

`contracts/openapi/granete-api.v1.yaml` updated + Go/TS regenerated, `pnpm openapi:check` clean: optional refresh/logout bodies (web flow is bodyless), `RefreshTransport` enum (`mobile` only), `refresh_token` documented mobile-only, `Set-Cookie` documented on login/refresh/logout/invitation-accept, transport dispatch described. `refresh_contract_test.go` locks the new shape.

### Verification (real PostgreSQL, no security skips)

- Makes exact and membership-wide revocation atomic across sessions, refresh families, credential epochs, and critical audit, with real PostgreSQL rollback/concurrency proofs.

## Changes

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| OpenAPI | Six canonical list/revoke operations plus safe `SessionSummary`, typed request/response, and `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`; regenerated Go/TS artifacts. |
| PostgreSQL | Migration `000107` adds fixed-search-path `SECURITY DEFINER` boundaries with exact actor/org/membership/session validation; RLS remains self-or-platform. |

Refs #460

## Type

- [x] New feature

## Summary

- Add hash-only, single-use opaque refresh families bound one-to-one to `auth_sessions`.
- Rotate refresh credentials atomically, revoke the family/session on replay, and cap every replacement at the original absolute session expiry.
- Add real idempotent server logout and typed generated OpenAPI contracts without migrating React storage yet.

## Slice boundary

This is **SEC-2A** only. The repository ledger maps issue #460 to **F202** (not F200; F200 is an unrelated completed plinth-parity feature), and F202 remains `in_progress`.

**SEC-2B** follows from `main` only after SEC-2A merges: self/org/platform session directory plus capability-checked session revocation commands. This PR does not close #460 and does not implement SEC-3/4/6/7/8/9.

## Architecture and security policy

| Area | Decision |
|---|---|
| Persistence | Migration `000106_auth_refresh_credentials` adds one family per session plus lineage-bearing credential rows; only a 32-byte verifier is stored. |
| Verifier | `HMAC-SHA-256(REFRESH_TOKEN_PEPPER, raw credential)` with an independent mandatory >=32-byte pepper; no JWT key reuse, bcrypt, plaintext, or reversible storage. |
| Lifetime | Family and credential expiry are FK-bound to `auth_sessions.absolute_expires_at`; refreshed access JWTs are explicitly capped at the same timestamp. |
| Rotation | One transaction locks credential, family, and session; revalidates live account/membership/org epochs; mints A2; inserts R2; consumes R1; advances generation; writes durable audit; commits. |
| Replay | A consumed credential revokes its family and `auth_session` atomically. Every access JWT with that sid fails on its next authenticated request. |
| Concurrency | Strict policy: one concurrent R1 request wins; the loser observes consumed R1 and is treated as replay. Exactly one descendant is created, then the family/session is revoked. |
| Logout | Opaque refresh possession resolves the session and idempotently revokes both session and family; unknown/malformed/repeated logout is enumeration-safe. |
| Scope | Only web/mobile receive these credentials. Support and SketchUp remain separate classes for SEC-7/SEC-6. |

## API and transition

- `POST /api/auth/refresh`: public typed body `{ refresh_token, transport }`; rotates R1 -> A2/R2.
- `POST /api/auth/logout`: public typed body `{ refresh_token }`; returns `{ logged_out: true }` idempotently.
- `LoginResponse`: optional `refresh_token` and `refresh_expires_at` for web/mobile login and invitation acceptance.
- Typed errors: `REFRESH_INVALID`, `REFRESH_EXPIRED`, `REFRESH_REVOKED`, `REFRESH_REUSED` (existing `SESSION_REVOKED` remains the access-token boundary).
- Canonical OpenAPI and generated Go/TypeScript clients are synchronized.
- The no-body access-bearer refresh handler remains runtime-only as a finite compatibility bridge until SEC-4/SEC-6; it is no longer the canonical OpenAPI contract.

## Negative proofs

- Fresh migration and upgrade from `000105`; FORCE RLS and runtime-role inventory; no plaintext credential column.
- R1 -> A2/R2; R1 replay -> family/session revoked; R2 and A2 rejected.
- Two concurrent R1 requests create exactly one descendant, never R2 and R3.
- Near-absolute-expiry rotation cannot extend refresh or access past the original bound.
- Wrong client class does not consume the credential.
- Membership A revocation cuts session A while an independent session for organization B remains valid.
- Logout cuts a still-unexpired access JWT and refresh credential; a second logout is safe.
- Mint callback, durable audit, deferred commit, and replay-revocation failures roll back without consuming R1 or publishing an uncommitted R2.
- Raw refresh credentials are absent from PostgreSQL, logs, audit payloads, errors, traces, and query parameters.

## Verification

- [x] `pnpm openapi:check`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm test`

2. `a174d990` — generated API contract, HTTP issuance/refresh/logout, deployment configuration, real HTTP proof, ADR/ledger/progress.

Revert both commits and apply `000106_auth_refresh_credentials.down.sql`. Outstanding SEC-2A refresh credentials then require re-login; existing access/session-registry behavior from SEC-1 remains. No React credential migration exists in this slice.

prs.body:
## Qué es este PR

Primer slice de #460 (tracker F200): el **session registry server-side** pasa a ser la autoridad de revocación y lifetime absoluto detrás de los tokens **ver5**, con política JWT exacta (alg/iss/aud/typ/sid/jti/kid con keyring). Plan de slicing y arquitectura: ADR-0007 + `docs/architecture/organization-foundation-v2.md` §13.

Alcance SEC-1 únicamente. **No** incluye (children siguientes): rotación de refresh/reuse detection/logout (SEC-2), migración de credencial web (SEC-4), SketchUp device boundary (SEC-6), MFA (SEC-7), remoción del fallback `?token=` (SEC-3), trusted proxy/rate limits (SEC-8), gate con EOL ver4 (SEC-9).

## Cambios

- **Migration `000105_auth_session_registry`**: `auth_sessions` platform-global con FORCE RLS **self-or-platform** (lectura/actualización: usuario dueño o autoridad platform explícita; insert sólo el usuario dueño), coherencia membership↔user↔org enforced en PostgreSQL (FKs compuestos + scope-shape CHECK), registro en `rls_policy_inventory`, sin grant de DELETE. Fresh + upgrade (desde 104) probados. La administración de sesiones ajenas por organización NO es un tenant policy: llega con el command boundary capability-checked de SEC-2.
- **`internal/auth`**: `Authority`/`Keyring`; ver5 con `sid`, `typ` (access_web/access_mobile/device_sketchup/support_access), `aud` por cliente, `iss`, `jti`, header `kid`; HS256 exacto (no la familia HMAC); rotación zero-downtime; aceptación transitoria ver4 (EOL=SEC-9); kidless ver4 falla cerrado bajo keyring sin entrada `legacy`.
- **Middleware**: resuelve la fila del registry en vivo por request → sesión revocada o `absolute_expires_at` vencido corta un JWT vigente (`SESSION_REVOKED` tipado); `client_type` debe matchear transporte; store sin lookup de sesiones falla cerrado para ver5.
- **Handlers**: login (org-less y scoped), select-org (sid estable, scope update in-place), refresh (upgrade ver4→ver5 acotado al `auth_started_at` original), me, invitations:accept y support start registran sesión; `session_id` en `LoginResponse`/`SessionScope`.
- **OpenAPI**: `session_id` (opcional hasta SEC-9 para no romper clientes/mocks vigentes), `ApiErrorCode` += `SESSION_REVOKED`, `TOKEN_TYPE_MISMATCH`; clientes regenerados, `pnpm openapi:check` sin drift.
- **Config/docs**: `JWT_ISSUER`/`JWT_KEYRING` (+ .env examples), ADR-0007, foundation-v2 §13, ledger F200 in_progress, progress/current.md.

## Verificación

- `go test ./... -count=1` verde con PostgreSQL real (incluye pilotreadiness: flujos HTTP reales sobre tokens ver5 con session lookup real).
- `pnpm openapi:check`, `pnpm test` (360 web), `pnpm typecheck` verde.

## Negative proofs

1. Sesión revocada corta un access token no expirado (`TestAuthMiddleware_RevokedSessionCutsImmediately`).
2. Expiración absoluta del registry corta aunque el JWT tenga ventana más amplia (`TestAuthMiddleware_SessionAbsoluteExpiryCutsToken`).
3. Confusión de clase de credencial: typ/aud/client_type mismatch → 401 (auth tests + `TestAuthMiddleware_SessionClientTypeMismatchRejected`).
4. ver5 sin store con lookup → fail closed (`TestAuthMiddleware_Ver5FailsClosedWithoutSessionLookup`).
5. Cross-user: RLS oculta la fila a otro usuario; insert claimando otro user_id rechazado por policy (`TestAuthSessions_RLSScopesUnderAppRole`).
6. Upgrade ver4→ver5 en refresh/select-org registra fila con `absolute_expires_at = auth_started_at original + TTL` — nunca extiende las 18h (`TestRefreshVer4UpgradesToVer5PreservingAbsoluteOrigin`).
7. Algoritmo/issuer/audience/jti/kid: HS384/HS512/none, issuer ajeno, aud ajeno, sin jti, kid desconocido → rechazados (`internal/auth/auth_test.go`).

## Comportamiento a vigilar en review

- `RegisterRoutes` ahora requiere authority válida al boot (fail-closed; antes un secret corto explotaba recién al validar).
- Tokens ver4 vigentes siguen funcionando sin cambios (path transitorio); al refrescar/select-org se upgradean a ver5 con fila en el registry.
- Web/mobile/SketchUp siguen usando bearer 18h como hoy — la migración de credencial es SEC-4; nada de cliente cambió aún.

## Rollback

Migrations aditivas (`down` incluido); revert del deploy = revert del commit. Tabla `auth_sessions` queda inofensiva sin código que la consulte. Los tokens ver5 emitidos dejarían de validar al revertir (los clientes re-login una vez), y los ver4 nunca dejaron de validar.

Closes #<child-issue SEC-1 cuando exista>; tracker #460 permanece abierto.

## Rounds de review

**Review 1 (CHANGES REQUIRED) — resuelto en `4cb1f29e`:**
1. Registry = autoridad del CURRENT scope: middleware exige igualdad exacta de scope (org-less/scoped/support) contra la fila; select-org A→B invalida al instante los bearers del scope previo (`TestSelectOrgSwitchInvalidatesPreviousScopeTokens`).
2. Coherencia membership↔user↔org en PostgreSQL: FKs compuestos `(membership_id,user_id)`/`(membership_id,active_organization_id)` + scope-shape CHECK; storage traduce a `ErrAuthSessionScopeIncoherent` (`TestAuthSessions_ScopeCoherenceRejected`).
3. RLS self-or-platform con direct-SQL proofs bajo `granete_app`: miembro ordinario del mismo taller no ve ni revoca sesiones ajenas; platform path explícito conserva acceso (`TestAuthSessions_RLSSelfOrPlatformOnly`).
4. Claims registrados ver5 obligatorios: exp/iat/nbf/sub y sub==user_id, fail-closed (`TestValidate_RequiresEveryRegisteredClaim`).
5. select-org atómico: user fetch y mint antes de la mutación de scope (última mutación del switch); failure injection prueba conservación de scope y vigencia del token previo (`TestSelectOrgFailedSwitchPreservesScope`).

**Review 2 (SECOND REVIEW) — blocker residual de política JWT exacta resuelto:**
1. `kid` obligatorio para ver5: header presente, string no vacío y registrado; el fallback kidless queda exclusivamente para ver4 durante la ventana SEC-9. Proofs: ver5 kidless firmado con la legacy key rechazado; kid no-string y kid vacío rechazados (`TestValidate_Ver5RequiresKidHeader`).
2. `iat` validado contra el reloj con `jwt.WithIssuedAt()` además de la presencia manual: iat futuro rechazado (`iat in the future` en `TestValidate_RequiresEveryRegisteredClaim`).
3. `aud` exactamente uno e igual al audience del client type (`len(aud)==1`): audience extra rechazado (`extra aud`).

- **Review UI**: diálogo "Migrar modelos anteriores…" (conteos según mockup, tabla por ítem, [Actualizar compatibles (N)] / [Más tarde], resúmenes parciales/abort honestos), entrada de menú + auto-oferta no bloqueante al abrir. Copy del inspector actualizado al nuevo flujo.

## Qué

Cierra el gap de paridad TS↔Go del tratamiento de base (#442): cotización, cut list y lista de herraje ya no discrepan para el mismo mueble.

- **Modo/B efectivos**: override de ítem → default de módulo; B del plano → B del módulo → 100 (wall elevation → 0).
- **Filtrado ZOCLO** por modo efectivo en la vía BOM (estructura y módulo).
- **Síntesis `ZOCLO-AUTO`** con identidad estable + vueltas laterales F088 según exposición del placement.
- **Herraje**: perfil → ml fraccional, patas → cantidad sugerida; techo a barras de compra en la lista de herraje.
- **Cableado**: `CalcProjectBreakdown`, `GenerateCutRows`, `GenerateHardwareList`, `collectUsedUnitPrices` con contexto por ítem (cut list ahora también pasa `customDims`, como TS `cut.ts`).
- **Float64 + migration 000104** (`hardware_lines.quantity` → `DOUBLE PRECISION`, patrón 00061).

## Paridad

Contract compartido `granete.plinthBaseParity.v1` (`contracts/plinthBaseParity.contract.json`, 13 escenarios con negativos anti-phantom) consumido por TS (`plinthBaseParity.contract.test.ts`) y Go (`plinthBaseParityContract_test.go`). Expecteds validados contra el motor TS de referencia antes de implementar Go. F089 (merge de runs) fuera de alcance a propósito: ningún caller de producción TS pasa `plinthRunMap`.

## Alineación

- Engine sigue tenant-agnostic (Org Foundation v2): sin handlers/OpenAPI/sesiones/UI — cero solapamiento con las sesiones en curso de #458/#460.
- Contratos del plugin SketchUp intactos (goldens sin regenerar); `B` sigue siendo variable de fórmula server-side, no typed parameter (#477/#483).
- Sin tablas nuevas; RLS de 000094 intacto.

- `go test ./internal/storage/ -run TestHardwareLineQuantityDoublePrecision` verde sobre PG15 fresco (000104 + round-trip 0.6 ml).
- `go test ./...` verde **salvo** fallo PRE-EXISTENTE de `00102_support_session_credential_epoch` (reproducido con stash en main limpio — programa sesiones #458, no tocado acá; heads-up a esa sesión).

## Objective

Closes #477 (F195) with one versioned, executable TypeScript ↔ Go ↔ Ruby boundary for rich SketchUp authoring intent:

```text
POST /api/furniture/authoring/resolve
granete.sketchup-authoring-resolve.v1
```

The endpoint resolves semantic occurrences, relationships and manual hardware placements without feature-specific query parameters or persistent Project/FurnitureInstance state before Gate A.

> **Final:** rebased onto `main` `d66baf13` after #482; implementation foundation `1bd72f65`, UTF-8/precision proof `1d1c90cb`, representation fixes `8433cbdf`, final host evidence `051512f3`, independent approval `21fb41a8`, ledger closure `8e635f94`. F195 is `done`.

## Type

- [x] Feature
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Documentation only
- [ ] Refactor

Label: `type:feature`.

## What changed

- **Canonical contract:** added `contracts/sketchupAuthoringResolve.schema.json` for request, accepted/rejected responses, closed issues and discriminated unions. Ajv validates every shared scenario; TS also performs strict runtime request/response validation and correlation/coherence checks.
- **One authoritative snapshot:** Go selects the furniture definition, calculates `catalogRevision` and resolves from the same full-catalog snapshot. The revision also pins compiled authoring joinery/machining rules.
- **Determinism:** arbitrary precision steps use step rounding; the manufacturing change fingerprint is `sha256-<64 hex>` over canonical UTF-8 JSON; non-ASCII and `precisionMm=0.25` have parity proofs.
- **Strict transport:** JSON content type, body/collection/string bounds, RFC3339 `sentAt`, second-decode EOF, POST-only typed envelopes and a real-router typed `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` fallback.
- **Fail-closed consumers:** TypeScript and Ruby validate the normalized snapshot, preflight subset/link, exact issues/severities, numeric holes, exclusive provenance, response/request correlation and layout/snapshot/placement coherence before host mutation.
- **Complete visual material projection:** NativeLayout image, texture, tile, roughness, metalness, clearcoat and grain fields are aligned across Go, JSON Schema/Ajv, TypeScript and Ruby.
- **Semantic hardware truth:** active manual hardware without a visual preview stays in the normalized snapshot and manufacturing fingerprint while remaining optional in `layout.hardware`.
- **Typed transport rejections:** Ruby preserves `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` and `CONTENT_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` issues for 405/415 responses.
- **Honest scope:** v1 projects the definition-backed width/height/depth parameters needed by the first #467/#468 slices. Generic number/integer/boolean/enum projection is explicitly tracked in #483 rather than overstated here.
- **Current identity model:** organization-scoped web/extension token fixtures carry membership identity and credential version after #482.
- **Definition availability:** `Module` has no active/inactive lifecycle today; only definitions present in the pinned catalog resolve. Withdrawn/absent definitions return `CATALOG_REFERENCE_MISSING`.

## Contract invariants

- `catalogRevision` is required; no implicit latest or second catalog read.
- Client occurrence and placement IDs survive request → Go resolve → Ruby parse.
- Query parameters, unknown fields, ad-hoc parameters, duplicate IDs, malformed tuples, partial orphan targets, multi-entry templates and stale pins reject with stable codes.
- Identical stateless retries are byte-identical and bypass durable idempotency receipts.
- Ruby consumes server-authored layout/machining/preflight data; it never computes manufacturing authority.
- `layout.hardware` is a visual subset of semantic hardware placements; absence of preview never deletes manufacturing truth.
- No business schema, records or temporary SketchUp persistence are introduced.
- Extension POST allowlisting remains transitional; final token capability/commercial use stays blocked by #460.

## Evidence

- Full isolated gate: `DATABASE_URL=<isolated-review-db> PATH="$HOME/.rbenv/shims:$PATH" GOFLAGS=-p=1 ./init.sh` — green: TypeScript typecheck/tests, all Go tests, Ruby syntax/RuboCop/unit/boundary and deterministic RBZ verification.
- Shared fixture: Go-generated scenarios validated by the canonical schema and consumed by TS/Go/Ruby, including `10-unicode-quarter-step`, `11-material-pbr-roundtrip` and `12-cost-only-manual-hardware`.
- Focused checks: TypeScript resolve/fixture/schema 25/25; Ruby authoring resolve 40 runs/377 assertions plus layout contract 14/57; focused Go authoring/industrial-rule suites green.
- Real host: SketchUp 26.2.242 / Ruby 3.2.2, installed RBZ SHA-256 `7c82a347863c46607c4712b6552f864f0c70b4cc69fb169307bac24c04d0ebd0` — **6/6 tests, 58 assertions, 0 failures/errors/skips**.
- Parseable host evidence: `progress/host_smoke_F195_testup_ci.json` and related stdout artifact.
- Independent reviewer: **APPROVED** in `progress/review_F195.md` (`21fb41a8`); all six remote checks are green on closure head `8e635f94`.

## Risk and rollback

Main risk is freezing a cross-runtime v1 shape used by #467/#468. The canonical schema, shared scenarios, strict parsers and real-host fail-before-mutation proof constrain that risk. Rollback is the PR commit series; no migration or persisted business state requires data recovery.

## Size exception

`size:exception` is intentionally scoped to this existing atomic TS ↔ Go ↔ Ruby wire contract. Splitting the schema, producer, consumer, generated scenario fixture and host proof would create independently unreviewable intermediate contracts; this does not establish a general exception policy.

Closes #477

- Invariante transaccional race-safe de último administrador.

- FactoryCost, wholesale y retail tienen ownership/visibilidad separados.

## Summary

F186 / #415 (SU-ENT-2, programa #413, ADR-0004): reemplaza el renderer final basado en Groups/AABB-boxes por la jerarquía nativa de `Sketchup::ComponentInstance`.

- **Jerarquía nativa:** mueble gestionado = ComponentInstance top-level con ComponentDefinition generada y **aislada por FurnitureInstance** (V1: FI-A y FI-B de la misma Granete FurnitureDefinition divergen sin efectos de definición compartida). Cada tablero/herraje gestionado = ComponentInstance anidado cuya definición porta la caja **LOCAL en origen** (`[0,width]×[0,thickness]×[0,length]`) y cuyo transform se construye 1:1 desde el contrato #414: `Geom::Transformation.axes(translationMm, basis.x/y/z)`.
- **Geometría:** sin bakeo de world AABB en definitions, sin escala no-uniforme para dimensiones productivas, sin inferencia de orientación (cero tabla slot/role→rotación). Mover/rotar el mueble toca sólo el transform top-level; el rebuild preserva identidad de negocio + world transform y hace cleanup scoped (sólo definiciones Granete Parte/Herraje sin instancias vivas; jamás purge broad).
- **Atomicidad:** insert/rebuild = una sola operación undoable; fallo ⇒ abort sin jerarquía parcial ni definiciones huérfanas; metadata se escribe sólo tras jerarquía válida; bodies crudos rechazados (sólo `NativeLayout` parseado). Legacy Group falla cerrado **por tipo** (`is_a?(Sketchup::ComponentInstance)` — en el host, `Group` también responde a `#definition`) con puntero a #416.
- **Identidad (#346):** el layout Go publica `components[].componentDefinitionId` (estable, compartido por todas las copias de un componente, ≠ GUID nativo, ≠ `catalogComponentId` opcional); el parser Ruby lo preserva verbatim y el metadata de child lleva `componentInstanceId` + `componentDefinitionId` + `furnitureInstanceRef` + slot/role/materialBindingRole (+ `hostComponentInstanceId` en herrajes). Rename no cambia IDs; GUID/persistent_id jamás son identidad. Observer recupera el mueble dueño vía metadata (drill-down).
- **Herrajes/paths:** asset `.skp` (AssetLoader devuelve la instancia, con metadata Granete) y fallback generado, ambos nativos; path genérico offline también nativo (base identidad por construcción).

- Matriz obligatoria + **negative proofs** golden-driven en `native_entity_renderer_test.rb`: fallan si se vuelve a Group-only, si se hornea world AABB, si se usa escala no-uniforme, si una definición compartida mutua cruza furnitures, si un GUID nativo reemplaza ID Granete o si Ruby infiere orientación.

prs.body:
Closes #414. Tracks #413. Exclusivamente contract/resolver/parsing — desbloquea #415 (renderer nativo). No toca renderer (#415), material rebuild (#404) ni introduce heurísticas Ruby.

## Contrato publicado

- `FurnitureLayout.transformContract = "granete.local-basis.v1"` (marker de capability/version; desconocido = fail safe).
- Por board: `localTransform { translationMm, basis{x,y,z} }` — base **ortonormal diestra** (det=+1) en el frame furniture (workshop Z-up, alineado a SketchUp) con `furniture_point = translationMm + basis · local_point` y caja local `[0,width]×[0,thickness]×[0,length]` (convención local X=width / Y=thickness / Z=length **conservada**).
- Elección de representación: base ortonormal exacta (entradas 0/±1 en placements k·90°) sobre Euler (orden ambiguo) o quaternion (orden de w + ruido trigonométrico); mapea 1:1 a `Geom::Transformation.axes`.

## Decisión de frame (documentada en `boardLocalPose` + docs §8)

La rotación interna vive en el frame render (Y-up); render→furniture es el swap Y/Z — un espejo (det −1). La imagen fiel del frame local del engine sería left-handed: no es una rotación y espejaría geometría en SketchUp. El frame local publicado conserva extents y semántica de caras (+Y hacia la cara frontal, +Z hacia la superior) pero espeja +X local; la traslación compensa un ancho y la caja ocupa **exactamente** la región física del AABB legacy.

## Compatibilidad y fail-safe

- AABB legacy (`transform.translationMm` + `dimensionsMm`) permanece para versiones viejas del plugin y pasa a **derivarse** del transform (`aabbFromLocalTransform`) con chequeo runtime contra el pose del engine — imposible que divergien.
- `validateLayoutBasis` (Go) rechaza espejo/no-unitaria/skew/NaN; un espejo nunca se publica.
- Ruby: `library/layout_contract.rb` (`LayoutContract.parse!` + `resolved_native_layout`) exige el marker exacto, valida base diestra/triples/dims y falla loudly (`ContractError < LayoutResolutionError`) ante contrato ausente/desconocido o payload malformado. AABB es passthrough opcional, nunca fuente de orientación. **Cero tabla slot/role→rotación**; el renderer Group actual no se tocó.

## Material-aware (#402/#431)

El transform se computa del board ya resuelto con espesor efectivo del MaterialBoard seleccionado (mismo T en fórmulas, pose, caja local, transform y AABB).

## Paridad Go↔Ruby

Golden compartido `contracts/sketchupLayoutTransform.contract.json` generado desde el resolver Go (`UPDATE_LAYOUT_CONTRACT_GOLDEN=1`) y consumido textual por los tests Ruby del parser.

## Tests

- Go (`layout_transform_test.go`): marker; boards canónicos (lateral izq, piso/techo horizontales, fondo, puerta) con bases ancladas y entradas 0/±1; paridad AABB derivada por 8 esquinas (con dims overrides); espesor mixto 16/18/6 antes del transform; agregado (3 frentes); hardware host atado a `componentInstanceId`; serialization/golden; validaciones negativas; **negative proof** (dos customs comparten slot/nombre/AABB y difieren sólo en base).
- API: endpoint sirve `transformContract` + `localTransform` en el wire.
- Ruby: parser contra el golden, fail-safe (ausente/desconocido/malformado/espejo), negative proof (renombrar slot no cambia el transform; AABB opcional), integración provider + estáticos nil.

## Verificación

- `go test ./...` OK · `pnpm test` completo OK (3.000+) · `pnpm typecheck` OK · `bundle exec rake verify` OK (rubocop + unit + boundary + RBZ)
- Review: `progress/review_F185.md` — APPROVED
